\section{V18: symmetry-localizer occurrence and the multiplicity-saturation alternative}
\label{sec:v18-context}

V17 isolated a genuine operational obstruction: the rank-six matching-axis
source projector is not an element of the bare commutative multiplication
algebra of the twelve half-edge point record.  The inherited Grand-Tensor
construction, however, also carries an exact diagonal $S_4$ covariance and a
canonical decomposition of the ordered-half-edge representation
\cite{GT77}.  This continuation asks a more precise question: how little of
that symmetry must be represented as an actual historical operation before the
renewal source projector becomes word-native?

The answer is unexpectedly small.  One self-adjoint class-sum operator---the
sum of the six transposition relabelings---has four distinct eigenvalues on the
ordered-half-edge carrier, and the rank-six renewal source plane is exactly its
eigenvalue-$2$ subspace.  Thus one represented symmetry localizer suffices to
recover the projector by finite polynomial functional calculus.  This result
is conditional on occurrence of that operator in the represented history
algebra; covariance by an external relabeling group is not silently promoted
to an executable historical operation.

The second part of this continuation classifies the corresponding common
$S_4$ source problem.  On any common carrier, all standard-isotypic ambiguity
lives in the multiplicity space.  If the represented standard multiplicity is
exactly two, a rank-six arithmetic source of the required type has no remaining
range freedom: it must fill the same standard isotypic component as the renewal
entry/axis source.  If the multiplicity is larger, the unresolved relative
orientation is precisely a Grassmannian variable and the mixed-source gates of
V15--V17 remain necessary.

\section{The ordered-half-edge symmetry localizer}
\label{sec:v18-halfedge-localizer}

Let
\[
 X=\{(i,j):1\le i,j\le4,\ i\ne j\}
\]
be the twelve ordered half-edges.  Via the matching-axis bijection of the
inherited theorem \emph{Matching-axis half-edges and the exact two-standard
plane} in \cite{GT77}, this is the same $S_4$-set as
$\Omega\times\mathscr M$.  Put
\[
 \HH_{\rm ha}=\C^X
\]
with the uniform inner product and let
\[
 (U_gf)(i,j)=f(g^{-1}i,g^{-1}j),\qquad g\in S_4.
\]
Write $W_0=\one_4^\perp$ for the standard representation and retain the
normalized source maps $E_0,A_0:W_0\to\HH_{\rm ha}$ imported from the same
inherited theorem.  Their renewal source projector is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{P_{\rm ren}=E_0E_0^*+A_0A_0^*.}
 \tag{V18.1}\label{eq:v18-pren}
\end{equation}

\begin{lemma}[Character of the ordered-half-edge representation]
\label{lem:v18-halfedge-character}
If $f(g)$ is the number of fixed vertices of $g\in S_4$, then
\[
 \boxed{\chi_{\rm ha}(g)=f(g)(f(g)-1).}
\]
On the conjugacy classes
\[
 1^4,\quad 2\,1^2,\quad 2^2,\quad 3\,1,\quad 4
\]
this character is
\[
 \boxed{(12,2,0,0,0).}
\]
Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \HH_{\rm ha}\cong[4]\oplus2[31]\oplus[22]\oplus[211].}
 \tag{V18.2}\label{eq:v18-halfedge-decomp}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
An ordered pair $(i,j)$ with $i\ne j$ is fixed exactly when both $i$ and $j$
are fixed vertices.  There are therefore $f(g)(f(g)-1)$ fixed ordered pairs.
The five displayed values follow immediately from the cycle types.  Taking
inner products with the ordinary $S_4$ character table gives multiplicities
$1,2,1,1$ for $[4],[31],[22],[211]$, respectively, and zero for the sign
representation.  This also recovers the decomposition already used in the
inherited matching-axis theorem, but here the character calculation is
retained because it identifies the spectral projector below.
\end{proof}

Let
\[
 K_2:=\sum_{\substack{g\in S_4\\g\text{ a transposition}}}U_g.
\]
This is a self-adjoint central element of the represented group algebra.

\begin{theorem}[One class-sum writer reconstructs the renewal source projector]
\label{thm:v18-class-sum-projector}
On $\HH_{\rm ha}$, the transposition class sum has spectrum
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 K_2=
 6\,P_{[4]}+2\,P_{[31]}-2\,P_{[211]}+0\,P_{[22]},}
 \tag{V18.3}\label{eq:v18-k2-spectrum}
\end{equation}
where $P_{\lambda}$ denotes the orthogonal isotypic projector.  In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 P_{\rm ren}=P_{[31]}
 =p(K_2),\qquad
 p(x)=\frac{x(6-x)(x+2)}{32}.}
 \tag{V18.4}\label{eq:v18-pren-polynomial}
\end{equation}
Thus the complete entry/matching-axis renewal plane is the eigenvalue-$2$
space of one self-adjoint symmetry localizer.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For an irreducible representation $V_\lambda$, Schur's lemma gives the scalar
by which a conjugacy-class sum $C$ acts:
\[
 \frac{|C|\chi_\lambda(C)}{\dim V_\lambda}.
\]
For the six transpositions the values on
$[4],[31],[22],[211]$ are respectively
$6,2,0,-2$.  These are all distinct on the four irreducible types actually
present in \eqref{eq:v18-halfedge-decomp}, proving
\eqref{eq:v18-k2-spectrum}.  The polynomial $p$ takes values
$0,1,0,0$ at $6,2,0,-2$, hence $p(K_2)=P_{[31]}$.

The inherited maps $E_0,A_0$ are orthogonal isometric intertwiners from one
copy of $W_0$ each, so their ranges form two orthogonal $[31]$ copies.  By
\eqref{eq:v18-halfedge-decomp} the total $[31]$ multiplicity is exactly two.
Their sum therefore exhausts the complete standard isotypic component, and
\eqref{eq:v18-pren} equals $P_{[31]}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Word-native renewal localizer under represented symmetry]
\label{cor:v18-word-native-pren}
Let $\mathcal A^{\rm hist}\subseteq\mathcal B(\HH_{\rm ha})$ be a represented
history algebra on the ordered-half-edge carrier.

If the single self-adjoint operation $K_2$ belongs to
$\mathcal A^{\rm hist}$, then
\[
 \boxed{P_{\rm ren}\in C^*(K_2)\subseteq\mathcal A^{\rm hist}.}
\]
In particular the projector is word-native in the sense of the inherited
Grand-Tensor compiler.  It is enough, but stronger than necessary, that all
six transposition relabeling unitaries $U_g$ occur as represented historical
operations.

If the $S_4$ action is only an external covariance of the point record, with
no represented $K_2$ or equivalent spectral localizer, no such occurrence
conclusion follows.  This is compatible with the bare-record obstruction of
\Cref{thm:v17-halfedge-no-projector}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Finite-dimensional functional calculus places the polynomial
$p(K_2)$ in every unital $C^*$-algebra containing $K_2$.  The second statement
is immediate from the definition of $K_2$.  The last statement is a logical
rather than algebraic implication: a group acting by external relabeling
automorphisms need not supply its implementing unitaries as admitted physical
operations on the historical carrier.
\end{proof}

The next result shows how substantial the addition of one such localizer is.
Let $\mathcal D_X\cong\C^{12}$ denote the diagonal multiplication algebra of
the twelve point Reads.

\begin{proposition}[One class sum plus the point record generates the full matrix carrier]
\label{prop:v18-point-plus-classsum}
On $\HH_{\rm ha}$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{C^*(\mathcal D_X,K_2)=M_{12}(\C).}
 \tag{V18.5}\label{eq:v18-full-matrix}
\end{equation}
Hence adjoining one represented transposition class-sum operation to the bare
point algebra is sufficient not only to represent $P_{\rm ren}$ but to remove
the entire commutative carrier obstruction.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Let $e_x$ be the point basis and $D_x=|e_x\rangle\langle e_x|$ the diagonal
rank-one projector.  If a transposition $g$ sends $x$ to $y\ne x$, then the
$(y,x)$ coefficient of $K_2$ is a positive integer, and therefore
\[
 D_yK_2D_x=c_{yx}|e_y\rangle\langle e_x|,
 \qquad c_{yx}>0.
\]
The graph whose edges are the nonzero off-diagonal coefficients of $K_2$ is
connected: transpositions generate $S_4$ and the $S_4$ action on ordered
half-edges is transitive.  Products of the resulting rank-one edge operators
therefore give every matrix unit $|e_y\rangle\langle e_x|$.  Together with the
diagonal units they generate $M_{12}(\C)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{scope}[Occurrence versus mathematical generation]
\label{scope:v18-execution}
Equation \eqref{eq:v18-full-matrix} is a represented-algebra statement.  It
says that once $K_2$ is admitted as one historical operation, all matrix
coefficients lie in the generated $C^*$-algebra.  It does not assert that every
matrix in that algebra is a separately executable stochastic or physical
operation.  The event grammar and source/localizer occurrence tests of
\cite{GT77} remain necessary for such a stronger interpretation.
\end{scope}

\section{All common tetrahedral source ambiguity lives in the multiplicity space}
\label{sec:v18-multiplicity}

The preceding result completely closes the renewal projector on the branch
where one symmetry localizer occurs.  It remains to understand what an
arithmetic source of the same abstract $S_4$ type can do on a larger common
carrier.

We state the result over the real carrier because V14's arithmetic tangent and
renewal entry/axis plane are six-real-dimensional.  Let $W_0$ be the real
three-dimensional standard representation of $S_4$.

\begin{theorem}[Multiplicity-space classification of standard source planes]
\label{thm:v18-multiplicity-classification}
Let $\mathcal H$ be a finite-dimensional orthogonal real $S_4$-module and let
$\mathcal H_{\rm std}$ be its complete standard isotypic component.  There is
a real multiplicity space $M$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\mathcal H_{\rm std}\cong W_0\otimes M,}
 \tag{V18.6}\label{eq:v18-isotypic}
\end{equation}
with $S_4$ acting only on $W_0$.

Every $S_4$-invariant orthogonal projection $Q\le P_{\rm std}$ is uniquely of
the form
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{Q=I_{W_0}\otimes q}
 \tag{V18.7}\label{eq:v18-proj-mult}
\end{equation}
for an orthogonal projection $q$ on $M$.  Consequently:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(M\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item a six-real-dimensional $S_4$ source of type $2[31]$ is exactly
      $W_0\otimes L$ for a two-plane $L\subseteq M$;
\item two such sources with multiplicity projectors $q_A,q_B$ satisfy
      \begin{equation}
       \boxed{
       \Tr_{\mathcal H}(Q_AQ_B)=3\Tr_M(q_Aq_B);}
       \tag{V18.8}\label{eq:v18-overlap-mult}
      \end{equation}
\item their principal angles are precisely the principal angles between
      $L_A$ and $L_B$, each repeated three times;
\item their mutual innovation rank is a multiple of three:
      \begin{equation}
       \boxed{
       \rank\bigl(Q_A(I-Q_B)Q_A\bigr)
       =3\rank\bigl(q_A(I-q_B)q_A\bigr).}
       \tag{V18.9}\label{eq:v18-rank-multiple-three}
      \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The real standard representation is absolutely irreducible and
$\End_{S_4}(W_0)=\R$.  The standard isotypic component therefore has the form
\eqref{eq:v18-isotypic}, and its commutant is
\[
 I_{W_0}\otimes\End(M).
\]
An invariant orthogonal projection belongs to this commutant and hence has the
form \eqref{eq:v18-proj-mult}; idempotence and self-adjointness make $q$ an
orthogonal projection.  The rank-six statement follows from
$\dim W_0=3$.  Equations \eqref{eq:v18-overlap-mult} and
\eqref{eq:v18-rank-multiple-three} follow from tensor-product trace and rank.
The principal-angle statement follows because the nonzero singular values of
$Q_BQ_A$ are those of $q_Bq_A$, each with multiplicity $\dim W_0=3$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Multiplicity-two saturation forces source-range equality]
\label{cor:v18-saturation}
Assume a genuinely common represented $S_4$ action on a real carrier has
standard multiplicity
\[
 \boxed{\dim M=2.}
\]
Then every six-real-dimensional $S_4$-invariant source of type $2[31]$ has
range
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal H_{\rm std}=W_0\otimes M.}
\]
In particular, if both the arithmetic tangent source of V14 and the renewal
entry/axis source occur on this same multiplicity-two standard sector, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{P_{\rm ar}=P_{\rm ren}=P_{\rm std}.}
 \tag{V18.10}\label{eq:v18-saturation-equality}
\end{equation}
No additional mixed projector-overlap scalar is needed to prove equality of
the source ranges on this saturation branch.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
A rank-six standard source corresponds by
\Cref{thm:v18-multiplicity-classification} to a rank-two projection on the
two-dimensional multiplicity space.  The only such projection is $I_M$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[If multiplicity exceeds two, symmetry type alone leaves a Grassmannian]
\label{cor:v18-grassmannian}
If $\dim M=m>2$, the rank-six standard source ranges are parametrized by
\[
 \boxed{\operatorname{Gr}_2(M).}
\]
Thus common $S_4$ covariance, equality of source dimension, and equality of
abstract representation type do not determine the relative arithmetic--renewal
source orientation.  The mixed scalar/projector gates of V15--V17 remain
necessary unless some independent occurrence principle selects the same
multiplicity two-plane.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{thm:v18-multiplicity-classification}, the only datum is the
rank-two multiplicity projection, equivalently its two-dimensional range.
\end{proof}

\section{Complex structure on a saturated two-standard sector}
\label{sec:v18-complex}

The range comparison is not the whole V14 duality: the arithmetic tangent is
complex rank three, whereas the renewal plane obtained its complex structure
by pairing the entry and axis copies.  On the saturated multiplicity-two
branch this residual ambiguity is also finite-dimensional.

\begin{proposition}[Equivariant complex structures live entirely on multiplicity]
\label{prop:v18-complex-multiplicity}
On
\[
 \mathcal H_{\rm std}=W_0\otimes\R^2,
\]
every $S_4$-equivariant orthogonal complex structure has the form
\[
 \boxed{J=I_{W_0}\otimes j,}
\]
where $j$ is an orthogonal complex structure on $\R^2$.  There are exactly two
such structures,
\[
 \boxed{j=\pm J_2,\qquad
 J_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.}
\]
Once one orientation of the multiplicity plane is independently fixed, the
complex structure is unique.  The complex-linear unitary commutant of the
resulting $S_4$ action is then one copy of $U(1)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Equivariance and $\End_{S_4}(W_0)=\R$ force
$J=I_{W_0}\otimes j$.  Orthogonality and $J^2=-I$ imply
$j^Tj=I$ and $j^2=-I$ on a real two-plane.  Such an operator is rotation by
$\pm\pi/2$, hence $\pm J_2$ in an oriented orthonormal basis.  Operators
commuting with $J_2$ and orthogonal on $\R^2$ are the rotations
$aI+bJ_2$ with $a^2+b^2=1$, which form $U(1)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Saturation route versus mixed-panel route]
\label{cor:v18-two-routes}
There are now two logically distinct ways to close the first local
arithmetic--renewal source gate.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(R\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item \emph{Symmetry-saturation route.}  Represent one common $S_4$ action,
      prove that its standard isotypic multiplicity on the declared common
      carrier is exactly two, and prove that the arithmetic source occurs in
      that sector.  Then source-range equality is automatic by
      \Cref{cor:v18-saturation}; only the binary multiplicity orientation and
      the resulting $U(1)$ phase remain.
\item \emph{General mixed-source route.}  If the common standard multiplicity
      is larger than two, or if saturation is not established, acquire the
      mixed projector/determinant witnesses of V16--V17 (or the complete mixed
      Gram of V15).  Common representation type alone cannot replace them.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\section{What has and has not been resolved operationally}
\label{sec:v18-status}

The renewal side has advanced from the V17 statement
\[
 P_{\rm ren}\notin\mathcal D_X
\]
to an exact conditional reconstruction:
\[
 \boxed{
 K_2\text{ represented}
 \Longrightarrow
 P_{\rm ren}=\frac1{32}K_2(6I-K_2)(K_2+2I)
 \text{ represented}.}
\]
This is a genuine reduction of the occurrence burden: one self-adjoint
symmetry-localizer operation suffices.  If the six transposition relabelings
are themselves represented, no separate source-projector writer is needed.

The arithmetic side remains different.  V12--V14 reconstruct the marked
arithmetic source and its six-real-dimensional tangent externally from the
curve/theta data, but no theorem yet represents that source projector as a
word-native operator in the locked renewal history algebra.  V18 does not
manufacture such an embedding.  Instead it identifies a second possible
closure mechanism: if an independently acquired common $S_4$ carrier has
standard multiplicity exactly two and the arithmetic source is proved to
occur inside that standard sector, then the range comparison closes by
multiplicity saturation rather than by a new mixed overlap measurement.

Accordingly the next noncircular audit is:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(N\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item determine whether the diagonal tetrahedral relabelings (or at least the
      transposition class sum $K_2$) are actual represented operations in the
      selected renewal history grammar, as opposed to external symmetries;
\item determine the standard multiplicity of the \emph{same} common carrier on
      which an arithmetic source occurrence is proposed;
\item search for an actual historical operation or source-localizer placing the
      arithmetic theta/moduli tangent inside that carrier;
\item on multiplicity two, test only the residual complex orientation/phase;
      on larger multiplicity, return to the mixed-source scalar or complete
      panel of V15--V17.
\end{enumerate}

The finite-prime Frobenius, determinant-line, Chern-holonomy and continuum
comparisons remain downstream.  No group-name coincidence or abstract
$S_4$-module is promoted into a physical source identity before the occurrence
rows above are closed.

\paragraph{Version integrity.}
All V1--V17 mathematical bodies and their historical status ledgers are
preserved byte for byte.  V18 adds only the ordered-half-edge symmetry
localizer, the polynomial reconstruction of the renewal source projector, the
common multiplicity-space classification, and the symmetry-saturation
alternative above.  Future continuations must follow this block.

\section{V19: executable symmetry, exact renewal saturation, and a one-scalar arithmetic occurrence gate}
\label{sec:v19-context}

V18 reduced the renewal source-projector occurrence problem to one represented
transposition class-sum $K_2$ and separated two possible closures of the common
$S_4$ source comparison: multiplicity saturation or a genuinely mixed source
measurement.  Two inherited facts in the Grand-Tensor monograph sharpen that
fork further.  First, the minimum active carry--exchange instrument already
uses the endpoint permutations
\[
 s=(12),\qquad r=(1234),\qquad \langle s,r\rangle=S_4,
\]
with the selected group element retained through one source cut.  Second, on
the selected Store master cylinder the readable standard source is written
\[
 S_3:W_0\otimes E_3\longrightarrow\mathcal H,
 \qquad \dim E_3\le2,
\]
while the same selected source contains the two faithful orthogonal entry and
matching-axis standard frames~\cite{GT77}.

This continuation isolates exactly what follows from those statements and what
does not.  On the renewal side, the standard multiplicity is forced to be
\emph{exactly} two.  Moreover, once the active endpoint generators admit the
same-history diagonal lift to the matching-axis half-edge record, they generate
the transposition class sum of V18 by finite words, so the renewal projector is
word-native.  Endpoint transport alone is insufficient: the matching-axis
coordinate is load bearing.

On that closed renewal branch, an arithmetic projector is not needed for the
first occurrence test.  If the six real arithmetic theta/moduli tangent writers
of V12--V14 actually occur on the same carrier, one positive scalar---their
normalized source energy outside the represented renewal standard plane---is
zero exactly when the arithmetic and renewal source ranges coincide.  Thus the
remaining local source problem can be stated as an occurrence test for six
arithmetic writers against one already represented renewal localizer, rather
than as an abstract comparison of two externally reconstructed projectors.

\section{The active exchange generators compile the class-sum localizer}
\label{sec:v19-active-classsum}

Let $s=(12)$ and $r=(1234)$ in $S_4$.  For any unitary representation
$g\mapsto U_g$ on a finite carrier write
\[
 S:=U_s,\qquad R:=U_r.
\]
The active carry--exchange instrument of~\cite{GT77} contains the three
branch controls $s,r,r^{-1}$.  The following algebraic statement records what
is available if those branch-resolved deterministic permutations are represented
as historical operations on the carrier under discussion.

\begin{theorem}[Two represented generators compile the complete transposition class sum]
\label{thm:v19-two-generators-k2}
Suppose $S,R$ are represented unitaries satisfying the $S_4$ relations for
$s=(12)$ and $r=(1234)$.  Put
\begin{align*}
 T_0&=S,\\
 T_1&=RSR^{-1},\\
 T_2&=R^2SR^{-2},\\
 T_3&=R^3SR^{-3},\\
 T_4&=S(RSR^{-1})S,\\
 T_5&=(RSR^{-1})(R^2SR^{-2})(RSR^{-1}).
\end{align*}
Then $(T_0,\ldots,T_5)$ are precisely the six transposition operators
\[
 U_{(12)},U_{(23)},U_{(34)},U_{(14)},U_{(13)},U_{(24)},
\]
and hence
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 K_2=\sum_{j=0}^{5}T_j\in C^*(S,R).}
 \tag{V19.1}\label{eq:v19-k2-word}
\end{equation}
Consequently, on the ordered-half-edge representation of V18,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 P_{\rm ren}
 =\frac1{32}K_2(6I-K_2)(K_2+2I)
 \in C^*(S,R).}
 \tag{V19.2}\label{eq:v19-pren-word}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Conjugating $(12)$ by successive powers of $(1234)$ gives
$(23),(34),(14)$.  The elementary identities
\[
 (13)=(12)(23)(12),\qquad
 (24)=(23)(34)(23)
\]
give the last two words.  These are the six transpositions of $S_4$, proving
\eqref{eq:v19-k2-word}.  Equation~\eqref{eq:v19-pren-word} is then the
polynomial spectral-projector identity proved in V18.
\end{proof}

The theorem is deliberately representation relative.  The active instrument
acts directly on its endpoint register.  The renewal source plane of V18 lives
on the larger half-edge record $\Omega\times\mathscr M$, where $\mathscr M$ is
the three-element matching-axis register.  The next proposition shows that
this extra coordinate cannot be ignored.

\begin{proposition}[Endpoint-only transport cannot generate the matching-axis source localizer]
\label{prop:v19-endpoint-only-no-pren}
Identify
\[
 \mathcal H_{\rm ha}\cong\C^4\otimes\C^3
\]
by the point basis $(i,m)\in\Omega\times\mathscr M$.  Let
$\mathcal A_{\rm end}=M_4(\C)\otimes I_3$ be the algebra generated by arbitrary
endpoint operations acting trivially on the matching-axis coordinate.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{P_{\rm ren}\notin\mathcal A_{\rm end}.}
 \tag{V19.3}\label{eq:v19-endpoint-only}
\end{equation}
In particular the endpoint carry--exchange operation, without an operation or
same-history compiler acting on the matching-axis record, does not by itself
close the V18 localizer-occurrence gate.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Every element of $M_4(\C)\otimes I_3$ has zero matrix coefficient between
$(i,m)$ and $(j,n)$ whenever $m\ne n$.  Using the explicit entry and
matching-axis sources of the inherited half-edge theorem, one obtains for
example, for two distinct matchings $m_0,m_1$,
\[
 \left\langle e_{(1,m_0)},P_{\rm ren}e_{(1,m_1)}\right\rangle=\frac18.
\]
Hence $P_{\rm ren}$ has a nonzero cross-matching coefficient and cannot belong
to the endpoint-only factor.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Minimal diagonal lift of the active symmetry]
\label{cor:v19-diagonal-lift}
Assume that, in addition to the active control $g\in\{s,r,r^{-1}\}$, the
same-history matching-axis record is transported covariantly,
\[
 (i,m)\longmapsto(gi,gm),
\]
for the two generators $s,r$.  Then the corresponding half-edge Koopman
unitaries $U_s^{\rm ha},U_r^{\rm ha}$ are represented and
\[
 \boxed{P_{\rm ren}\in C^*(U_s^{\rm ha},U_r^{\rm ha}).}
\]
Thus one diagonal two-generator symmetry action is sufficient.  Some
matching-axis-sensitive operation is necessary by
\Cref{prop:v19-endpoint-only-no-pren}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The diagonal maps are permutations of the twelve half-edges, hence their
Koopman maps are unitary.  Apply \Cref{thm:v19-two-generators-k2} on the
half-edge representation.  Necessity follows from
\Cref{prop:v19-endpoint-only-no-pren}.
\end{proof}

\begin{scope}[Relation to the inherited stopped-$S_4$ audit]
The domain-enriched synchronized-interface packet of~\cite{GT77} already
contains a stopped $S_4$ edge-regeneration residual.  Vanishing of that
residual on a packet containing the matching-axis Read is one possible physical
route to the diagonal lift used above.  V19 does not replace that occurrence
test by abstract covariance: it only proves that, once the two generator maps
are represented on the correct half-edge carrier, no further symmetry writer
is needed to obtain $K_2$ or $P_{\rm ren}$.
\end{scope}

\section{The selected Store standard source has multiplicity exactly two}
\label{sec:v19-renewal-saturation}

The preceding localizer question concerns occurrence as an operation.  The
source multiplicity itself can be closed directly from inherited source data.
Retain the readable standard source of~\cite{GT77},
\[
 S_3:W_0\otimes E_3\longrightarrow\mathcal H,
 \qquad S_3^*S_3=I_{W_0}\otimes G,
 \qquad \dim E_3\le2.
\]
On the selected Store master cylinder, the inherited entry and matching-axis
frames give two orthogonal faithful standard copies $E_0(W_0)$ and
$A_0(W_0)$ inside the same readable standard source.

\begin{theorem}[Exact two-standard saturation of the selected renewal source]
\label{thm:v19-renewal-exact-two}
Under the selected-Store hypotheses above,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\dim E_3=2,\qquad G\succ0,\qquad \rank S_3=6.}
 \tag{V19.4}\label{eq:v19-e3-two}
\end{equation}
Moreover
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{Ran} S_3
 =\operatorname{Ran} E_0\oplus\operatorname{Ran} A_0
 =\operatorname{Ran} P_{\rm ren}.}
 \tag{V19.5}\label{eq:v19-store-range}
\end{equation}
Thus the selected readable renewal standard source is already a saturated
multiplicity-two $S_4$ sector; no third standard copy is hidden in this source
packet.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The two inherited maps $E_0,A_0:W_0\to\mathcal H$ are isometries with
orthogonal ranges.  Hence their direct sum has rank six and, by the stated
selected-Store provenance, its range lies in $\operatorname{Ran} S_3$.  Therefore
$\rank S_3\ge6$.  But the domain of $S_3$ has dimension
$3\dim E_3\le6$.  It follows that $\dim E_3=2$ and $\rank S_3=6$.
The identity
$S_3^*S_3=I_{W_0}\otimes G$ then forces $G$ to have rank two and hence to be
positive definite.  Since a six-dimensional subspace
$\operatorname{Ran} E_0\oplus\operatorname{Ran} A_0$ is contained in the six-dimensional range of $S_3$,
the two ranges coincide.  V18 identified the former range with
$\operatorname{Ran} P_{\rm ren}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Renewal-side multiplicity gate is closed on the selected Store source]
\label{cor:v19-renewal-mult-closed}
For the selected readable standard source of
\Cref{thm:v19-renewal-exact-two}, the multiplicity-space alternative of V18
lands on the saturated branch:
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal H_{\rm std}^{\rm ren}\cong W_0\otimes\R^2.}
\]
Hence any six-real-dimensional $S_4$-invariant source that actually occurs
\emph{inside this same readable standard carrier} has the same source range as
the renewal entry/axis source.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first statement is \eqref{eq:v19-e3-two}.  The second is exactly the
multiplicity-two saturation theorem of V18 applied on this fixed carrier.
\end{proof}

\begin{scope}[This is not yet a common arithmetic--renewal carrier]
\label{fire:v19-renewal-not-common}
Equation~\eqref{eq:v19-store-range} closes the multiplicity of the selected
\emph{renewal} readable source.  It does not place the arithmetic theta/moduli
tangent on that carrier.  V12--V14 reconstruct that arithmetic source
externally from the curve and its marked theta data.  The remaining occurrence
question is therefore whether six real arithmetic tangent writers are actually
represented on, or map into, the selected Store standard source.  No abstract
$S_4$ module is used to infer that occurrence.
\end{scope}

\section{A one-scalar arithmetic occurrence test against the represented renewal localizer}
\label{sec:v19-arithmetic-occurrence}

The renewal projector can now be treated as a represented localizer on the
branch of \Cref{cor:v19-diagonal-lift}.  This removes the need to represent an
arithmetic projector in order to test the first source-range equality.

Let
\[
 A_{\rm ar}:\R^6\longrightarrow\mathcal H
\]
be an \emph{actually occurring} arithmetic theta/moduli tangent source on the
same physical carrier, with positive Gram
\[
 G_{\rm ar}=A_{\rm ar}^*A_{\rm ar}\succ0.
\]
The six-real-dimensional rank is the one proved necessary in V14 and locally
available from the marked theta-source differential in V12.  Define its
whitened synthesis
\[
 \widehat A_{\rm ar}:=A_{\rm ar}G_{\rm ar}^{-1/2},
 \qquad \widehat A_{\rm ar}^*\widehat A_{\rm ar}=I_6.
\]

\begin{definition}[Arithmetic-to-renewal source-loss form]
\label{def:v19-source-loss}
Put
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb L_{{\rm ar}\mid{\rm ren}}
 :=A_{\rm ar}^*(I-P_{\rm ren})A_{\rm ar}\succeq0,}
 \tag{V19.6}\label{eq:v19-loss-form}
\end{equation}
and its normalized scalar loss
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \varepsilon_{{\rm ar}\mid{\rm ren}}
 :=\Tr\!\left(
 G_{\rm ar}^{-1/2}
 \mathbb L_{{\rm ar}\mid{\rm ren}}
 G_{\rm ar}^{-1/2}\right)
 =\Tr\bigl(\widehat A_{\rm ar}^*(I-P_{\rm ren})\widehat A_{\rm ar}\bigr).}
 \tag{V19.7}\label{eq:v19-loss-scalar}
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[One positive scalar decides arithmetic occurrence in the saturated renewal plane]
\label{thm:v19-one-scalar-occurrence}
Assume $P_{\rm ren}$ has rank six and
$A_{\rm ar}$ has positive rank-six Gram.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{0\le\varepsilon_{{\rm ar}\mid{\rm ren}}\le6,}
 \tag{V19.8}\label{eq:v19-loss-window}
\end{equation}
and the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item $\varepsilon_{{\rm ar}\mid{\rm ren}}=0$;
\item $\mathbb L_{{\rm ar}\mid{\rm ren}}=0$;
\item $\operatorname{Ran} A_{\rm ar}\subseteq\operatorname{Ran} P_{\rm ren}$;
\item $\operatorname{Ran} A_{\rm ar}=\operatorname{Ran} P_{\rm ren}$.
\end{enumerate}
If $P_{\rm ar}:=\widehat A_{\rm ar}\widehat A_{\rm ar}^*$ denotes the
mathematically reconstructed arithmetic source projector, then moreover
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|P_{\rm ar}-P_{\rm ren}\|_{\HS}^2
 =2\varepsilon_{{\rm ar}\mid{\rm ren}}.}
 \tag{V19.9}\label{eq:v19-projector-distance}
\end{equation}
Thus a single nonnegative source-loss scalar certifies exact source-range
identity or returns a quantitative obstruction; occurrence of $P_{\rm ar}$ as
an independent historical operation is not required for this first test.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Since $0\preceq I-P_{\rm ren}\preceq I$ and
$\widehat A_{\rm ar}^*\widehat A_{\rm ar}=I_6$,
\[
 0\preceq
 \widehat A_{\rm ar}^*(I-P_{\rm ren})\widehat A_{\rm ar}
 \preceq I_6,
\]
which gives \eqref{eq:v19-loss-window}.  A positive matrix has zero trace if
and only if it vanishes, proving (i)$\Leftrightarrow$(ii).  Vanishing of the
Gram is equivalent to
$(I-P_{\rm ren})\widehat A_{\rm ar}=0$, hence to (iii).  Both ranges have
dimension six, so (iii)$\Leftrightarrow$(iv).

Finally, $P_{\rm ar}$ and $P_{\rm ren}$ are rank-six orthogonal projections,
and
\[
 \Tr(P_{\rm ar}P_{\rm ren})
 =\Tr(\widehat A_{\rm ar}^*P_{\rm ren}\widehat A_{\rm ar})
 =6-\varepsilon_{{\rm ar}\mid{\rm ren}}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \|P_{\rm ar}-P_{\rm ren}\|_{\HS}^2
 =\Tr P_{\rm ar}+\Tr P_{\rm ren}
  -2\Tr(P_{\rm ar}P_{\rm ren})
 =2\varepsilon_{{\rm ar}\mid{\rm ren}}.
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The first common-source gate needs arithmetic writers, not an arithmetic projector]
\label{cor:v19-no-arithmetic-projector-needed}
Suppose the renewal localizer $P_{\rm ren}$ is represented by
\eqref{eq:v19-pren-word}, and suppose six real arithmetic theta/moduli tangent
writers occur as the columns of $A_{\rm ar}$ with a faithful measured Gram.
Then the scalar \eqref{eq:v19-loss-scalar} is a complete test of source-range
equality.  No separately represented arithmetic source projector and no full
$6\times6$ arithmetic--renewal cross Gram are required for this gate.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
All ingredients of \eqref{eq:v19-loss-form} are then on the same source
carrier.  Apply \Cref{thm:v19-one-scalar-occurrence}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Symmetry forces triplet-sized leakage; complex covariance makes it all-or-nothing]
\label{cor:v19-symmetric-loss}
Assume in addition that the arithmetic writer is $S_4$-equivariant of real
type $2[31]$ and that $P_{\rm ren}$ is the complete standard isotypic projector.
Then the whitened loss operator has the form
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 D:=\widehat A_{\rm ar}^*(I-P_{\rm ren})\widehat A_{\rm ar}
 =I_{W_0}\otimes d,}
 \tag{V19.10}\label{eq:v19-loss-mult}
\end{equation}
for one $2\times2$ positive semidefinite real matrix $d$.  Hence
\[
 \boxed{\rank D\in\{0,3,6\}.}
\]
If the same source writer also intertwines the arithmetic and renewal complex
structures, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{D=\rho I_6,\qquad
 \rho=\varepsilon_{{\rm ar}\mid{\rm ren}}/6,}
 \tag{V19.11}\label{eq:v19-loss-scalar-symmetric}
\end{equation}
and therefore the leakage rank is either zero or six.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The loss operator commutes with the coefficient $S_4$ action, so the real
standard-isotypic commutant gives \eqref{eq:v19-loss-mult}.  Its rank is three
times the rank of $d$.  If it also commutes with the orthogonal complex
structure $J_2$ on the multiplicity plane, then a real symmetric matrix $d$
commuting with $J_2$ must be a scalar multiple of the identity.  Taking the
trace gives \eqref{eq:v19-loss-scalar-symmetric}.
\end{proof}

\section{The exact remaining occurrence hierarchy}
\label{sec:v19-status}

V19 closes two renewal-side questions that were open in V18:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item on the selected Store readable standard source, the standard multiplicity
      is exactly two, not merely at most two;
\item the active endpoint generators compile the complete transposition class
      sum, and hence $P_{\rm ren}$, as soon as their physical action is lifted
      to the matching-axis half-edge record.
\end{enumerate}
The second item has a sharp boundary: endpoint-only operations cannot generate
$P_{\rm ren}$, so the matching-axis-sensitive lift is not cosmetic.

The arithmetic-side burden is now correspondingly smaller but still physical.
One does not need an arithmetic projector.  One needs six real arithmetic
source-motion writers on the same history carrier, with the faithful Gram
already reconstructed externally in V12--V14 or measured directly.  Against a
represented $P_{\rm ren}$ their complete source-range occurrence is decided by
one scalar,
\[
 \boxed{\varepsilon_{{\rm ar}\mid{\rm ren}}.}
\]
A positive value is a quantitative failure witness and must not be normalized
away.  A zero value closes source-range equality; the remaining binary complex
orientation and $U(1)$ phase of V18 then become the next local tests.

This gives the next noncircular audit order:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(N\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item verify, on the selected Store cylinder, the actual matching-axis-sensitive
      diagonal lift of the active generators (or an equivalent represented
      $K_2$); the inherited stopped-$S_4$ edge-regeneration residual is the
      natural existing gate;
\item acquire the six real arithmetic theta/moduli source-motion writers as
      actual same-history sources, rather than as an external moduli
      reconstruction alone;
\item evaluate the single positive source-loss scalar
      \eqref{eq:v19-loss-scalar};
\item only on its zero branch test the residual complex orientation/phase and
      then transfer/Krylov equality;
\item defer Frobenius--Wilson comparison until those source and transfer gates
      have passed.
\end{enumerate}

The finite-prime Frobenius, determinant-line and Chern-holonomy constructions of
V5--V13 remain available arithmetic structures, but they cannot substitute for
the missing same-history arithmetic writer occurrence in item~(N2).

All V1--V18 mathematical bodies and their historical status ledgers are

\section{V20: finite Hellinger occurrence, secant duality, and a minimal statistical completion}
\label{sec:v20-context}

V19 reduced the first arithmetic--renewal source comparison to the occurrence
of six real arithmetic theta/moduli tangent writers on the selected Store
carrier.  The full Grand-Tensor calculus already contains a more primitive
source notion: actual neighbouring laws on one resolved record determine
canonical square-root-probability (Hellinger) secants before any smooth
parameter or derivative is assumed~\cite{GT77}.  The purpose of V20 is to
splice that upstream occurrence calculus into the arithmetic programme.

The result is twofold.  First, six actually occurring neighbouring Store laws,
labelled by six independently declared real arithmetic moduli directions,
produce a finite source packet whose Gram and source-range residual can be
compared directly with finite arithmetic theta-projector secants.  Equality of
the two finite Grams and vanishing renewal source loss give an exact finite
source duality, with no derivative assumption.  On a genuine shrinking family,
these finite tests converge to the V12 arithmetic Fubini--Study metric and the
physical Fisher metric, so the tangent occurrence gate of V19 is recovered as
a limit rather than postulated at the entrance.

Second, there is no positivity or probability-simplex obstruction to such an
occurrence.  On the twelve-state half-edge record, every prescribed positive
six-dimensional arithmetic source metric admits a strictly positive
six-parameter exponential family whose Fisher tangent is exactly the saturated
renewal entry/axis plane.  This is an existence benchmark only: because the
family is constructed from the desired metric, it cannot be used as evidence
that the selected Store law physically realizes the arithmetic source.

\section{Finite arithmetic and renewal secant packets}
\label{sec:v20-secant-packets}

Let $Q\subset\R^6$ be a real coordinate chart for the marked genus-two moduli
germ of V12 at the arithmetic point $q_0$, and let
\[
 \rho_\Theta(q)
\]
be the corresponding rank-one marked theta-source projector.  Thus V12 proves
that the differential of this projective source is faithful and reconstructs
the positive realified source metric $G_{\rm ar}^{\R}$ with
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{G_{\rm ar}^{\R}\succ0.0706\,I_6.}
 \tag{V20.1}\label{eq:v20-ar-floor}
\end{equation}
Here $G_{\rm ar}^{\R}$ denotes the realification of the Hermitian matrix
$g_{\rm src}$ of V12.

Let $\Omega$ be the selected twelve-state half-edge record and let
$p_0\in\mathcal P_+(\Omega)$ be an actually occurring reference law.  Write
\[
 \mathfrak h(p):=2(\sqrt{p(\omega)})_{\omega\in\Omega}
 \in\ell^2(\Omega)
\]
for the Hellinger embedding used in the inherited source calculus.  Let
$P_{\rm ren}$ denote the represented rank-six renewal standard-source
localizer of V18--V19.

Fix six linearly independent real parameter directions
$e_1,\ldots,e_6\in\R^6$ and a nonzero step $h$.  Suppose, in addition to the
arithmetic points $q_0+he_a$, that six actual neighbouring Store laws
\[
 p_a(h)\in\mathcal P_+(\Omega),\qquad a=1,\ldots,6,
\]
are supplied with these same independently declared direction labels.
No smooth interpolation through the seven laws is assumed.

\begin{definition}[Finite theta-projector and Hellinger secant syntheses]
\label{def:v20-secant-syntheses}
Define
\begin{align}
 A_h e_a
 &:=\frac{\rho_\Theta(q_0+he_a)-\rho_\Theta(q_0)}{\sqrt2\,h},
 \tag{V20.2}\label{eq:v20-ar-secant}\\
 R_h e_a
 &:=\frac{\mathfrak h(p_a(h))-\mathfrak h(p_0)}{h}.
 \tag{V20.3}\label{eq:v20-ren-secant}
\end{align}
The arithmetic carrier is the real Hilbert space of Hermitian matrices with
Hilbert--Schmidt inner product, and the renewal carrier is
$\ell^2(\Omega;\R)$.  Put
\[
 G_{\Theta,h}:=A_h^*A_h,
 \qquad
 G_{{\rm Hel},h}:=R_h^*R_h.
\]
When $G_{{\rm Hel},h}\succ0$, define the finite renewal source-loss scalar
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \varepsilon_{{\rm Hel}\mid{\rm ren}}(h)
 :=\Tr\!\left[
 G_{{\rm Hel},h}^{-1/2}
 R_h^*(I-P_{\rm ren})R_h
 G_{{\rm Hel},h}^{-1/2}\right].}
 \tag{V20.4}\label{eq:v20-finite-loss}
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact finite secant duality test]
\label{thm:v20-finite-secant-duality}
Assume $G_{\Theta,h}\succ0$ and $G_{{\rm Hel},h}\succ0$.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item
\[
 \boxed{G_{\Theta,h}=G_{{\rm Hel},h}}
\]
if and only if there is a unique source-fixing unitary
\[
 U_h:\\operatorname{Ran} A_h\longrightarrow\\operatorname{Ran} R_h,
 \qquad U_hA_h=R_h;
\]
\item
\[
 \boxed{\varepsilon_{{\rm Hel}\mid{\rm ren}}(h)=0}
\]
if and only if
\[
 \\operatorname{Ran} R_h=\\operatorname{Ran} P_{\rm ren};
\]
\item consequently the two equations
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 G_{\Theta,h}=G_{{\rm Hel},h},
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_{{\rm Hel}\mid{\rm ren}}(h)=0}
 \tag{V20.5}\label{eq:v20-finite-duality-gate}
\end{equation}
are necessary and sufficient for an exact source-fixing unitary from the
finite arithmetic secant source onto the represented saturated renewal plane.
\end{enumerate}
No arithmetic source projector on the renewal carrier is required.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Part~(i) is the same-source Gram construction applied to the common coefficient
space $\R^6$: equality of the Grams makes
$A_hx\mapsto R_hx$ well defined and isometric, and both maps have rank six.
For part~(ii), put
\[
 \widehat R_h=R_hG_{{\rm Hel},h}^{-1/2}.
\]
Then $\widehat R_h^*\widehat R_h=I_6$ and
\[
 \varepsilon_{{\rm Hel}\mid{\rm ren}}(h)
 =\Tr\bigl(\widehat R_h^*(I-P_{\rm ren})\widehat R_h\bigr)
 =\|(I-P_{\rm ren})\widehat R_h\|_{\HS}^2.
\]
Thus the scalar vanishes exactly when
$\\operatorname{Ran} R_h\subseteq\\operatorname{Ran} P_{\rm ren}$.  Both spaces have dimension six, so the
inclusion is equality.  Part~(iii) combines the first two statements.
\end{proof}

\begin{scope}[What the finite test assumes]
The common direction labels $e_a$ are part of the occurrence claim.  The
arithmetic states $\rho_\Theta(q_0+he_a)$ are computed from the independently
marked theta construction, while the laws $p_a(h)$ must be actual neighbouring
Store laws or actual outputs of a declared Store deformation.  Choosing the
$p_a(h)$ after inspecting the arithmetic Gram would construct a completion but
would not verify occurrence.
\end{scope}

\section{Tangent limit: Fubini--Study versus Fisher geometry}
\label{sec:v20-tangent-limit}

The factor $1/\sqrt2$ in \eqref{eq:v20-ar-secant} is chosen so that the
arithmetic projector chord has the V12 Fubini--Study metric as its tangent
Gram, with no residual factor of two.

\begin{lemma}[Projector derivative realizes the real Fubini--Study metric]
\label{lem:v20-projector-FS}
Let $\rho=|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$ be a smooth rank-one projector with
$\|\psi\|=1$.  For real tangent directions $u,v$, one has
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac12\Tr\bigl((\dd\rho[u])(\dd\rho[v])\bigr)
 =g_{\rm FS}^{\R}(u,v).}
 \tag{V20.6}\label{eq:v20-projector-FS}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
At the point under consideration choose the phase of $\psi$ so that the
chosen tangent lifts are horizontal:
$\langle\psi,\dd\psi[u]\rangle=
 \langle\psi,\dd\psi[v]\rangle=0$.
Then
\[
 \dd\rho[u]
 =|\dd\psi[u]\rangle\langle\psi|
 +|\psi\rangle\langle\dd\psi[u]|.
\]
Multiplying the two expressions and taking the trace gives
\[
 \Tr\bigl((\dd\rho[u])(\dd\rho[v])\bigr)
 =2\Re\langle\dd\psi[u],\dd\psi[v]\rangle,
\]
which is twice the real Fubini--Study metric.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Hellinger derivative is the Fisher score synthesis]
\label{lem:v20-Hellinger-Fisher}
Let $p(q)$ be a $C^1$ strictly positive family of laws on a finite set and put
\[
 s_u(\omega)=\dd\log p(q)[u](\omega).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \dd\mathfrak h[p][u](\omega)
 =\sqrt{p(\omega)}\,s_u(\omega),}
 \tag{V20.7}\label{eq:v20-Hellinger-derivative}
\end{equation}
and hence
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \langle\dd\mathfrak h[p][u],\dd\mathfrak h[p][v]\rangle
 =\sum_\omega p(\omega)s_u(\omega)s_v(\omega)
 =I_{\rm Fish}(u,v).}
 \tag{V20.8}\label{eq:v20-Fisher}
\end{equation}
Every score is centered:
$\sum_\omega p(\omega)s_u(\omega)=0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Differentiate $2\sqrt p$ to obtain
$p^{-1/2}\dd p=\sqrt p\,\dd\log p$, proving
\eqref{eq:v20-Hellinger-derivative}.  Taking the counting-measure inner product
gives \eqref{eq:v20-Fisher}.  Differentiating
$\sum_\omega p(\omega)=1$ gives centering.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Shrinking-law limit of the finite source audit]
\label{thm:v20-shrinking-limit}
Assume there is an actually supplied $C^2$ Store-law family
$p(q)$ on a neighbourhood of $q_0$, with $p(q_0)=p_0$, and take
$p_a(h)=p(q_0+he_a)$.  Then, as $h\to0$,
\begin{align}
 \boxed{G_{\Theta,h}\longrightarrow G_{\rm ar}^{\R},}
 \tag{V20.9}\label{eq:v20-ar-limit}\\
 \boxed{G_{{\rm Hel},h}\longrightarrow I_{\rm Fish}(q_0).}
 \tag{V20.10}\label{eq:v20-ren-limit}
\end{align}
If the Fisher matrix has rank six, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \varepsilon_{{\rm Hel}\mid{\rm ren}}(h)
 \longrightarrow
 \varepsilon_{{\rm tan}\mid{\rm ren}}
 :=\Tr\!\left[
 I_{\rm Fish}^{-1/2}
 A_{\rm Fish}^*(I-P_{\rm ren})A_{\rm Fish}
 I_{\rm Fish}^{-1/2}\right],}
 \tag{V20.11}\label{eq:v20-loss-limit}
\end{equation}
where $A_{\rm Fish}$ is the Hellinger/Fisher tangent synthesis.
Consequently, if along one shrinking sequence
\[
 \|G_{\Theta,h}-G_{{\rm Hel},h}\|_{\HS}\to0,
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_{{\rm Hel}\mid{\rm ren}}(h)\to0,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 I_{\rm Fish}(q_0)=G_{\rm ar}^{\R},
 \qquad
 \\operatorname{Ran} A_{\rm Fish}=\\operatorname{Ran} P_{\rm ren}.}
 \tag{V20.12}\label{eq:v20-tangent-duality}
\end{equation}
Thus the finite neighbouring-law test converges exactly to the arithmetic
source-occurrence gate left open in V19.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Equation~\eqref{eq:v20-ar-limit} is the definition of the differential of the
rank-one projector together with \Cref{lem:v20-projector-FS} and the V12
identification of its pullback metric.  Equation~\eqref{eq:v20-ren-limit} is
\Cref{lem:v20-Hellinger-Fisher}.  Full rank makes matrix inverse square roots
continuous, so \eqref{eq:v20-loss-limit} follows by continuity of every finite
matrix operation in \eqref{eq:v20-finite-loss}.  The two conclusions in
\eqref{eq:v20-tangent-duality} follow from the two assumed limits and the
rank-six version of the zero-loss argument in
\Cref{thm:v20-finite-secant-duality}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Quantitative stability of the finite loss]
\label{thm:v20-loss-stability}
Let $A:\R^6\to\mathcal H$ have $A^*A\succ0$ and
$\sigma=\sigma_{\min}(A)$.  Let $V$ be another rank-six synthesis with
\[
 \delta:=\|V-A\|_{\op}<\sigma.
\]
For any rank-six orthogonal projector $P$, define
\[
 \varepsilon(A;P)
 :=6-\Tr(PP_A),
 \qquad
 \varepsilon(V;P)
 :=6-\Tr(PP_V),
\]
where $P_A,P_V$ are the range projectors.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 |\varepsilon(V;P)-\varepsilon(A;P)|
 \le
 6\sqrt2\,\frac{\delta}{\sigma-\delta}.}
 \tag{V20.13}\label{eq:v20-loss-stability}
\end{equation}
If $V$ is the one-sided Hellinger secant synthesis of a $C^2$ family and
\[
 M^2:=\sum_{a=1}^6
 \sup_{|t|\le|h|}
 \left\|\frac{\dd^2}{\dd t^2}
 \mathfrak h(p(q_0+te_a))\right\|^2,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\delta\le \frac{|h|M}{2}.}
 \tag{V20.14}\label{eq:v20-secant-error}
\end{equation}
For the V12 arithmetic source normalization,
\eqref{eq:v20-ar-floor} gives
\[
 \sigma_{\min}(A_{\rm ar})>\sqrt{0.0706}>0.2657.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Since $\sigma_{\min}(V)\ge\sigma-\delta$, every unit vector in $\\operatorname{Ran} V$ has
distance at most $\delta/(\sigma-\delta)$ from $\\operatorname{Ran} A$, and the same estimate
holds with the two ranges exchanged.  Hence
\[
 \|P_V-P_A\|_{\op}
 \le\frac{\delta}{\sigma-\delta}.
\]
Both projectors have rank six, so
\[
 \|P_V-P_A\|_{\HS}
 \le\sqrt{12}\,\|P_V-P_A\|_{\op}.
\]
Also $\|P\|_{\HS}=\sqrt6$.  Therefore
\[
 |\Tr(P(P_V-P_A))|
 \le\sqrt6\sqrt{12}\,\frac{\delta}{\sigma-\delta},
\]
which is \eqref{eq:v20-loss-stability}.  Taylor's theorem with integral
remainder gives a column error at most
$|h|M_a/2$; summing the squared column errors bounds the operator norm by the
Hilbert--Schmidt norm and yields \eqref{eq:v20-secant-error}.  The last bound is
\eqref{eq:v20-ar-floor}.
\end{proof}

\section{A minimal positive Store realization exists for every arithmetic source metric}
\label{sec:v20-exponential-completion}

The preceding tests are occurrence tests.  It is nevertheless useful to know
whether positivity of probability laws itself forbids the desired source
geometry.  It does not.

Let $p_0$ be the uniform law on the twelve half-edge states and let
$\mathcal R_2=\\operatorname{Ran} P_{\rm ren}$.  Since $\mathcal R_2$ is a sum of nontrivial
standard $S_4$ representations, it is orthogonal to the constant vector.  Under
the unitary identification
\[
 U_0:L^2(\Omega,p_0)\to\ell^2(\Omega),
 \qquad
 (U_0f)(\omega)=\sqrt{p_0(\omega)}\,f(\omega),
\]
write $\widetilde{\mathcal R}_2=U_0^{-1}\mathcal R_2$.

\begin{theorem}[Minimal exponential-family realization of an arbitrary positive arithmetic metric]
\label{thm:v20-exponential-realization}
Let $G\succ0$ be any real $6\times6$ matrix.  Choose an isometry
\[
 B:\R^6\longrightarrow\widetilde{\mathcal R}_2
 \subset L^2(\Omega,p_0)
\]
and put
\[
 S:=BG^{1/2}.
\]
For $\theta\in\R^6$ define the strictly positive law
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 p_\theta(\omega)
 ={\\frac{p_0(\\omega)\\exp((S\\theta)(\\omega))}{\\sum_{\\nu\\in\\Omega}p_0(\\nu)\\exp((S\\theta)(\\nu))}}.}
 \tag{V20.15}\label{eq:v20-exponential-family}
\end{equation}
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the score synthesis at $\theta=0$ is exactly $S$;
\item the Fisher information is exactly
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{I_{\rm Fish}(0)=G;}
 \tag{V20.16}\label{eq:v20-exp-Fisher}
\end{equation}
\item the Hellinger tangent range is exactly the represented renewal source
plane:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \\operatorname{Ran}\dd\mathfrak h[p_\theta]_{\theta=0}
 =\mathcal R_2;}
 \tag{V20.17}\label{eq:v20-exp-range}
\end{equation}
\item six real parameters are minimal among smooth families with rank-six
Fisher information.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, taking $G=G_{\rm ar}^{\R}$ proves that the arithmetic tangent
metric and the saturated renewal plane are simultaneously realizable by a
strictly positive Store law family with no additional source dimension.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every column of $B$ is centered because
$\widetilde{\mathcal R}_2\perp1$; hence every column of $S$ is centered.  If
\[
 \psi(\theta)=\log\sum_\omega p_0(\omega)e^{(S\theta)(\omega)},
\]
then
\[
 \log p_\theta(\omega)
 =\log p_0(\omega)+(S\theta)(\omega)-\psi(\theta).
\]
Since $\dd\psi(0)=\mathbb E_{p_0}S=0$, the score columns at the origin are
exactly the columns of $S$.  Their Fisher Gram is
\[
 S^*S
 =G^{1/2}B^*BG^{1/2}
 =G,
\]
proving \eqref{eq:v20-exp-Fisher}.  By
\Cref{lem:v20-Hellinger-Fisher}, the Hellinger tangent is $U_0S$, whose range
is $U_0\widetilde{\mathcal R}_2=\mathcal R_2$, proving
\eqref{eq:v20-exp-range}.  Finally, a Fisher matrix of rank six is the Gram of
the differential of the family and therefore cannot be generated by a
parameter manifold of real dimension below six.  The construction uses exactly
six parameters.
\end{proof}

\begin{scope}[Existence is not occurrence]
\label{fire:v20-existence-not-occurrence}
The family \eqref{eq:v20-exponential-family} is built using the target metric
$G$.  It proves that probability positivity, normalization, and the twelve
half-edge alphabet impose no obstruction to the desired six-dimensional
source geometry.  It does \emph{not} prove that the locked Store dynamics
realizes this family, that its physical deformation coordinates are the
arithmetic moduli coordinates, or that its transition law generates the same
transport.  Using \eqref{eq:v20-exponential-family} as the occurrence witness
would be circular.
\end{scope}

\begin{theorem}[One static Store law does not determine its tangent source]
\label{cth:v20-static-law-no-tangent}
Let $p_0$ be any strictly positive law on a finite alphabet with at least two
points.  For every finite centered score bank
$S:\R^m\to L^2(\Omega,p_0)$, the exponential construction
\eqref{eq:v20-exponential-family} has reference law $p_0$ and score synthesis
$S$.  Consequently the static law $p_0$ alone determines neither the Fisher
metric nor the source tangent.  Actual neighbouring laws, an executable
unnormalized deformation, or an equivalent physical derivative panel are
necessary to identify the tangent source.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The proof of \Cref{thm:v20-exponential-realization} uses only centering of the
chosen score bank and works for any finite alphabet.  Distinct centered banks
therefore produce the same $p_0$ with different tangent source Grams and
ranges.
\end{proof}

\section{V20 status and exact next attack}
\label{sec:v20-status}

V20 moves the unresolved arithmetic occurrence gate one step upstream.  The
six tangent writers of V19 need not be assumed at the entrance.  They can be
approached through six actual neighbouring Store laws on the same resolved
half-edge record.  The finite packet
\[
 \boxed{
 G_{\Theta,h},\qquad
 G_{{\rm Hel},h},\qquad
 \varepsilon_{{\rm Hel}\mid{\rm ren}}(h)}
\]
is defined before differentiation and has an exact interpretation:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(S\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item equality of the two finite Grams gives the unique source-fixing unitary
between the arithmetic projector secants and the renewal Hellinger secants;
\item zero finite renewal loss places that physical secant source exactly in
the represented saturated renewal plane;
\item a genuine shrinking family transports these tests to the arithmetic
Fubini--Study and physical Fisher tangent metrics, recovering the V19 source
loss as a limit;
\item a minimal six-parameter positive Store family realizing the required
metric and range exists, so the remaining obstacle is selection/occurrence,
not positivity or source dimension.
\end{enumerate}

The next noncircular audit is therefore more literal than V19's tangent-writer
request:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(N\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item acquire six actual neighbouring Store laws associated with six
independently declared real arithmetic moduli directions, or acquire one
executable six-parameter unnormalized Store deformation from which they are
obtained;
\item compute the Hellinger secants and their complete Gram before fitting any
smooth interpolation;
\item compare that Gram with the finite arithmetic theta-projector secant Gram
and evaluate \eqref{eq:v20-finite-loss};
\item on a shrinking family, verify the quantitative stability window
\eqref{eq:v20-loss-stability}--\eqref{eq:v20-secant-error};
\item only on the zero/equality branch proceed to the binary complex
orientation, the residual $U(1)$ phase, and transfer/Krylov equality.
\end{enumerate}

A failure to supply the neighbouring laws is now the exact occurrence
obstruction.  A positive finite loss is a source-range obstruction.  A Gram
mismatch is a metric/source-duality obstruction.  None should be normalized
away by choosing the exponential completion of
\Cref{thm:v20-exponential-realization}.

All V1--V19 mathematical bodies and their status ledgers are preserved byte

exponential-family realization, and the static-law tangent nonidentifiability

\section{V21: a canonical complex Store score source and the real-structure gate}
\label{sec:v21-context}

V20 replaced the unobserved arithmetic tangent writer by finite Hellinger
secants of actual neighbouring laws.  The remaining occurrence question was
whether the selected Store possesses a non-target-fitted six-parameter local
family with the correct source dimension and a natural complex structure.
The inherited primitive-score theorem already contains exactly the data needed
for such a construction: on one resolved Store cell the branch-local tangent
space is three dimensional, with orthogonal coordinates given by the active
Doob innovation, route provenance, and endpoint-sign innovation~\cite{GT77}.

The present continuation isolates the two-dimensional part which is invisible
to the later active phase, complexifies it using the already resolved endpoint
sign, and then passes to four cells.  The result is a target-independent
complex rank-three standard source, together with an explicit conditional
exponential family of Store laws.  This removes the arbitrary six-dimensional
statistical completion used only as a nonemptiness benchmark in V20.

A second point is equally important.  Classical Hellinger/Fisher data determine
the real source metric but not the holomorphic orientation of the arithmetic
theta source.  The Store score construction supplies a natural candidate real
structure and hence reduces the remaining complex ambiguity to a discrete
comparison.  It does not identify the Store and arithmetic complex structures
without an actual common occurrence map.

\section{The intrinsic future-null score plane}
\label{sec:v21-future-null}

Recall the resolved primitive branch alphabet
\[
 \Sigma_{\rm ren}=\{hh,hp,pp,b_+,b_-\}
\]
with stationary branch masses
\[
 \mu=(1,4,2,2,2)/11.
\]
The inherited score theorem gives the row-centred three-dimensional source
\[
 \mathscr I_{\rm br}
 =\ker\mathbb E[\,\cdot\mid X_n]
 =\Span_{\R}\{\widehat\eta,\zeta,\epsilon\},
\]
where the normalized vectors are orthonormal.  In the branch order above,
\begin{align}
 \zeta&=
 \left(-\frac{\sqrt{22}}2,\frac{\sqrt{22}}8,
       -\frac{\sqrt{22}}4,\frac{\sqrt{22}}8,
       \frac{\sqrt{22}}8\right),
 \tag{V21.1}\label{eq:v21-zeta}\\
 \epsilon&=
 \left(0,0,0,\frac{\sqrt{11}}2,-\frac{\sqrt{11}}2\right).
 \tag{V21.2}\label{eq:v21-epsilon}
\end{align}

\begin{definition}[Future-null one-cell score plane]
\label{def:v21-future-null}
Define
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal N_{\rm fn}
 :=\mathscr I_{\rm br}^{\R}
   \cap\ker\mathbb E[\,\cdot\mid X_{n+1}].}
 \tag{V21.3}\label{eq:v21-future-null}
\]
This definition uses only the resolved one-step Store law and its current/next
phase records.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact future-null decomposition]
\label{thm:v21-future-null}
One has
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal N_{\rm fn}
 =\Span_{\R}\{\zeta,\epsilon\},
 \qquad \dim_{\R}\mathcal N_{\rm fn}=2.}
 \tag{V21.4}\label{eq:v21-future-null-span}
\end{equation}
The orthogonal complement inside $\mathscr I_{\rm br}^{\R}$ is the normalized
active Doob direction $\R\widehat\eta$.  In particular,
$\mathcal N_{\rm fn}$ is intrinsic to the Store branch law and is not selected
using the arithmetic target.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The inherited primitive-score theorem gives
\[
 \mathbb E[\zeta\mid X_{n+1}]
 =\mathbb E[\epsilon\mid X_{n+1}]=0,
\]
so the displayed two-plane lies in \eqref{eq:v21-future-null}.  The target
space of conditional expectation onto the two-valued variable $X_{n+1}$ has a
one-dimensional centred subspace.  It remains only to check that the
restriction of this conditional expectation to $\mathscr I_{\rm br}$ is
nonzero.  For the unnormalized active innovation
$\eta=\varphi(X_{n+1})-\rho\varphi(X_n)$, with
$\rho=-7/15$, direct evaluation gives
\[
 \mathbb E[\eta\mid X_{n+1}=H]
 =-\frac{176\sqrt{30}}{1125}\ne0,
\]
\[
 \mathbb E[\eta\mid X_{n+1}=P]
 =\frac{88\sqrt{30}}{675}\ne0.
\]
Thus the restricted conditional-expectation map has rank one.  Its kernel in
the three-dimensional space $\mathscr I_{\rm br}^{\R}$ therefore has dimension
two and must equal the span of $\zeta,\epsilon$.  Orthogonality to
$\widehat\eta$ follows from the inherited orthonormal score decomposition.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Unique six-real-dimensional future-null tetrahedral source]
\label{cor:v21-four-cell-null}
For four independent Store cells let
$W_0=\one_4^\perp$ be the real standard $S_4$ module.  Inside the complete
primitive tetrahedral score carrier
\[
 W_0\otimes\mathscr I_{\rm br}^{\R}
\]
the unique $S_4$-stable source which is pointwise future-null in the sense of
\eqref{eq:v21-future-null} is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal S_{\rm fn}^{\R}
 =W_0\otimes\mathcal N_{\rm fn},
 \qquad \dim_{\R}\mathcal S_{\rm fn}^{\R}=6.}
 \tag{V21.5}\label{eq:v21-six-plane}
\end{equation}
Its inherited Fisher/source metric is the Euclidean tensor product metric.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The later-phase conditional expectation acts as the identity on the cell-label
factor and as the one-cell conditional expectation on
$\mathscr I_{\rm br}^{\R}$.  Hence its kernel on the standard four-cell score
carrier is exactly
$W_0\otimes\mathcal N_{\rm fn}$.  The dimensions are $3\cdot2=6$, and the
metric is Euclidean because $\zeta,\epsilon$ are orthonormal and the four-cell
standard synthesis is isometric on $W_0$.
\end{proof}

\section{A proper complex Store score and an explicit six-parameter law family}
\label{sec:v21-complex-score}

\begin{definition}[Proper complex primitive score]
\label{def:v21-complex-score}
Set
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 w:=\frac{\zeta+i\epsilon}{\sqrt2}.}
 \tag{V21.6}\label{eq:v21-w}
\end{equation}
In the branch order $(hh,hp,pp,b_+,b_-)$ this is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 w=\left(
 -\frac{\sqrt{11}}2,
 \frac{\sqrt{11}}8,
 -\frac{\sqrt{11}}4,
 \frac{\sqrt{11}}8+i\frac{\sqrt{22}}4,
 \frac{\sqrt{11}}8-i\frac{\sqrt{22}}4
 \right).}
 \tag{V21.7}\label{eq:v21-w-values}
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Proper complex score and complex standard source]
\label{thm:v21-proper-complex-score}
The score $w$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E_\mu w=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_\mu|w|^2=1,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_\mu w^2=0,}
 \tag{V21.8}\label{eq:v21-proper}
\end{equation}
and
\[
 \mathbb E[w\mid X_{n+1}]=0.
\]
It is therefore a proper complex martingale-difference score.  For four
independent cells, the centred complex synthesis
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal S_{\rm fn}^{\C}
 =\left\{(z_1w_1+\cdots+z_4w_4):
 z_i\in\C,\ \sum_i z_i=0\right\}}
 \tag{V21.9}\label{eq:v21-complex-standard}
\end{equation}
is a complex rank-three $S_4$ standard source with Hermitian Gram
$I_{W_0^\C}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Equations \eqref{eq:v21-zeta}--\eqref{eq:v21-epsilon} and the inherited
orthonormality of $\zeta,\epsilon$ give
\[
 \mathbb E|w|^2
 =\frac12(\|\zeta\|^2+\|\epsilon\|^2)=1,
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb Ew^2
 =\frac12(\|\zeta\|^2-\|\epsilon\|^2
            +2i\langle\zeta,\epsilon\rangle)=0.
\]
Centering and future-nullity follow componentwise from
\Cref{thm:v21-future-null}.  For four independent cells, cross-cell score
covariances vanish.  Therefore
\[
 \mathbb E\left[
 \overline{\sum_i z_iw_i}\,
 \sum_j y_jw_j\right]
 =\sum_i\bar z_i y_i.
\]
Restricting to $\sum_i z_i=0$ gives the standard complex module with unit
Hermitian Gram.  Cell permutations give the usual complexified standard
$S_4$ action.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Complex Brownian score limit]
\label{cor:v21-complex-Brownian}
For one cell,
\[
 \sqrt\tau\sum_{n<t/\tau}w_n
\]
converges to a standard circular complex Brownian motion.  Four independent
cells, restricted to the centred standard subspace, converge to a complex
rank-three Brownian motion with covariance $I_{W_0^\C}$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The inherited vector martingale functional central limit theorem applies to
the real pair $(\zeta,\epsilon)$.  Its covariance is $I_2$ and the
pseudocovariance vanishes by \eqref{eq:v21-proper}, which is precisely the
circular complex Brownian normalization.  Independence across cells and
orthogonal projection to $W_0$ give the rank-three statement.
\end{proof}

The score also produces a target-independent finite law family.  For
$z=x+iy\in\C$ define the one-cell conditional law
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 p_z(a\mid X_n)
 =p_0(a\mid X_n)
 \exp\!\left(
 \sqrt2\,\Re(\bar z\,w(a))-\psi_{X_n}(z)
 \right),}
 \tag{V21.10}\label{eq:v21-one-cell-family}
\end{equation}
where $\psi_x(z)$ is the row log-normalizer.  Explicitly,
\begin{align}
 Z_H(x)
 &=\frac15e^{-x\sqrt{22}/2}
   +\frac45e^{x\sqrt{22}/8},
 \tag{V21.11}\label{eq:v21-ZH}\\
 Z_P(x,y)
 &=\frac13e^{-x\sqrt{22}/4}
   +\frac23e^{x\sqrt{22}/8}
      \cosh\!\left(\frac{y\sqrt{11}}2\right).
 \tag{V21.12}\label{eq:v21-ZP}
\end{align}
Thus $\psi_H=\log Z_H$ and $\psi_P=\log Z_P$.

\begin{theorem}[Canonical six-parameter Store deformation]
\label{thm:v21-canonical-Store-family}
Let
\[
 \mathcal E_{\rm can}
 :=\{(z_1,z_2,z_3,z_4)\in\C^4:\sum_i z_i=0\}
 \cong W_0^\C.
\]
For four independent primitive Store cells define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbf P_z:=\bigotimes_{i=1}^4p_{z_i}.}
 \tag{V21.13}\label{eq:v21-product-family}
\end{equation}
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item $\mathbf P_z$ is strictly positive for every finite $z$ and is defined
using only the resolved primitive Store law and its intrinsic future-null score
plane;
\item the family is $S_4$-equivariant under permutation of the four cells;
\item its real parameter dimension is six, and its Fisher metric at $z=0$ is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 I_{\rm Fish,0}(\delta z,\delta y)
 =\Re\sum_{i=1}^4\overline{\delta z_i}\,\delta y_i;}
 \tag{V21.14}\label{eq:v21-Fisher}
\end{equation}
\item its Hellinger tangent range is exactly the canonical six-real-dimensional
source $\mathcal S_{\rm fn}^{\R}$ of \eqref{eq:v21-six-plane};
\item six real parameters are minimal for this rank-six source.
\end{enumerate}
No arithmetic quantity enters the definition of $\mathbf P_z$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Strict positivity and normalization follow from the finite exponential formula.
Permutation equivariance is immediate because every cell uses the same
one-cell family.  At the origin a real tangent $\delta z_i$ has score
\[
 \sqrt2\,\Re(\overline{\delta z_i}w_i).
\]
Using $\mathbb E|w|^2=1$ and $\mathbb Ew^2=0$ gives
\[
 \mathbb E\left[
 2\Re(\overline{\delta z_i}w_i)
   \Re(\overline{\delta y_i}w_i)
 \right]
 =\Re(\overline{\delta z_i}\delta y_i).
\]
Cross-cell covariances vanish, proving \eqref{eq:v21-Fisher}.  The Hellinger
derivative is the square-root-weighted score synthesis, so its range is
$W_0\otimes\Span\{\zeta,\epsilon\}$, namely
$\mathcal S_{\rm fn}^{\R}$.  A rank-six Fisher matrix requires at least six
real parameters.
\end{proof}

\begin{scope}[Canonical family versus historical occurrence]
\label{fire:v21-family-occurrence}
The family \eqref{eq:v21-product-family} is no longer fitted to the arithmetic
metric: it is selected entirely by the Store branch law, the current/next
phase filtration, and the future-null score condition.  It is therefore a
canonical Store deformation candidate, unlike the target-metric completion of
V20.  The inherited score theorem guarantees that it is a legitimate
fixed-support conditional exponential deformation.  It does not prove that the
historical selected Store autonomously executes this six-parameter family or
that its parameter labels coincide with arithmetic moduli labels.  Actual
execution or an equivalent physical derivative panel remains an occurrence
row.
\end{scope}

\section{Arithmetic K\"ahler data and the phase information absent from Hellinger metrics}
\label{sec:v21-kahler}

The arithmetic marked theta source is a holomorphic map into projective space.
Its tangent therefore carries not only the real Fubini--Study metric used in
V20 but also the corresponding symplectic form.

\begin{lemma}[Projector formula for the Fubini--Study K\"ahler pair]
\label{lem:v21-projector-kahler}
Let $\rho=|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$ be a smooth rank-one projector and let
$D_u=\dd\rho[u]$, $D_v=\dd\rho[v]$.  Then
\begin{align}
 \boxed{
 g_{\rm FS}(u,v)
 =\frac12\Tr(D_uD_v),}
 \tag{V21.15}\label{eq:v21-FS-g}\\
 \boxed{
 \omega_{\rm FS}(u,v)
 =\frac1{2i}\Tr\bigl(\rho[D_u,D_v]\bigr).}
 \tag{V21.16}\label{eq:v21-FS-omega}
\end{align}
In horizontal lifts these are respectively
$\Re\langle\dd\psi[u],\dd\psi[v]\rangle$ and
$\Im\langle\dd\psi[u],\dd\psi[v]\rangle$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Choose horizontal tangent lifts $\xi=\dd\psi[u]$ and
$\eta=\dd\psi[v]$.  The metric identity is V20's projector calculation.  Also
\[
 \langle\psi,D_uD_v\psi\rangle=\langle\xi,\eta\rangle,
 \qquad
 \langle\psi,D_vD_u\psi\rangle=\langle\eta,\xi\rangle.
\]
Taking their difference gives
$\Tr(\rho[D_u,D_v])=2i\Im\langle\xi,\eta\rangle$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The arithmetic source carries nontrivial phase geometry]
\label{thm:v21-arithmetic-phase}
At the arithmetic fibre, the theta-null source map of V12 is locally
biholomorphic.  Hence its pullback Fubini--Study two-form
$\omega_{\rm ar}$ is nondegenerate on the six-real-dimensional arithmetic
tangent.  In the declared complex period coordinates the inherited certified
source matrix satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 -0.065518601724154544
 <\Im(g_{\rm src})_{13}
 <-0.065518601724154543,}
 \tag{V21.17}\label{eq:v21-ar-phase-witness}
\end{equation}
so this phase geometry is not identically zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Local biholomorphy and positivity are the V12 inverse and source-metric
theorems.  A local biholomorphism pulls the nondegenerate Fubini--Study
K\"ahler form back to a nondegenerate two-form.  The explicit nonzero entry is
the V12 certified interval \eqref{eq:v12-imaginary-witness}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Classical Hellinger data do not determine holomorphic orientation]
\label{cth:v21-Hellinger-no-orientation}
The complete family of classical probability laws
$\{\mathbf P_z\}$, their Hellinger vectors, Hellinger secant Grams, Fisher
metrics, and source ranges do not by themselves distinguish the two
$S_4$-equivariant orthogonal complex structures
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 J_+=I_{W_0}\otimes
 \begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 J_-=-J_+.}
 \tag{V21.18}\label{eq:v21-two-J}
\end{equation}
Consequently a successful V20 real Hellinger/Fisher source match does not by
itself prove complex-linear arithmetic--renewal source duality.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
All classical law and Hellinger quantities depend only on real probability
vectors and real inner products.  Replacing the declared complex structure
$J_+$ by $J_-$ changes none of those objects.  On the $S_4$ module
$W_0\otimes\R^2$, Schur's lemma gives
\[
 \End_{S_4}(W_0\otimes\R^2)=I_{W_0}\otimes M_2(\R).
\]
An orthogonal complex structure in this algebra is
$I_{W_0}\otimes j$ with $j^2=-I_2$ and $j^*j=I_2$.  In real dimension two
these equations have exactly the two solutions displayed in
\eqref{eq:v21-two-J}.  Thus the ambiguity is genuine and binary.
\end{proof}

\section{The Store real structure and the reduced complex-duality residual}
\label{sec:v21-real-structure}

The resolved labels $b_+,b_-$ define an involution of the branch alphabet:
\[
 \kappa_{\rm br}(b_+)=b_-,\qquad
 \kappa_{\rm br}(b_-)=b_+,
\]
fixing $hh,hp,pp$.  It preserves the primitive law.

\begin{proposition}[Store conjugation on the complex score]
\label{prop:v21-Store-conjugation}
The pullback by $\kappa_{\rm br}$ fixes $\zeta$, sends
$\epsilon\mapsto-\epsilon$, and hence
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{w\longmapsto\bar w.}
 \tag{V21.19}\label{eq:v21-w-conj}
\end{equation}
On the four-cell complex standard source it therefore induces the ordinary
antilinear conjugation
\[
 K_{\rm ren}(z_1,\ldots,z_4)
 =(\bar z_1,\ldots,\bar z_4).
\]
The canonical family obeys
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \kappa_{\rm br\,*}\mathbf P_z
 =\mathbf P_{\bar z}.}
 \tag{V21.20}\label{eq:v21-family-real}
\end{equation}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The explicit vectors \eqref{eq:v21-zeta}--\eqref{eq:v21-epsilon} have the
stated parity under exchange of $b_+,b_-$.  Equation
\eqref{eq:v21-w-conj} follows.  The exponential family
\eqref{eq:v21-one-cell-family} depends on
$\sqrt2\Re(\bar z w)$, which is invariant under simultaneous
$z\mapsto\bar z$ and $w\mapsto\bar w$.  Tensoring gives
\eqref{eq:v21-family-real}.
\end{proof}

V4 and V12 give the arithmetic marked theta source and its tangent an
antilinear real descent $K_{\rm ar}$.  After an independently established
$S_4$ label identification, compare it with $K_{\rm ren}$.

\begin{theorem}[Real descent collapses the residual phase]
\label{thm:v21-real-descent-phase}
Suppose the V20 real source-range and metric tests pass at the tangent level,
and suppose an $S_4$-equivariant complex-linear unitary
\[
 U:\mathcal T_{\rm ar}\longrightarrow\mathcal S_{\rm fn}^{\C}
\]
is sought.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item without imposing real descent, the $S_4$-equivariant unitary ambiguity is
one phase $U(1)$;
\item if in addition
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{UK_{\rm ar}=K_{\rm ren}U,}
 \tag{V21.21}\label{eq:v21-real-intertwining}
\end{equation}
then the ambiguity reduces to
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{U\longmapsto\pm U;}
 \tag{V21.22}\label{eq:v21-sign-ambiguity}
\end{equation}
\item if a consistently oriented top exterior source is also fixed, the sign is
fixed as well.
\end{enumerate}
Thus the Store endpoint-sign real structure converts the continuous phase left
in V15 into at most one binary comparison once real descent is matched.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Both complex sources are copies of the irreducible complex standard
$S_4$ module.  Schur's lemma makes any two equivariant complex-linear
intertwiners differ by a scalar $c\in\C^*$.  Unitarity gives $|c|=1$, proving
(i).  If both intertwiners commute with the declared real descents, then
$c=\bar c$, so $c=\pm1$, proving (ii).  On complex dimension three the two
choices act on the top exterior line by determinants $+1$ and $-1$;
compatibility with a fixed oriented determinant source therefore selects one
of them.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Complex-source residual after the real V20 gate]
\label{def:v21-complex-residual}
After a real source-fixing isometry $U_\R$ has been obtained from the V20
finite/tangent gate, define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Delta_{J,K}(U_\R)
 :=\|U_\R J_{\rm ar}-J_{\rm ren}U_\R\|_{\HS}^2
  +\|U_\R K_{\rm ar}-K_{\rm ren}U_\R\|_{\HS}^2.}
 \tag{V21.23}\label{eq:v21-complex-residual}
\end{equation}
Here the second term is interpreted on the realified carriers, where the
antilinear involutions are ordinary real-linear isometries.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Exact complex source gate]
\label{prop:v21-complex-gate}
The residual \eqref{eq:v21-complex-residual} vanishes exactly when the V20 real
source equivalence extends through $U_\R$ to an $S_4$-compatible complex source
equivalence respecting the arithmetic and Store real structures.  On the
multiplicity-two standard branch there are only the two candidate complex
orientations \eqref{eq:v21-two-J}; choosing the wrong one changes the complex
structure by $2J$ and contributes
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\|J_+-J_-\|_{\HS}^2=24.}
 \tag{V21.24}\label{eq:v21-J-gap}
\end{equation}
Thus the orientation failure has a fixed nonzero finite witness.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Both summands in \eqref{eq:v21-complex-residual} are nonnegative and vanish
exactly on the corresponding intertwining relations.  Those relations are the
definition of a complex-linear real-structure-preserving source equivalence.
For the final statement, $J_-=-J_+$ and $J_+$ is orthogonal on a real
six-dimensional space.  Therefore
\[
 \|J_+-J_-\|_{\HS}^2
 =4\|J_+\|_{\HS}^2=4\cdot6=24.
\]
\end{proof}

\section{V21 status and next attack}
\label{sec:v21-status}

The Store side of the first arithmetic--renewal source comparison now has a
canonical target-independent complex candidate:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \text{resolved primitive Store law}
 \longrightarrow
 \mathcal N_{\rm fn}=\Span\{\zeta,\epsilon\}
 \longrightarrow
 w=\frac{\zeta+i\epsilon}{\sqrt2}
 \longrightarrow
 W_0^\C.}
 \tag{V21.25}\label{eq:v21-chain}
\end{equation}
It comes with:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(S\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item an exact unit Hermitian source metric;
\item an explicit strictly positive six-real-parameter conditional exponential
family \eqref{eq:v21-product-family}, defined without arithmetic input;
\item a circular complex Brownian scaling source;
\item an actual Store branch involution which acts as complex conjugation.
\end{enumerate}

This strengthens V20 in one direction and sharpens its remaining occurrence
claim in another.  The target-metric exponential completion of V20 is no
longer the only available six-parameter Store family: the future-null score
condition selects one canonically from the Store law itself.  Nevertheless the
historical selected Store has not yet been shown to execute that family, and no
same-history map from arithmetic moduli moves to the Store deformation
parameters has been acquired.

The next finite programme is therefore:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(N\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item use the predeclared family \eqref{eq:v21-product-family} to generate its
six finite Hellinger neighbouring laws at a chosen small step, without
inspecting the arithmetic target;
\item compare their finite Gram with the independently computed arithmetic
theta-projector secant Gram of V20 and evaluate the renewal loss against
$P_{\rm ren}$;
\item on a zero/equality branch, compare the arithmetic and Store real
structures through \eqref{eq:v21-complex-residual};
\item only after this complex source gate passes, reopen transfer/Krylov and
Frobenius--Wilson comparison.
\end{enumerate}

A finite Gram mismatch is a real source obstruction.  Vanishing real source
loss together with nonzero \eqref{eq:v21-complex-residual} is a complex/real-
descent obstruction.  Neither should be removed by rechoosing the Store family
after the arithmetic comparison has been evaluated.

All V1--V20 mathematical bodies and their historical status ledgers are
