\section{V22: curvature obstruction to the canonical product Store family and the second-order occurrence gate}
\label{sec:v22-context}

V21 supplied a target-independent complex rank-three Store source and a canonical
six-real-parameter conditional exponential family obtained from four independent
primitive cells.  At the reference law its Fisher metric is the Euclidean metric
on the complex standard module, so the first-order source dimension, real
structure, and complex structure are all compatible with the arithmetic theta
source.  What remained untested was the nonlinear local geometry of the two
families.

The present continuation performs that test before acquiring another arbitrary
finite-neighbour panel.  The arithmetic source side is already rigid enough:
V12 proves that the marked theta-source map is a local biholomorphism onto an
open subset of projective three-space and that its source metric is exactly the
pullback of the Fubini--Study metric.  Hence its intrinsic curvature is the
Fubini--Study curvature, independently of the chosen period coordinates.  On
the Store side, the V21 family is a product natural exponential family
restricted to the centred tetrahedral coefficient space.  That product
structure forces an exactly flat two-plane at the reference law.  Therefore the
V21 family cannot be locally isometric to the arithmetic theta-source germ,
even after an arbitrary smooth reparameterization and tangent-space isometry.

This obstruction does not invalidate the V21 source construction.  It says
that the canonical future-null score family is a correct first-order source
candidate but not a complete nonlinear arithmetic dual.  The missing
information begins at second order.  The mature Grand-Tensor calculus already
contains the appropriate upstream object: actual intervention cubes produce
finite Hellinger interaction secants before a tangent is assumed, and their
shrinking limit is the efficient connected Fisher action~\cite{GT77}.  The
last part of V22 therefore formulates a finite second-order curvature audit
which can detect precisely the additional connected occurrence needed by a
nonlinear arithmetic comparison.

\section{Hessian curvature of the canonical Store exponential chart}
\label{sec:v22-store-curvature}

We first isolate a finite-dimensional differential-geometric fact.  Let
$\Psi$ be a smooth strictly convex potential on an open set in a real affine
space and put
\[
 g_{ij}=\partial_i\partial_j\Psi,
 \qquad
 C_{ijk}=\partial_i\partial_j\partial_k\Psi.
\]
Thus $g$ is a Hessian metric and $C$ is its cubic tensor.

\begin{lemma}[Curvature of a Hessian metric]
\label{lem:v22-hessian-curvature}
At a point at which affine coordinates have been chosen so that $g=I$, the
Riemann curvature tensor, with convention
$R(X,Y,Y,X)=\langle R(X,Y)Y,X\rangle$, satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 R(X,Y,Y,X)
 =\frac14\left(
   \|C(X,Y,\cdot)\|^2
   -\langle C(X,X,\cdot),C(Y,Y,\cdot)\rangle
 \right).}
 \label{eq:v22-hessian-curvature}
\end{equation}
In particular, if
\[
 C(X,X,Z)=C(X,Y,Z)=C(Y,Y,Z)=0
 \qquad\text{for every }Z,
\]
then the sectional curvature of the plane $\Span\{X,Y\}$ is zero whenever
$X,Y$ are orthonormal.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
In affine coordinates the lowered Christoffel symbols are
$\Gamma_{ijk}=C_{ijk}/2$.  At the chosen point,
$\partial_i g^{jk}=-C_{ijk}$ after identifying indices with the Euclidean
metric.  Differentiating the raised Christoffel symbols, the fourth derivatives
of $\Psi$ cancel because they are fully symmetric.  One obtains
\[
 R_{ijkl}
 =\frac14\sum_p
 \bigl(C_{jlp}C_{ikp}-C_{ilp}C_{jkp}\bigr).
\]
Substituting $(i,j,k,l)=(X,Y,Y,X)$ gives
\eqref{eq:v22-hessian-curvature}.  The final statement is immediate.
\end{proof}

The V21 one-cell conditional family is a natural exponential family in two
real parameters.  Freeze the input-phase weights at their reference values,
which is exactly the source experiment used to define the V21 Fisher metric,
and let $\psi:\R^2\to\R$ denote the resulting one-cell log-partition
potential.  Four independent identical cells have potential
\[
 \Psi(z_1,z_2,z_3,z_4)=\sum_{i=1}^4\psi(z_i),
 \qquad z_i\in\R^2.
\]
Restrict this potential to
\[
 W_0\otimes\R^2,
 \qquad
 W_0=\{u\in\R^4:\sum_i u_i=0\}.
\]
At the origin the V21 normalization gives the Euclidean metric.

\begin{theorem}[Universal balanced flat plane for four identical product cells]
\label{thm:v22-balanced-flat-plane}
Let a two-real-parameter one-cell natural exponential family have positive
Fisher metric at its reference point.  Normalize its two tangent coordinates
so that the one-cell Fisher metric is $I_2$.  Form four independent identical
copies and restrict to the centred tetrahedral parameter space
$W_0\otimes\R^2$.  Put
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 u=\frac12(1,1,-1,-1)\in W_0,
 \qquad \|u\|=1.}
 \label{eq:v22-balanced-u}
\end{equation}
For any orthonormal one-cell tangent vectors $a,b\in\R^2$, the two vectors
\[
 X=u\otimes a,
 \qquad
 Y=u\otimes b
\]
are orthonormal and span a zero-sectional-curvature plane at the product
reference point:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{K_{\rm prod}(X,Y)=0.}
 \label{eq:v22-product-flat}
\end{equation}
This conclusion is independent of the one-cell third cumulants.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $C_{\rm cell}$ be the one-cell cubic tensor.  The cubic tensor of the
four-cell product family, restricted to the centred coefficient space, obeys
\[
 C(u\otimes a,u\otimes b,v\otimes c)
 =\left(\sum_{i=1}^4u_i^2v_i\right)
   C_{\rm cell}(a,b,c)
\]
for $u,v\in W_0$ and $a,b,c\in\R^2$.  For the vector
\eqref{eq:v22-balanced-u}, one has $u_i^2=1/4$ for every $i$.  Hence, for
all $v\in W_0$,
\[
 \sum_i u_i^2v_i=\frac14\sum_i v_i=0.
\]
Therefore
\[
 C(X,X,Z)=C(X,Y,Z)=C(Y,Y,Z)=0
\]
for every $Z\in W_0\otimes\R^2$.  Apply
\Cref{lem:v22-hessian-curvature}.  Orthogonality and unit norm follow from the
product Fisher normalization and $\|u\|=1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[An exact flat complex line in the V21 Store family]
\label{cor:v22-store-flat-complex-line}
For the V21 Store family take
$a=e_x$, $b=e_y$ in the normalized future-null score plane
$\Span\{\zeta,\epsilon\}$.  Since the Store complex structure satisfies
$J_{\rm ren}e_x=e_y$, the plane
\[
 \boxed{
 \Span_{\R}\{u\otimes e_x,u\otimes e_y\}}
 \label{eq:v22-store-hol-plane}
\]
is a $J_{\rm ren}$-complex line with
\[
 \boxed{K_{\rm Store}=0}
\]
at the reference law.
\end{corollary}

\section{The arithmetic theta-source germ has strictly positive Fubini--Study curvature}
\label{sec:v22-arithmetic-curvature}

V12 proves that, in the fixed theta marking, the marked theta-source map is a
local biholomorphism from the genus-two moduli germ to an open subset of
$\mathbb{CP}^3$, and that the arithmetic source metric is the pullback of the
standard Fubini--Study metric.  We record the curvature normalization used by
that metric.

\begin{lemma}[Fubini--Study real sectional curvature in the V12 normalization]
\label{lem:v22-fs-curvature}
Let $g_{\rm FS}$ be the Fubini--Study metric whose affine Hermitian matrix is
\[
 g_{i\bar j}
 =\frac{(1+\|z\|^2)\delta_{ij}-\bar z_i z_j}
        {(1+\|z\|^2)^2}.
\]
For orthonormal real tangent vectors $X,Y$ one has
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 K_{\rm FS}(X,Y)
 =1+3\,\langle JX,Y\rangle^2.}
 \label{eq:v22-fs-sectional}
\end{equation}
Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{1\le K_{\rm FS}\le4,}
 \label{eq:v22-fs-window}
\end{equation}
and every holomorphic real two-plane $\Span\{X,JX\}$ has curvature four.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
At the affine origin the K\"ahler potential is
$\log(1+\|z\|^2)$.  Direct differentiation gives
\[
 R_{i\bar j k\bar l}
 =\delta_{ij}\delta_{kl}+\delta_{il}\delta_{kj}.
\]
The unitary group acts transitively on projective space and preserves the
metric, so this formula determines the curvature at every point.  Passing from
the complex tensor to the real tangent space gives
\eqref{eq:v22-fs-sectional}.  The final statements follow from
$|\langle JX,Y\rangle|\le1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Curvature obstruction to the canonical V21 nonlinear duality]
\label{thm:v22-curvature-obstruction}
Let $\mathcal M_{\rm ar}$ be the marked arithmetic theta-source germ with the
V12 source metric, and let $\mathcal M_{\rm Store}^{\rm can}$ be the canonical
six-real-parameter Store exponential family of V21 with its Fisher metric.
There is no local Riemannian isometry between neighborhoods of their reference
points.  In particular, no smooth reparameterization, no tangent-space
whitening, and no choice of the V21 binary complex orientation can turn the
canonical product Store family into the complete nonlinear arithmetic
source germ.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The arithmetic source map is a local diffeomorphism onto an open subset of
$\mathbb{CP}^3$, so every real sectional curvature of
$\mathcal M_{\rm ar}$ lies in $[1,4]$ by
\Cref{lem:v22-fs-curvature}.  By
\Cref{cor:v22-store-flat-complex-line}, the canonical Store family has an
exact zero-curvature plane at its reference point.  Sectional curvature is
preserved by local Riemannian isometries, giving the contradiction.  The
argument is intrinsic and therefore survives coordinate changes, tangent
whitening, and the replacement $J_{\rm ren}\mapsto-J_{\rm ren}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[First-order source matching remains possible]
\label{cor:v22-first-order-still-open}
The obstruction in \Cref{thm:v22-curvature-obstruction} begins strictly beyond
first order.  At one point the Store Fisher metric is positive definite and the
arithmetic Fubini--Study metric is positive definite, so a linear source
isometry between the two tangent spaces always exists after normalization.
Thus V14--V21's first-order source, complex-structure, and real-structure gates
remain meaningful.  What fails is promotion of the particular V21 independent-
cell exponential family to an exact local nonlinear arithmetic dual.
\end{corollary}

\begin{remark}[Do not fit away intrinsic curvature]
\label{fire:v22-no-curvature-fitting}
A nonlinear parameter change can alter coordinate expressions of the Fisher
metric but cannot alter its Riemann curvature tensor.  Therefore the zero-versus-
positive curvature obstruction cannot be removed by relabeling the six Store
parameters after inspecting the arithmetic target.  Repairing the nonlinear
comparison requires additional physical law data, not a coordinate choice.
\end{remark}

\section{Second-order Hellinger geometry and the connected-occurrence budget}
\label{sec:v22-second-order}

The preceding obstruction identifies the grade at which new Store information
must enter.  The Hellinger map
\[
 \mathfrak h(p)=2\sqrt p
\]
places every normalized positive law on the sphere of radius two in its
ambient real $L^2$ space.  Hence the ambient sphere itself has sectional
curvature $1/4$.

Let $p(\theta)$ be a $C^2$ six-parameter physical Store family with
$p(0)=p_0$.  Put
\[
 H(\theta)=\mathfrak h(p(\theta)),
 \qquad \nu_0=H(0)/2.
\]
Let $P_T$ be the orthogonal projection onto the six-dimensional tangent range
of $DH_0$, and define the sphere-normal projector
\[
 Q_S=I-P_T-|\nu_0\rangle\langle\nu_0|.
\]

\begin{definition}[Hellinger second fundamental form]
\label{def:v22-second-form}
For tangent vectors $u,v$, define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathrm{II}_{\rm Hel}(u,v)
 :=Q_S\,D^2H_0[u,v].}
 \label{eq:v22-II}
\end{equation}
This is the second fundamental form of the Store law manifold inside the
Hellinger sphere.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Gauss curvature budget for an arithmetic source realization]
\label{thm:v22-gauss-budget}
Let $X,Y$ be Fisher-orthonormal tangent vectors of a Store law family.  Its
sectional curvature satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 K_{\rm Store}(X,Y)
 =\frac14
 +\langle\mathrm{II}_{\rm Hel}(X,X),
           \mathrm{II}_{\rm Hel}(Y,Y)\rangle
 -\|\mathrm{II}_{\rm Hel}(X,Y)\|^2.}
 \label{eq:v22-gauss}
\end{equation}
If a local source isometry identifies the Store family with the arithmetic
Fubini--Study germ, then necessarily
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \langle\mathrm{II}(X,X),\mathrm{II}(Y,Y)\rangle
 -\|\mathrm{II}(X,Y)\|^2
 =\frac34+3\langle JX,Y\rangle^2.}
 \label{eq:v22-extrinsic-budget}
\end{equation}
In particular every holomorphic plane must satisfy the exact extrinsic budget
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \langle\mathrm{II}(X,X),\mathrm{II}(JX,JX)\rangle
 -\|\mathrm{II}(X,JX)\|^2
 =\frac{15}{4}.}
 \label{eq:v22-hol-budget}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Hellinger image lies on the sphere of radius two.  The Gauss equation for a
submanifold of a sphere of sectional curvature $1/4$ gives
\eqref{eq:v22-gauss}.  If the induced metric is locally isometric to the
arithmetic source metric, substitute the Fubini--Study curvature
\eqref{eq:v22-fs-sectional} and rearrange.  For a holomorphic plane,
$Y=JX$ and $\langle JX,Y\rangle=1$.
\end{proof}

For the balanced complex line of \Cref{cor:v22-store-flat-complex-line}, the
canonical V21 family has $K=0$.  Hence its extrinsic expression in
\eqref{eq:v22-gauss} equals $-1/4$, whereas the arithmetic target requires
$15/4$.  The exact curvature deficit is therefore
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{4.}
 \label{eq:v22-curvature-deficit}
\end{equation}
This is not a small conditioning error.

\section{A finite second-order occurrence test}
\label{sec:v22-finite-second-order}

The second fundamental form can be approached without assuming derivatives.
This is the same order-of-operations principle as the inherited physical subset
secant theorem: actual intervention cubes carry finite Hellinger interaction
secants before a shrinking-family limit is taken~\cite{GT77}.

Assume six first-neighbour Store laws $p_{he_a}$ have been acquired as in V20,
and let $P_{T,h}$ be the tangent projector obtained after first removing the
radial line $\R H_0$ from their Hellinger secants.  For two declared tangent
directions $u,v$, acquire in addition the laws at $2hu$, $2hv$, and
$h(u+v)$.  Define
\begin{align}
 D^{(2)}_h(u,u)
 &:=\frac{H(2hu)-2H(hu)+H(0)}{h^2},\notag\\
 D^{(2)}_h(v,v)
 &:=\frac{H(2hv)-2H(hv)+H(0)}{h^2},\notag\\
 D^{(2)}_h(u,v)
 &:=\frac{H(h(u+v))-H(hu)-H(hv)+H(0)}{h^2}.
 \label{eq:v22-finite-second-diff}
\end{align}
Let
\[
 Q_{S,h}=I-P_{T,h}-|\nu_0\rangle\langle\nu_0|
\]
and put
\[
 \mathrm{II}_h(a,b)=Q_{S,h}D^{(2)}_h(a,b).
\]

\begin{theorem}[Finite Hellinger curvature audit]
\label{thm:v22-finite-curvature-audit}
Suppose the physical law family is $C^2$, its first Hellinger derivative has
rank six, and the acquired finite laws above belong to that same family.  Then
as $h\to0$,
\[
 \mathrm{II}_h(a,b)\longrightarrow
 \mathrm{II}_{\rm Hel}(a,b)
\]
for $a,b\in\{u,v\}$.  Consequently the finite scalar
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal K_h(u,v)
 :=\frac14
 +\langle\mathrm{II}_h(u,u),\mathrm{II}_h(v,v)\rangle
 -\|\mathrm{II}_h(u,v)\|^2}
 \label{eq:v22-finite-curvature}
\end{equation}
converges to the physical sectional curvature of the limiting Fisher metric.
For a proposed arithmetic holomorphic-plane comparison the target value is
exactly four.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The three second differences in \eqref{eq:v22-finite-second-diff} converge to
$D^2H_0[u,u]$, $D^2H_0[v,v]$, and $D^2H_0[u,v]$ by the two-variable
fundamental theorem of calculus.  Full first-order rank implies convergence of
the finite tangent projectors $P_{T,h}$ to $P_T$.  Hence $Q_{S,h}\to Q_S$ and
the projected second differences converge to
\eqref{eq:v22-II}.  Apply \Cref{thm:v22-gauss-budget}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Ten-law local curvature card]
\label{cor:v22-ten-law-card}
Fix a real basis $e_1,\ldots,e_6$ of the Store tangent and choose one test plane
$u,v$ among their declared linear combinations.  The first-order tangent
projector uses the reference law and the six one-step neighbours.  Adding only
the three laws at $2hu$, $2hv$, and $h(u+v)$ is sufficient to evaluate
\eqref{eq:v22-finite-curvature}.  Thus one reference law plus nine neighbouring
laws gives a complete finite card for one sectional-curvature target.  No
smooth interpolation needs to be fitted before the card is acquired.
\end{corollary}

\section{Why a connected Store occurrence is now the natural upstream target}
\label{sec:v22-connected-target}

The V21 family is a product of four independently deformed one-cell laws.  The
flat-plane theorem shows that this independence structure removes precisely the
second-order geometry required by the arithmetic source.  The Grand-Tensor
connected-source calculus already distinguishes the product-connected tensor
from the nonmonoidal occurrence innovation, and its physical subset-secants
theorem reconstructs finite Hellinger interaction terms from actual
intervention cubes before a tangent is taken~\cite{GT77}.

\begin{proposition}[Product-family repair requires genuinely new second-order data]
\label{prop:v22-product-repair}
Keep the V21 one-cell marginal deformation laws and their first-order
future-null score source fixed.  Any four-cell deformation whose Hellinger
second-order card agrees with the independent product family on all mixed
second differences has the same zero curvature on the balanced plane
\eqref{eq:v22-store-hol-plane}.  Therefore any realization of the arithmetic
curvature on that plane must alter at least one second-order mixed Hellinger
panel beyond the V21 independent-product value.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The tangent metric is fixed by the common first-order source.  The Gauss
formula \eqref{eq:v22-gauss} depends at the reference point only on that metric
and the sphere-normal second derivatives.  If all relevant mixed second
Hellinger panels agree with the product family, then the projected second
fundamental-form entries agree and the curvature remains the product value
zero.  Since the arithmetic target is four on the corresponding holomorphic
plane, at least one second-order panel must differ.
\end{proof}

\begin{scope}[Connected occurrence is a candidate repair, not yet a theorem of occurrence]
The mature Grand-Tensor calculus provides a canonical location for the missing
second-order information: after proper-subset shorting, an actual intervention
cube splits into a product-connected component and a nonmonoidal occurrence
innovation.  V22 proves that the independent product chart is insufficient and
that some second-order Hellinger data must change.  It does not prove that the
required correction is already populated by the historical Store, nor that a
particular pair-, triple-, or four-body interaction is selected.  Those are
next occurrence tests.
\end{scope}

\section{V22 status and next attack}
\label{sec:v22-status}

The canonical Store source of V21 survives as a first-order result but fails as
a complete nonlinear arithmetic dual:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{array}{c}
 \text{arithmetic theta-source germ}\\[-0.1em]
 K_{\rm real}\in[1,4],\quad K_{\rm hol}=4
 \end{array}
 \qquad\not\simeq_{\rm local}\qquad
 \begin{array}{c}
 \text{V21 product Store germ}\\[-0.1em]
 K_{\rm balanced}=0.
 \end{array}}
 \label{eq:v22-final-obstruction}
\end{equation}
The obstruction is intrinsic and cannot be repaired by coordinate fitting.
The nonlinear programme therefore moves one grade upstream, from first-order
scores to actual second-order occurrence.

The next noncircular attack is:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(N\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item retain the V21 future-null score family as the fixed first-order Store
source;
\item populate one actual two-parameter intervention square, or the equivalent
pair-connected writer, whose balanced tetrahedral mode probes
\eqref{eq:v22-store-hol-plane};
\item evaluate the finite second-order card
\eqref{eq:v22-finite-curvature} before fitting any continuum connection;
\item compare its shrinking limit with the arithmetic target value four and,
more strongly, with the full Fubini--Study curvature tensor;
\item only after the real second-order geometry passes, reopen the V21
complex/real-descent residual and then transfer/Krylov comparison.
\end{enumerate}

A zero Store curvature on the balanced plane is now an exact nonlinear
obstruction to the canonical product completion, not evidence against the
first-order source correspondence.  A nonzero connected occurrence is not by
itself a success: its sign and magnitude must satisfy the explicit Gauss budget
\eqref{eq:v22-extrinsic-budget}.  This keeps source occurrence, nonlinear
geometry, and later transport as separate gates.

\paragraph{Version integrity.}
All V1--V21 mathematical bodies and historical status ledgers are preserved
byte for byte.  V22 adds only the Hessian-curvature identity, the universal
balanced flat-plane theorem, the Fubini--Study curvature comparison, the
nonlinear no-go for the V21 product family, and the finite second-order
Hellinger curvature audit above.  Future continuations must follow this block.

\section{V23: Pair-connected completion of the arithmetic curvature source}
\label{sec:v23-context}

\paragraph{Context and nonduplication.}
V22 isolated the first nonlinear obstruction: the target-independent V21
independent-cell Store family has a balanced holomorphic plane of zero
sectional curvature, whereas the marked arithmetic theta-source germ has
Fubini--Study holomorphic sectional curvature four.  The Grand-Tensor monograph
already contains the general pair-connected/Hoeffding source calculus and, for
two primitive cells, a complete nine-dimensional connected score carrier after
one-cell shorting~\cite{GT77}.  The purpose of V23 is not to reprove those
results.  Instead we answer the next more specific question:

\begin{quote}
What second-order source is required by the arithmetic Fubini--Study germ, and
can the already selected complex Store score of V21 support that source using
pair interactions alone?
\end{quote}

The answer is sharp at one fibre.  The arithmetic quadratic normal source has
real rank nine.  It is canonically a Hermitian endomorphism carrier.  The V21
complex Store score generates a target-independent twelve-real-dimensional
pair-edge score bank; a tetrahedral compression has a three-dimensional
phase-gradient kernel and a nine-dimensional quotient carrying exactly the
same representation types.  No triple- or four-cell coefficient space is
needed for \emph{capacity} at the quadratic source level.  Actual historical
occurrence and equality of the measured second-order Gram remain independent
gates.

Throughout, let
\[
 W=\{z\in\C^4:\mathbf 1^*z=0\}\cong\C^3
\]
be the complexified tetrahedral standard module, with Hermitian product
$\langle x,y\rangle=x^*y$, real metric
$g(x,y)=\Re\langle x,y\rangle$, and complex structure $Jx=ix$.
We normalize $g$ so that the arithmetic Fubini--Study sectional curvature is
\[
 K_{\rm FS}(X,Y)=1+3g(JX,Y)^2
\]
for real orthonormal $X,Y$, as in V22.

\section{The rank-nine Fubini--Study quadratic source}
\label{sec:v23-fs-normal}

Let $\operatorname{Herm}(W)$ be the real Hilbert space of Hermitian endomorphisms of $W$,
with
\[
 \langle A,B\rangle_{\HS}=\Tr(AB).
\]
Put
\begin{equation}
 c=\frac1{\sqrt2},
 \qquad
 d=\frac{\sqrt{29}-2\sqrt2}{6}.
 \label{eq:v23-cd}
\end{equation}
For real tangent vectors $X,Y\in W_{\R}$ define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal B_{\rm FS}(X,Y)
 =c\,(XY^*+YX^*)+d\,g(X,Y)I_W.}
 \label{eq:v23-BFS}
\end{equation}
This is symmetric and real bilinear.

\begin{theorem}[Exact Fubini--Study Gauss normal]
\label{thm:v23-fs-gauss-normal}
For every real orthonormal $X,Y\in W_{\R}$, putting
$t=g(JX,Y)$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac14
 +\langle\mathcal B_{\rm FS}(X,X),
          \mathcal B_{\rm FS}(Y,Y)\rangle_{\HS}
 -\|\mathcal B_{\rm FS}(X,Y)\|_{\HS}^2
 =1+3t^2.}
 \label{eq:v23-fs-gauss}
\end{equation}
Moreover the real span of the values of $\mathcal B_{\rm FS}$ is all of
$\operatorname{Herm}(W)$, hence has dimension nine.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $\alpha=\langle X,Y\rangle$.  Since $X,Y$ are real-orthonormal for
$g$, one has $\Re\alpha=0$ and $|\alpha|^2=t^2$.  Put
$S(X,Y)=XY^*+YX^*$.  Direct Hilbert--Schmidt multiplication gives
\[
 \Tr(S(X,X)S(Y,Y))=4t^2,
 \qquad
 \|S(X,Y)\|_{\HS}^2=2-2t^2,
\]
and
\[
 \Tr S(X,X)=\Tr S(Y,Y)=2.
\]
Therefore the extrinsic part of the left side of
\eqref{eq:v23-fs-gauss} is
\[
 c^2(6t^2-2)+4cd+3d^2.
\]
The constants in \eqref{eq:v23-cd} satisfy
\[
 6c^2=3,
 \qquad
 -2c^2+4cd+3d^2=\frac34,
\]
so the displayed expression is $3t^2+3/4$.  Adding the ambient sphere
curvature $1/4$ proves \eqref{eq:v23-fs-gauss}.

For spanning, choose a unitary basis $e_1,e_2,e_3$ of $W$.  For $i\ne j$,
$\mathcal B(e_i,e_j)$ and $\mathcal B(e_i,Je_j)$ span respectively the real
symmetric and imaginary-skew Hermitian off-diagonal matrix units.  Differences
$\mathcal B(e_i,e_i)-\mathcal B(e_j,e_j)$ span the traceless diagonal
subspace.  Finally
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^3\mathcal B(e_i,e_i)
 =(2c+3d)I_W=\frac{\sqrt{29}}2I_W\ne0.
\]
Thus all of $\operatorname{Herm}(W)$ is spanned.
\end{proof}

The preceding formula has an especially simple source Gram.

\begin{proposition}[Closed quadratic Gram formula]
\label{prop:v23-fs-quadratic-gram}
For arbitrary $X,Y,Z,T\in W_{\R}$,
\begin{equation}
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
&\langle\mathcal B_{\rm FS}(X,Y),
          \mathcal B_{\rm FS}(Z,T)\rangle_{\HS}\\
&\quad=
 \Re\!\left(
 \langle Y,Z\rangle\langle T,X\rangle
 +\langle Y,T\rangle\langle Z,X\rangle
 \right)
 +\frac74\,g(X,Y)g(Z,T).
\end{aligned}}
\label{eq:v23-fs-quadratic-gram}
\end{equation}
Thus the complete arithmetic second-order source Gram is determined by the
first-order Hermitian metric; no period or theta constant enters at this stage.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For $S(X,Y)=XY^*+YX^*$,
\[
 \Tr(S(X,Y)S(Z,T))
 =2\Re\!\left(
 \langle Y,Z\rangle\langle T,X\rangle
 +\langle Y,T\rangle\langle Z,X\rangle
 \right).
\]
Also $\Tr S(X,Y)=2g(X,Y)$.  Substitution in
\eqref{eq:v23-BFS}, followed by $c^2=1/2$ and
$4cd+3d^2=7/4$, gives \eqref{eq:v23-fs-quadratic-gram}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{K\"ahler quotient and exact rank}

Let $\operatorname{Sym}^2_{\R}(W_{\R})$ carry its standard Hilbert metric, so
$X\odot Y=(X\otimes Y+Y\otimes X)/\sqrt2$ for $X\perp Y$.  Let
$\widetilde{\mathcal B}_{\rm FS}$ be the linear map induced by
$\mathcal B_{\rm FS}$, with the corresponding $\sqrt2$ factor on off-diagonal
orthonormal tensors.  Define the involution
\[
 \mathscr J_2(X\odot Y)=JX\odot JY.
\]

\begin{theorem}[K\"ahler quadratic quotient and exact spectrum]
\label{thm:v23-kahler-quadratic}
The map $\widetilde{\mathcal B}_{\rm FS}$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \widetilde{\mathcal B}_{\rm FS}\mathscr J_2
 =\widetilde{\mathcal B}_{\rm FS}.}
 \label{eq:v23-J2-even}
\end{equation}
Its kernel is exactly the $(-1)$-eigenspace of $\mathscr J_2$, of real
dimension twelve.  The $(+1)$-eigenspace has dimension nine and is carried
isomorphically onto $\operatorname{Herm}(W)$.  Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
ank\widetilde{\mathcal B}_{\rm FS}=9.}
 \label{eq:v23-B-rank}
\end{equation}
With the canonical symmetric-tensor metric,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{spec}
 (\widetilde{\mathcal B}_{\rm FS}^*
  \widetilde{\mathcal B}_{\rm FS})
 =\left\{
 \frac{29}{2}^{[1]},\;4^{[8]},\;0^{[12]}
 \right\}.}
 \label{eq:v23-B-spectrum}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
From \eqref{eq:v23-BFS},
\[
 \mathcal B(JX,JY)=\mathcal B(X,Y),
 \qquad
 \mathcal B(JX,Y)+\mathcal B(X,JY)=0.
\]
Thus the $(-1)$-eigenspace of $\mathscr J_2$ lies in the kernel.  For a
complex three-space, the $J$-invariant real symmetric tensors are naturally
Hermitian forms and have real dimension $3^2=9$; hence the anti-invariant
space has dimension $21-9=12$.  By
\Cref{thm:v23-fs-gauss-normal} the image has dimension nine, so the kernel is
exactly the anti-invariant space and the restriction to the invariant space is
an isomorphism.

The map is $U(3)$-equivariant.  The $J$-invariant symmetric-tensor space
splits into the scalar metric line and the eight-dimensional traceless
Hermitian subspace.  Schur's lemma makes
$\widetilde{\mathcal B}^*\widetilde{\mathcal B}$ scalar on each.
For a unitary basis $e_1,e_2,e_3$, the normalized scalar tensor is
\[
 q_0=\frac1{\sqrt6}
 \sum_{i=1}^3(e_i\odot e_i+Je_i\odot Je_i).
\]
Using $2c+3d=\sqrt{29}/2$ gives
\[
 \|\widetilde{\mathcal B}(q_0)\|_{\HS}^2=\frac{29}{2}.
\]
For the normalized traceless tensor
\[
 q_1=\frac12\bigl(
 e_1\odot e_1+Je_1\odot Je_1
 -e_2\odot e_2-Je_2\odot Je_2
 \bigr),
\]
one obtains
$\|\widetilde{\mathcal B}(q_1)\|_{\HS}^2=4$.
This proves \eqref{eq:v23-B-spectrum}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Tetrahedral representation content}

The $S_4$ action on $W$ is the complexification of the real standard module
$[31]$.  Since the matrices are real in that marking,
\[
 \operatorname{Herm}(W)\cong\operatorname{Sym}^2W_0\oplus i\Lambda^2W_0
\]
as real $S_4$ modules.

\begin{proposition}[Multiplicity-free tetrahedral normal type]
\label{prop:v23-normal-S4}
One has
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{Herm}(W)
 \cong[4]\oplus[31]\oplus[22]\oplus[211].}
 \label{eq:v23-normal-S4}
\end{equation}
The scalar line is $[4]$; the remaining eight-dimensional traceless sector is
$[31]\oplus[22]\oplus[211]$.  Therefore the arithmetic quadratic Gram
\eqref{eq:v23-B-spectrum} has the isotypic weights
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \gamma_{[4]}=\frac{29}{2},
 \qquad
 \gamma_{[31]}=\gamma_{[22]}=\gamma_{[211]}=4.}
 \label{eq:v23-target-weights}
\end{equation}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The standard character on the conjugacy classes
$1,(12),(12)(34),(123),(1234)$ is
$(3,1,-1,0,-1)$.  The standard formulas
\[
 \chi_{\operatorname{Sym}^2}(g)=\frac{\chi(g)^2+\chi(g^2)}2,
 \qquad
 \chi_{\Lambda^2}(g)=\frac{\chi(g)^2-\chi(g^2)}2
\]
give respectively
\[
 \operatorname{Sym}^2[31]=[4]\oplus[31]\oplus[22],
 \qquad
 \Lambda^2[31]=[211].
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:v23-normal-S4}.  The weight statement is
\Cref{thm:v23-kahler-quadratic}, with the scalar line separated from the
traceless sector.
\end{proof}

\section{A target-independent pair-connected Store edge bank}
\label{sec:v23-store-pair-bank}

Retain the V21 proper complex one-cell scores $w_i$, $i=1,2,3,4$, on four
independent primitive cells:
\[
 \mathbb Ew_i=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E|w_i|^2=1,
 \qquad
 \mathbb Ew_i^2=0.
\]
Let
\[
 \mathcal E_{\rm off}
 =\{M\in\operatorname{Herm}_4(\C):M_{ii}=0\},
 \qquad \dim_{\R}\mathcal E_{\rm off}=12.
\]
For $M\in\mathcal E_{\rm off}$ define the real pair score
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 q_M=w^*Mw
 =\sum_{i\ne j}\overline{w_i}M_{ij}w_j.}
 \label{eq:v23-qM}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical pair-connected edge isometry]
\label{thm:v23-edge-isometry}
The score $q_M$ is real, centered, and orthogonal to every one-cell function.
Moreover, for $M,N\in\mathcal E_{\rm off}$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathbb E[q_Mq_N]=\Tr(MN).}
 \label{eq:v23-edge-gram}
\end{equation}
Hence
\[
 M\longmapsto q_M
\]
is an isometry from the twelve-real-dimensional Hilbert--Schmidt edge space
onto a target-independent pair-connected Store score bank.  Every direction is
supported on cell pairs; no triple- or four-cell score is used.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Hermiticity of $M$ makes $w^*Mw$ real.  Since $M$ has zero diagonal and the
cells are independent and centered, every term has zero mean.  Conditioning
on any one cell still leaves at least one independent centered factor in every
term, so the conditional mean is zero and $q_M$ is orthogonal to all one-cell
functions.

Expand
\[
 \mathbb E[q_Mq_N]
 =\sum_{i\ne j}\sum_{k\ne l}
 M_{ij}N_{kl}
 \mathbb E[\overline w_iw_j\overline w_kw_l].
\]
Independence, $\mathbb Ew_i=0$, $\mathbb Ew_i^2=0$, and
$\mathbb E|w_i|^2=1$ leave only $i=l$, $j=k$.  Thus the sum is
$\sum_{i\ne j}M_{ij}N_{ji}=\Tr(MN)$.
\end{proof}

The bank \eqref{eq:v23-qM} is selected solely by the V21 Store complex score
and tetrahedral cell labels.  It is not fitted to the arithmetic curvature.
It is an executable conditional-exponential tangent bank, but historical
occurrence of a particular connected deformation remains a separate row.

\section{The tetrahedral edge quotient and its three-dimensional gauge kernel}
\label{sec:v23-edge-quotient}

Let
\[
 P=I_4-\frac14\mathbf1\mathbf1^*
\]
be the orthogonal projection onto $W$.  Define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Phi:\mathcal E_{\rm off}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Herm}(W),
 \qquad
 \Phi(M)=(PMP)|_W.}
 \label{eq:v23-Phi}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Exact edge quotient]
\label{thm:v23-edge-quotient}
The map $\Phi$ is $S_4$-equivariant and surjective.  Its kernel is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \ker\Phi
 =\left\{
 \frac{i}{2}(r\mathbf1^T-\mathbf1r^T):
 r\in\R^4,\ \mathbf1^Tr=0
 \right\}.}
 \label{eq:v23-Phi-kernel}
\end{equation}
Hence
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal E_{\rm off}/\ker\Phi
 \cong\operatorname{Herm}(W),
 \qquad
 12-3=9.}
 \label{eq:v23-edge-nine}
\end{equation}
The kernel is one real standard $[31]$ module and consists of edge phase
gradients $i(r_i-r_j)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Equivariance follows because $P$ commutes with coordinate permutations.  To
identify the kernel, decompose
$\C^4=\C\mathbf1\oplus W$.  If $PMP=0$, then in this decomposition a Hermitian
$M$ has only the scalar--standard off-diagonal block and a scalar entry on the
trivial line.  Writing the off-diagonal block as $b\in W$, the zero-diagonal
condition in the original coordinate basis forces the scalar entry to vanish
and $\Re b=0$.  Thus $b=ir/2$ for a real centered vector $r$, giving exactly
\eqref{eq:v23-Phi-kernel}.  Conversely every displayed matrix has
$PMP=0$.  The kernel has dimension three, so the image has dimension
$12-3=9=\dim_{\R}\operatorname{Herm}(W)$ and is therefore all of $\operatorname{Herm}(W)$.  Permuting the
coordinates permutes $r$, so the kernel is the standard module.
\end{proof}

The quotient map has a useful exact singular-value structure.

\begin{proposition}[Isotypic singular values of the edge quotient]
\label{prop:v23-Phi-spectrum}
Equip $\mathcal E_{\rm off}$ and $\operatorname{Herm}(W)$ with Hilbert--Schmidt metrics and
restrict $\Phi$ to $(\ker\Phi)^\perp$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Phi\Phi^*
 =\frac14P_{[4]}
 +\frac12P_{[31]}
 +P_{[22]}+P_{[211]}.}
 \label{eq:v23-Phi-spectrum}
\end{equation}
Equivalently, the squared singular values are
\[
 \boxed{\frac14^{[1]},\ \frac12^{[3]},\ 1^{[2]},\ 1^{[3]}.}
\]
Therefore the minimum-Hilbert--Schmidt right inverse $\Phi^\dagger$ has
squared amplification factors
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{4,\ 2,\ 1,\ 1}
 \label{eq:v23-Phi-inverse-weights}
\end{equation}
on $[4],[31],[22],[211]$ respectively.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
By $S_4$ equivariance and the multiplicity-free decomposition
\eqref{eq:v23-normal-S4}, $\Phi\Phi^*$ is scalar on each isotype.  Evaluate it
on: the identity endomorphism for $[4]$; a diagonal traceless standard vector
for $[31]$; a diagonal/off-diagonal vector in the two-dimensional $[22]$
space; and an imaginary skew-Hermitian basis vector for $[211]$.  Direct
sandwiching by $P$ gives the four scalars $1/4,1/2,1,1$.  The Moore--Penrose
right inverse has the reciprocal squared singular values.
\end{proof}

\section{The exact arithmetic pair-writer target}
\label{sec:v23-pair-target}

The edge bank is target independent.  The arithmetic Fubini--Study source now
selects a precise nine-dimensional pattern inside it.  Define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal Q_{\rm FS}
 :=\Phi^\dagger\widetilde{\mathcal B}_{\rm FS}:
 \operatorname{Sym}^2_{\R}(W_{\R})	o\mathcal E_{\rm off}.}
 \label{eq:v23-QFS}
\end{equation}
This is the minimum-edge-norm coefficient lift of the arithmetic quadratic
normal source.  It is a comparison target, not a claim that the historical
Store selects these coefficients.

\begin{theorem}[Four exact pair-writer weights]
\label{thm:v23-pair-writer-weights}
The map $\mathcal Q_{\rm FS}$ has the same twelve-dimensional K\"ahler kernel
as $\widetilde{\mathcal B}_{\rm FS}$.  On the nine-dimensional invariant
quotient its coefficient Gram is multiplicity free with exact weights
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Gamma_{[4]}=58,
 \qquad
 \Gamma_{[31]}=8,
 \qquad
 \Gamma_{[22]}=4,
 \qquad
 \Gamma_{[211]}=4.}
 \label{eq:v23-edge-target-weights}
\end{equation}
In particular
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
ank(\mathcal Q_{\rm FS})=9.}
 \label{eq:v23-QFS-rank}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Moore--Penrose lift is injective on the image of
$\widetilde{\mathcal B}_{\rm FS}$, so the kernel and rank are unchanged.
Both factors are $S_4$ equivariant.  Multiply the target normal weights
\eqref{eq:v23-target-weights} by the squared amplification factors
\eqref{eq:v23-Phi-inverse-weights}.  This gives
$(29/2)\cdot4=58$, $4\cdot2=8$, and $4\cdot1=4$ on the remaining two
isotypes.
\end{proof}

The theorem turns the V22 qualitative statement ``some pair-connected data
must change'' into an exact coefficient-level target.  Under exact common
$S_4$ covariance, a candidate minimum-norm pair writer can be tested by four
isotypic energies rather than an unrestricted matrix comparison.

\section{A strong finite quadratic-source duality gate}
\label{sec:v23-strong-gate}

Let $\mathrm{II}_{\rm St}$ be the sphere-normal second Hellinger source map of
an actually acquired Store family after the V20--V21 first-order source has
been identified with $W_{\R}$.  Regard it as a linear map on
$\operatorname{Sym}^2_{\R}(W_{\R})$ and put
\[
 G_{\rm St}^{(2)}=\mathrm{II}_{\rm St}^*\mathrm{II}_{\rm St}.
\]
Let $P_\pm=(I\pm\mathscr J_2)/2$.

\begin{theorem}[Strong quadratic-source recognition]
\label{thm:v23-strong-quadratic-gate}
Assume the Store second-order packet is exactly $S_4$ covariant and complex
compatible, so $G_{\rm St}^{(2)}$ commutes with $S_4$ and $\mathscr J_2$.
On the $P_+$ sector let $P_\lambda$ be the four central isotypic projectors for
$\lambda=[4],[31],[22],[211]$, and define
\[
 \gamma_\lambda
 =\frac1{\dim\lambda}\Tr(P_\lambda G_{\rm St}^{(2)}).
\]
Then the nonnegative scalar
\begin{equation}
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
 \Delta_{\rm FS}^{(2)}
 :={}&\|\mathrm{II}_{\rm St}P_-\|_{\HS}^2
 +\left(\gamma_{[4]}-\frac{29}{2}\right)^2\\
 &+(\gamma_{[31]}-4)^2
 +(\gamma_{[22]}-4)^2
 +(\gamma_{[211]}-4)^2
\end{aligned}}
\label{eq:v23-Delta2}
\end{equation}
vanishes if and only if
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 G_{\rm St}^{(2)}
 =\widetilde{\mathcal B}_{\rm FS}^*
  \widetilde{\mathcal B}_{\rm FS}.}
 \label{eq:v23-strong-Gram-equality}
\end{equation}
On that branch there is a unique source-fixing isometry from the arithmetic
nine-dimensional normal carrier onto the Store second-order normal range, and
the complete Store sectional-curvature tensor at the reference point equals
the Fubini--Study tensor.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first term in \eqref{eq:v23-Delta2} vanishes exactly when the anti-K\"ahler
quadratic sector is killed.  On the $P_+$ sector, the four irreducible
$S_4$ types occur with multiplicity one by
\Cref{prop:v23-normal-S4}.  Hence an $S_4$-invariant positive Gram is scalar on
each type.  The four remaining terms therefore vanish exactly when those
scalars equal the arithmetic values in
\eqref{eq:v23-target-weights}, proving
\eqref{eq:v23-strong-Gram-equality}.

Equality of source Grams defines the usual source-fixing isometry on the
quotient by the common twelve-dimensional kernel.  The arithmetic source has
rank nine by \Cref{thm:v23-kahler-quadratic}, so this isometry is onto the
Store normal range and unique there.  Finally the Gauss equation depends only
on the tangent metric, ambient sphere curvature, and all inner products of the
second fundamental form.  Those inner products agree by
\eqref{eq:v23-strong-Gram-equality}; hence the complete curvature tensors
agree.  \Cref{thm:v23-fs-gauss-normal} identifies the arithmetic tensor with
Fubini--Study.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Strong Gram equality is sufficient, not logically necessary]
\label{rem:v23-strong-not-necessary}
Different second fundamental forms can have the same Gauss curvature tensor.
Therefore \eqref{eq:v23-strong-Gram-equality} is a deliberately strong source
recognition criterion.  Its advantage is finite identifiability and a unique
normal-source isometry.  Failure of this strong gate does not by itself prove
that every weaker curvature-only comparison fails; V22's direct sectional
curvature card remains the weaker necessary test.
\end{remark}

\section{Capacity theorem and operational scope}
\label{sec:v23-capacity}

The inherited Grand-Tensor theorem gives a nine-dimensional complete connected
carrier for two primitive cells after both one-cell score spaces are shorted,
with positive tensor-product source Gram~\cite{GT77}.  V23 gives a separate
arithmetic statement:
\[
 \rank
 (\widetilde{\mathcal B}_{\rm FS}^*
  \widetilde{\mathcal B}_{\rm FS})=9.
\]
These two facts have a precise but limited consequence.

\begin{corollary}[Exact second-order capacity match]
\label{cor:v23-capacity-match}
The smallest source dimension capable of realizing the \emph{strong}
arithmetic quadratic Gram is nine.  The already available primitive
pair-connected renewal carrier has exactly that dimension.  Hence there is no
dimension obstruction to realizing the strong arithmetic second-order source
inside a pair-connected renewal sector.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Any realization of a positive Gram requires source dimension at least its
rank, which is nine.  The inherited pair-connected source has dimension nine,
so it meets this lower bound exactly.
\end{proof}

\begin{scope}[Capacity is not occurrence]
The dimension match in \Cref{cor:v23-capacity-match} does not identify the
arithmetic normal carrier with the inherited primitive pair carrier.  The
latter comes with its own physical score coordinates and occurrence semantics.
Likewise the target-independent edge bank \eqref{eq:v23-qM} is an executable
score family constructed from V21's complex Store source, but the particular
minimum-norm arithmetic pattern \eqref{eq:v23-QFS} is a comparison target.
Historical duality requires an actual connected Store occurrence whose
second-order Gram passes \eqref{eq:v23-Delta2}, or at least the weaker V22
curvature audit.  No target-fitted pair writer is counted as physical evidence.
\end{scope}

\text{V21 complex Store source }W_0^{\C}\\
\Downarrow\\

The arithmetic target has exact K\"ahler kernel dimension twelve and exact

 \frac{29}{2},4,4,4
\]
on the four tetrahedral normal isotypes.  In the canonical minimum-edge-norm

 58,8,4,4.
\]
Thus the next noncircular finite attack is:

\section{Why the four-weight V23 target collapses to one relative calibration}
\label{sec:v24-context}

V23 identified the complete arithmetic Fubini--Study quadratic source and
showed that, after tetrahedral reduction, its nonzero normal isotypes have
weights
\[
 \frac{29}{2},\ 4,\ 4,\ 4
\]
on $[4],[31],[22],[211]$, while the corresponding minimum-edge-norm writer
has weights $58,8,4,4$.  Those four numbers were presented as a finite strong
source target.  The purpose of V24 is to determine which part of that target
is genuinely new once the V21 complex source itself is retained.

The answer is sharper than a generic four-isotype comparison.  The complex
rank-three source already determines a canonical Hermitian quadratic map whose
nine-dimensional source Gram has weight $4$ on \emph{every} K\"ahler normal
direction.  The arithmetic Fubini--Study map differs from this canonical map
only on the one-dimensional trivial isotype.  Equivalently, all eight
traceless Hermitian normal directions are already fixed by the first-order
complex source; the remaining arithmetic datum is one collective scalar
calibration.

No occurrence statement is inferred from this algebraic reduction.  The
canonical pair map is executable through V23's target-independent pair-score
bank, but historical realization of its normalization remains a physical
connected-panel question.

\section{The universal Hermitian quadratic source}
\label{sec:v24-universal-hermitian}

Retain the notation of V23.  Thus $W\cong\C^3$ has Hermitian product
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$, real metric
$g(X,Y)=\Re\langle X,Y\rangle$, complex structure $JX=iX$, and
$\operatorname{Herm}(W)$ carries the Hilbert--Schmidt metric.  Define the
symmetric real-bilinear map
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal B_0(X,Y)
 :=\frac1{\sqrt2}\bigl(XY^*+YX^*\bigr).}
 \label{eq:v24-B0}
\end{equation}
Let $\widetilde{\mathcal B}_0$ be its induced linear map on
$\operatorname{Sym}_{\R}^2(W_{\R})$, with the same symmetric-tensor
normalization used in V23, and let
\[
 P_+=\frac12(I+\mathscr J_2),\qquad P_-=\frac12(I-\mathscr J_2).
\]

\begin{theorem}[Universal K\"ahler quadratic source]
\label{thm:v24-universal-B0}
The map $\widetilde{\mathcal B}_0$ is $J$-even,
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal B}_0\mathscr J_2
 =\widetilde{\mathcal B}_0,
\]
its kernel is exactly $\operatorname{Ran} P_-$, and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \widetilde{\mathcal B}_0^*\widetilde{\mathcal B}_0
 =4P_+.}
 \label{eq:v24-B0-Gram}
\end{equation}
Hence its rank is nine and every nonzero K\"ahler quadratic direction has the
same source weight $4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The identities
\[
 \mathcal B_0(JX,JY)=\mathcal B_0(X,Y),
 \qquad
 \mathcal B_0(JX,Y)+\mathcal B_0(X,JY)=0
\]
show that $\operatorname{Ran} P_-$ lies in the kernel.  The $J$-even symmetric tensors have
real dimension nine and identify naturally with $\operatorname{Herm}(W)$, so
it suffices to show that the restriction is nonsingular and has constant
squared singular value $4$.

The map is $U(W)$-equivariant.  Under unitary conjugation both the domain
$\operatorname{Ran} P_+$ and the target decompose as a scalar line plus the traceless
Hermitian module.  On the scalar line choose a real orthonormal basis
$f_1,\ldots,f_6$ of $W_{\R}$ and put
\[
 \tau=\frac1{\sqrt6}\sum_{a=1}^6 f_a\odot f_a.
\]
Then $\|\tau\|=1$ and
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal B}_0\tau
 =\frac{2}{\sqrt3}I_W,
 \qquad
 \bigl\|\widetilde{\mathcal B}_0\tau\bigr\|_{\HS}^2=4.
\]
On the traceless module take a unitary basis $e_1,e_2,e_3$ and the unit
$J$-even tensor
\[
 \sigma=\frac12\bigl(
 e_1\odot e_1+Je_1\odot Je_1
 -e_2\odot e_2-Je_2\odot Je_2\bigr).
\]
Direct substitution gives
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal B}_0\sigma
 =\sqrt2\,(E_{11}-E_{22}),
 \qquad
 \bigl\|\widetilde{\mathcal B}_0\sigma\bigr\|_{\HS}^2=4.
\]
The scalar and traceless targets are nonzero.  Equivariance and irreducibility
of the traceless Hermitian adjoint module therefore give squared singular
value $4$ on both summands.  The nine-dimensional restriction is injective,
so the twelve-dimensional anti-K\"ahler subspace is the complete kernel.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Closed universal quadratic Gram]
\label{prop:v24-B0-Gram-formula}
For arbitrary $X,Y,Z,T\in W_{\R}$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 &\langle\mathcal B_0(X,Y),\mathcal B_0(Z,T)\rangle_{\HS}\\
 &\qquad=\Re\!\left(
 \langle Y,Z\rangle\langle T,X\rangle
 +\langle Y,T\rangle\langle Z,X\rangle
 \right).
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:v24-B0-Gram-formula}
\end{equation}
Thus the universal nine-dimensional quadratic Gram is already a deterministic
function of the first-order complex Hermitian source.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Put $S(X,Y)=XY^*+YX^*$.  Cyclicity of the trace gives
\[
 \Tr\bigl(S(X,Y)S(Z,T)\bigr)
 =2\Re\!\left(
 \langle Y,Z\rangle\langle T,X\rangle
 +\langle Y,T\rangle\langle Z,X\rangle
 \right).
\]
The factor $1/\sqrt2$ in each copy of \eqref{eq:v24-B0} cancels the factor two.
\end{proof}

\section{The Fubini--Study correction is purely scalar}
\label{sec:v24-scalar-correction}

Let $\mathcal B_{\rm FS}$ be the arithmetic map of V23,
\[
 \mathcal B_{\rm FS}(X,Y)
 =\mathcal B_0(X,Y)+d\,g(X,Y)I_W,
 \qquad
 d=\frac{\sqrt{29}-2\sqrt2}{6}.
\]
Let
\[
 P_{\rm sc}=|\tau\rangle\langle\tau|,
 \qquad
 P_{\rm tr}=P_+-P_{\rm sc},
 \qquad
 r_{\rm FS}:=\sqrt{\frac{29}{8}}.
\]

\begin{theorem}[One-scalar deformation of the universal quadratic source]
\label{thm:v24-one-scalar-normal}
One has the exact operator identity
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \widetilde{\mathcal B}_{\rm FS}
 =\widetilde{\mathcal B}_0
  \bigl(P_{\rm tr}+r_{\rm FS}P_{\rm sc}\bigr).}
 \label{eq:v24-BFS-B0}
\end{equation}
Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \widetilde{\mathcal B}_{\rm FS}^*
 \widetilde{\mathcal B}_{\rm FS}
 =4P_{\rm tr}+\frac{29}{2}P_{\rm sc},}
 \label{eq:v24-BFS-Gram-decomp}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \widetilde{\mathcal B}_{\rm FS}^*
 \widetilde{\mathcal B}_{\rm FS}
 -\widetilde{\mathcal B}_0^*\widetilde{\mathcal B}_0
 =\frac{21}{2}P_{\rm sc}.}
 \label{eq:v24-normal-rankone-defect}
\end{equation}
Thus the complete Fubini--Study quadratic source differs from the universal
Hermitian quadratic source by one positive rank-one scalar-channel retuning.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For every $X,Y$,
\[
 \Tr\mathcal B_0(X,Y)=\sqrt2\,g(X,Y),
\]
whereas
\[
 \Tr\mathcal B_{\rm FS}(X,Y)
 =(\sqrt2+3d)g(X,Y)
 =\frac{\sqrt{29}}2g(X,Y).
\]
Subtracting one third of the trace shows that the traceless parts are exactly
equal:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal B_{\rm FS}^{\circ}(X,Y)
 =\mathcal B_0^{\circ}(X,Y).}
 \label{eq:v24-traceless-equality}
\end{equation}
The metric contraction $g(X,Y)$ vanishes on the traceless K\"ahler quadratic
sector and on the anti-K\"ahler sector, so the two maps agree there.

On the unit scalar tensor $\tau$,
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal B}_0\tau=\frac2{\sqrt3}I_W,
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal B}_{\rm FS}\tau
 =\sqrt{\frac{29}{6}}I_W.
\]
Their positive amplitude ratio is
\[
 \frac{\sqrt{29/6}}{2/\sqrt3}=\sqrt{\frac{29}{8}}=r_{\rm FS}.
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:v24-BFS-B0}.  Apply
\Cref{thm:v24-universal-B0} to obtain
\eqref{eq:v24-BFS-Gram-decomp}, and subtract $4P_+$ to obtain
\eqref{eq:v24-normal-rankone-defect}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[All anisotropic normal geometry is already universal]
\label{cor:v24-anisotropic-universal}
On the eight-dimensional traceless K\"ahler quadratic sector,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \widetilde{\mathcal B}_{\rm FS}
 =\widetilde{\mathcal B}_0,
 \qquad
 G_{\rm FS}^{(2)}=4I.}
 \label{eq:v24-traceless-universal}
\end{equation}
In particular the $[31]$, $[22]$, and $[211]$ arithmetic normal weights are not
independent arithmetic calibrations; they are fixed by the first-order complex
Hermitian source.  The only additional normal-source magnitude is the trivial
$[4]$ weight $29/2$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The traceless K\"ahler sector is the orthogonal complement of $\tau$ inside
$\operatorname{Ran} P_+$.  Apply \eqref{eq:v24-BFS-B0} and
\Cref{thm:v24-universal-B0}.  Under the $S_4$ decomposition of V23 this sector
is exactly $[31]\oplus[22]\oplus[211]$.
\end{proof}

\section{The corresponding Store edge writer is explicit}
\label{sec:v24-edge-scalar}

Retain V23's target-independent pair bank
$M\mapsto q_M$ on
$\mathcal E_{\rm off}$ and its tetrahedral quotient
$\Phi:\mathcal E_{\rm off}\to\operatorname{Herm}(W)$.  Put
\[
 \mathbf J_4=\mathbf1_4\mathbf1_4^*,
 \qquad
 M_{\rm coll}=I_4-\mathbf J_4.
\]
Since the diagonal of $M_{\rm coll}$ is zero, it belongs to
$\mathcal E_{\rm off}$.

\begin{proposition}[The collective scalar pair writer]
\label{prop:v24-collective-writer}
One has
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Phi(M_{\rm coll})=I_W,
 \qquad
 \Phi^\dagger(I_W)=M_{\rm coll},
 \qquad
 \|M_{\rm coll}\|_{\HS}^2=12.}
 \label{eq:v24-Mcoll}
\end{equation}
The corresponding Store pair score is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 q_{\rm coll}
 :=q_{M_{\rm coll}}
 =\sum_{i=1}^4|w_i|^2
  -\left|\sum_{i=1}^4w_i\right|^2.}
 \label{eq:v24-qcoll}
\end{equation}
It is real, centered, pair-connected, and $S_4$ invariant, with
\[
 \boxed{\mathbb E q_{\rm coll}^2=12.}
\]
Thus the missing scalar normal channel corresponds to one explicit collective
pair observable already present in the target-independent V23 edge bank.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Because $P\mathbf1_4=0$,
\[
 P(I_4-\mathbf J_4)P=P,
\]
which restricts to the identity on $W$.  The trivial isotype in
$\mathcal E_{\rm off}$ is one dimensional and orthogonal to the standard
kernel of $\Phi$, so this preimage is the Moore--Penrose one.  Since
$\mathbf J_4^2=4\mathbf J_4$,
\[
 \|I_4-\mathbf J_4\|_{\HS}^2
 =\Tr(I_4+2\mathbf J_4)=12.
\]
Formula \eqref{eq:v24-qcoll} is $w^*M_{\rm coll}w$.  The remaining statements
follow from V23's pair-score isometry and the permutation invariance of
$M_{\rm coll}$.
\end{proof}

Define the target-independent canonical edge lift
\[
 \mathcal Q_0:=\Phi^\dagger\widetilde{\mathcal B}_0.
\]

\begin{theorem}[One-scalar reduction of the V23 edge target]
\label{thm:v24-edge-one-scalar}
The coefficient Gram of $\mathcal Q_0$ has exact $S_4$ weights
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 16,\quad 8,\quad 4,\quad 4
 }
 \label{eq:v24-Q0-weights}
\end{equation}
on $[4],[31],[22],[211]$.  Moreover
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal Q_{\rm FS}
 =\mathcal Q_0\bigl(P_{\rm tr}+r_{\rm FS}P_{\rm sc}\bigr),}
 \label{eq:v24-QFS-Q0}
\end{equation}
so
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal Q_{\rm FS}^*\mathcal Q_{\rm FS}
 -\mathcal Q_0^*\mathcal Q_0
 =42P_{\rm sc}.}
 \label{eq:v24-edge-rankone-defect}
\end{equation}
On the scalar unit tensor specifically,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal Q_0\tau
 =\frac2{\sqrt3}M_{\rm coll},
 \qquad
 \mathcal Q_{\rm FS}\tau
 =\sqrt{\frac{29}{6}}M_{\rm coll}.}
 \label{eq:v24-scalar-edge-amplitudes}
\end{equation}
Thus the four V23 pair-writer targets $58,8,4,4$ reduce to the canonical
$16,8,4,4$ bank plus one relative scalar rescaling
$r_{\rm FS}=\sqrt{29/8}$ of the explicit collective writer.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
V23 proves that $\Phi^\dagger$ has squared amplification
$4,2,1,1$ on the four normal isotypes.  By
\Cref{thm:v24-universal-B0}, $\widetilde{\mathcal B}_0$ has weight $4$ on
each.  Multiplication gives \eqref{eq:v24-Q0-weights}.
Equation \eqref{eq:v24-QFS-Q0} follows by applying $\Phi^\dagger$ to

$16(29/8)=58$, while every nontrivial weight is unchanged; subtraction gives

\Cref{prop:v24-collective-writer} and the scalar outputs in the proof of

\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[One overall pair coupling cannot reproduce the arithmetic target]
\label{cth:v24-one-coupling-no-go}
There is no scalar $s\ge0$ such that
\[
 \mathcal Q_{\rm FS}^*\mathcal Q_{\rm FS}
 =s^2\mathcal Q_0^*\mathcal Q_0.
\]
Hence an $S_4$-symmetric connected model with only one overall normalization
for the canonical pair bank cannot reproduce the arithmetic Fubini--Study
quadratic source.  A relative scalar-versus-traceless calibration is necessary.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The $[22]$ or $[211]$ weight forces $s^2=1$ because both target and canonical
weights are $4$.  The scalar weight would then remain $16$, whereas the
arithmetic value is $58$.
\end{proof}

\section{A one-parameter canonical deformation family and the mean-curvature card}
\label{sec:v24-one-parameter}

For $\rho\ge0$ define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal Q_\rho
 :=\mathcal Q_0(P_{\rm tr}+\rho P_{\rm sc}).}
 \label{eq:v24-Qrho}

This is a target-independent one-parameter relative calibration family once
the scalar collective channel has been physically normalized.

\begin{corollary}[Exact one-parameter landing]
\label{cor:v24-one-parameter-landing}
The edge-source weights of $\mathcal Q_\rho$ are
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 16\rho^2,\quad8,\quad4,\quad4.}
 \label{eq:v24-Qrho-weights}
\end{equation}
Therefore
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal Q_\rho^*\mathcal Q_\rho
 =\mathcal Q_{\rm FS}^*\mathcal Q_{\rm FS}
 \iff
 \rho=\sqrt{\frac{29}{8}}.}
 \label{eq:v24-rho-FS}
\end{equation}
Thus, relative to the canonical Hermitian pair source, the strong V23
quadratic target contains only one independent positive calibration.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Only the scalar line is rescaled in \eqref{eq:v24-Qrho}; apply
\eqref{eq:v24-Q0-weights}.  Positivity of $\rho$ selects the positive square
root of $58/16=29/8$.
\end{proof}

The same scalar can be read without choosing the edge realization.  For a
symmetric normal map $\mathcal B$ on the six-real-dimensional tangent, define
its mean-curvature vector
\[
 H_{\mathcal B}
 :=\frac16\sum_{a=1}^6\mathcal B(f_a,f_a),
\]
where $(f_a)$ is any real orthonormal tangent frame.

\begin{proposition}[Mean-curvature normalization of the scalar channel]
\label{prop:v24-mean-curvature}
If $\widetilde{\mathcal B}^*\widetilde{\mathcal B}$ agrees with the universal
weight $4$ on the traceless K\"ahler sector and vanishes on the anti-K\"ahler
sector, while its scalar K\"ahler weight is $\gamma_{\rm sc}$, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|H_{\mathcal B}\|^2=\frac{\gamma_{\rm sc}}6.}
 \label{eq:v24-H-gamma}
\end{equation}
In particular
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|H_{0}\|^2=\frac23,
 \qquad
 \|H_{\rm FS}\|^2=\frac{29}{12}.}
 \label{eq:v24-H-values}
\end{equation}
Once the traceless quadratic gate has passed, the single scalar condition
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\|H_{\rm St}\|^2=\frac{29}{12}}
 \label{eq:v24-H-gate}
\end{equation}
is equivalent to the remaining Fubini--Study scalar-source match.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
By definition of $\tau$,
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal B}\tau
 =\frac1{\sqrt6}\sum_a\mathcal B(f_a,f_a)
 =\sqrt6\,H_{\mathcal B}.
\]
Taking squared norms gives
$\gamma_{\rm sc}=6\|H_{\mathcal B}\|^2$.  Substitute the scalar weights
$4$ and $29/2$ for the two displayed cases.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Constant-curvature-offset interpretation]
\label{cor:v24-curvature-offset}
Assume two quadratic normal sources have identical traceless K\"ahler Gram,
zero anti-K\"ahler leakage, and scalar weights $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$.  Then the
sectional curvatures reconstructed by the Gauss equation differ by the same
constant on every real orthonormal two-plane:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 K_2(X,Y)-K_1(X,Y)=\frac{\gamma_2-\gamma_1}{6}.}
 \label{eq:v24-constant-shift}
\end{equation}
Consequently the passage from the universal Hermitian quadratic source to the
Fubini--Study source raises every sectional curvature by
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{1}{6}\left(\frac{29}{2}-4\right)=\frac74.}
 \label{eq:v24-seven-fourths}
\end{equation}
The K\"ahler-angle-dependent part of the curvature is unchanged.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The scalar normal component has the form
$\alpha g(X,Y)n$ for a unit normal $n$ and is orthogonal to the common
traceless normal source.  Its scalar quadratic weight is
$\gamma=6\alpha^2$.  For orthonormal $X,Y$, the mixed scalar normal term
vanishes and the diagonal scalar contribution to the Gauss equation is
$\alpha^2=\gamma/6$.  Subtracting the two Gauss equations proves
\eqref{eq:v24-constant-shift}.  The numerical value follows from the two
scalar weights.
\end{proof}

\section{From scalar retuning to a genuine occurrence prediction}
\label{sec:v25-context}

V24 showed that the arithmetic Fubini--Study quadratic source differs from the
universal Hermitian quadratic source by the positive rank-one correction
\[
 G_{\rm FS}^{(2)}-G_0^{(2)}
 =\frac{21}{2}P_{\rm sc},
 \qquad
 G_0^{(2)}=4P_+.
\]
Here $P_{\rm sc}=|\tau\rangle\langle\tau|$ is the scalar K\"ahler line,
$P_+=P_{\rm sc}+P_{\rm tr}$ is the full nine-dimensional K\"ahler quadratic
sector, and the twelve-dimensional anti-K\"ahler sector is the kernel of
$G_0^{(2)}$.

The mature Grand-Tensor fusion calculus supplies a stronger structural split.
After proper-subset shorting, the all-residual degree-two source decomposes
orthogonally into the product-connected tensor and a genuinely nonmonoidal
occurrence sector.  When the degree-one multiplication map has zero metric
fusion defect, the product-connected carrier is an isometric tensor product of
the one-cell source and its source metric is fixed; a positive orthogonal
occurrence innovation is then the only way to add source Gram without retuning
the product tensor \cite{GT77}.

The purpose of V25 is to combine these two facts.  The result is a concrete
prediction: on the exact-fusion branch, arithmetic Fubini--Study geometry
requires exactly one arithmetic-visible nonmonoidal occurrence direction, it
must be $S_4$-invariant and isotropic, and its normalization is fixed.  This is
not an occurrence theorem for the old Store.  It is a necessary-and-sufficient
form of the degree-two occurrence packet if the arithmetic quadratic duality is
to hold on the exact product-fusion branch.

\section{Exact-fusion decomposition and the compressed occurrence Gram}
\label{sec:v25-fusion-occurrence}

Let
\[
 \mathcal K:=\operatorname{Sym}_{\R}^2(W_{\R}),
 \qquad \dim_{\R}\mathcal K=21,
\]
with the scalar unit vector $\tau$ and projectors
\[
 P_{\rm sc}=|\tau\rangle\langle\tau|,
 \qquad Q=I-P_{\rm sc}.
\]
Retain the V24 universal product-connected synthesis
\[
 S_0:\mathcal K\longrightarrow H_{\rm prod},
 \qquad S_0^*S_0=G_0^{(2)}=4P_+.
\]

At degree two, let $S_2:E_2\to H_2$ be the actual source-minimal synthesis and
let $m_{1,1}:E_1\otimes E_1\to E_2$ be the declared coefficient occurrence
map.  On the branch
\[
 \Delta_{1,1}^{\rm met}=0,
\]
the Grand-Tensor fusion theorem gives the canonical isometry
\[
 \Gamma:H_1\otimes H_1\longrightarrow H_2
\]
and the positive occurrence innovation
\[
 \mathbb I_{1,1}^{\rm fus}
 =S_2^*(I-\Gamma\Gamma^*)S_2\succeq0.
\]
Let $c:\mathcal K\to E_2$ be the independently declared quadratic coefficient
compiler after the same proper-subset, nuisance, mediator, and provenance
shorts used by the arithmetic comparison.  Define the arithmetic-visible
nonmonoidal occurrence Gram
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 N:=c^*\mathbb I_{1,1}^{\rm fus}c\succeq0.}
 \label{eq:v25-N-def}
\end{equation}
On the exact source-fusion branch the product and nonmonoidal occurrence ranges
are orthogonal, so the complete quadratic source Gram is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{G_{\rm all}^{(2)}=G_0^{(2)}+N.}
 \label{eq:v25-total-Gram}
\end{equation}
No claim is made that $c$ or the occurrence panel is already populated by the
old Store; \eqref{eq:v25-N-def} is the correct compressed object once that
physical panel exists.

\begin{theorem}[Rank-one nonmonoidal occurrence theorem]
\label{thm:v25-rankone-occurrence}
Assume the V21 first-order complex source has been identified, the degree-two
metric fusion defect vanishes, and the complete all-residual quadratic source
is compared on the common coefficient space $\mathcal K$ above.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 G_{\rm all}^{(2)}=G_{\rm FS}^{(2)}
 \iff
 N=\frac{21}{2}P_{\rm sc}.}
 \label{eq:v25-N-target}
\end{equation}
Consequently exact arithmetic quadratic duality on this branch forces
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \rank N=1,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Ker} N=\tau^\perp,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Ran} N=\R\tau.}
 \label{eq:v25-rank-one}
\end{equation}
In particular every arithmetic-visible anti-K\"ahler, $[31]$, $[22]$, or
$[211]$ nonmonoidal occurrence component must vanish.

If the compressed occurrence synthesis is source minimal for the arithmetic
quadratic coefficient bank, its source dimension is exactly one.  If the full
physical nonmonoidal occurrence carrier is larger, all additional directions
must be orthogonal to the arithmetic quadratic compiler and are therefore not
licensed as part of this duality by the present theorem.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
V24 proves
\[
 G_{\rm FS}^{(2)}
 =G_0^{(2)}+\frac{21}{2}P_{\rm sc}.
\]
Subtract $G_0^{(2)}$ from \eqref{eq:v25-total-Gram}.  This gives
\eqref{eq:v25-N-target} immediately.  Since $P_{\rm sc}$ is a rank-one
orthogonal projection and the coefficient $21/2$ is strictly positive,
\eqref{eq:v25-rank-one} follows.  For a source-minimal synthesis the source
rank equals the Gram rank.  The final statement follows because the theorem
constrains only the compression $c^*\mathbb I_{1,1}^{\rm fus}c$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact product closure is incompatible with arithmetic Fubini--Study geometry]
\label{cor:v25-product-only-no-go}
Under the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:v25-rankone-occurrence}, if the degree-two
fusion is onto on the arithmetic quadratic bank, so that $N=0$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \|G_{\rm all}^{(2)}-G_{\rm FS}^{(2)}\|_{\HS}
 =\frac{21}{2}.}
\]
Thus the arithmetic quadratic source does not lie on the purely monoidal
product-system branch.  Exact metric fusion together with arithmetic
Fubini--Study duality requires a genuine positive occurrence innovation.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If $N=0$, the Gram difference is
$-(21/2)P_{\rm sc}$.  A rank-one orthogonal projection has Hilbert--Schmidt
norm one.
\end{proof}

\section{The minimal geometric realization: one isotropic normal}
\label{sec:v25-isotropic-normal}

The rank-one occurrence theorem has a direct second-fundamental-form
interpretation.  Let $\nu$ be a unit normal orthogonal to the V24 universal
Hermitian normal carrier and define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal C_{\rm occ}(X,Y)
 :=\frac{\sqrt7}{2}\,g(X,Y)\nu.}
 \label{eq:v25-Cocc}
\end{equation}

\begin{proposition}[Unique source-minimal isotropic occurrence normalization]
\label{prop:v25-isotropic-normal}
The induced quadratic Gram of \eqref{eq:v25-Cocc} is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \widetilde{\mathcal C}_{\rm occ}^*
 \widetilde{\mathcal C}_{\rm occ}
 =\frac{21}{2}P_{\rm sc}.}
 \label{eq:v25-Cocc-Gram}
\end{equation}
Hence the orthogonal sum
\[
 \mathcal B_0\oplus\mathcal C_{\rm occ}
\]
has exactly the arithmetic Fubini--Study quadratic source Gram.
For every real orthonormal tangent pair $X,Y$, the added normal contributes
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \langle\mathcal C_{\rm occ}(X,X),
       \mathcal C_{\rm occ}(Y,Y)\rangle
 -\|\mathcal C_{\rm occ}(X,Y)\|^2
 =\frac74.}
 \label{eq:v25-curv-shift}
\end{equation}
Thus the single nonmonoidal occurrence line supplies exactly the universal
$7/4$ sectional-curvature offset identified in V24.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Let $(f_a)_{a=1}^6$ be a real orthonormal tangent frame and
\[
 \tau=\frac1{\sqrt6}\sum_{a=1}^6 f_a\odot f_a.
\]
The map \eqref{eq:v25-Cocc} vanishes on traceless K\"ahler tensors and on the
anti-K\"ahler sector, while
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal C}_{\rm occ}\tau
 =\frac{\sqrt7}{2}\sqrt6\,\nu.
\]
Its squared norm is $6(7/4)=21/2$, proving
\eqref{eq:v25-Cocc-Gram}.  For orthonormal $X,Y$,
$g(X,X)=g(Y,Y)=1$ and $g(X,Y)=0$, so the Gauss contribution is
$(\sqrt7/2)^2=7/4$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Occurrence rank one is source-dimension minimal]
\label{cor:v25-minimal-rank}
Among exact-fusion extensions of the V24 universal quadratic source, one new
real source direction is necessary and sufficient to realize the arithmetic
Fubini--Study Gram.  No zero-dimensional extension can work, and any
source-minimal extension of larger dimension contains redundant directions for
this quadratic target.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Necessity is \Cref{cor:v25-product-only-no-go}; sufficiency is
\Cref{prop:v25-isotropic-normal}.  Gram rank equals minimum source dimension.
\end{proof}

\section{A two-scalar finite certificate for the complete occurrence Gram}
\label{sec:v25-two-scalar}

Although \eqref{eq:v25-N-target} is a $21\times21$ matrix identity, positivity
collapses its exact certification to two nonnegative scalar reads.  Put
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 a:=\Tr(P_{\rm sc}N)=\langle\tau,N\tau\rangle,
 \qquad
 b:=\Tr N,
 \qquad
 \ell:=b-a.}
 \label{eq:v25-two-scalars}
\end{equation}
Since $N\succeq0$ and $P_{\rm sc}$ is an orthogonal projection,
$\ell\ge0$.

\begin{theorem}[Two-scalar occurrence certificate]
\label{thm:v25-two-scalar}
For every positive arithmetic-visible occurrence Gram $N\succeq0$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 N=\frac{21}{2}P_{\rm sc}
 \iff
 a=b=\frac{21}{2}.}
 \label{eq:v25-two-scalar-exact}
\end{equation}
Thus exact quadratic source duality on the exact-fusion branch is decided by
only:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item the scalar-channel occurrence energy $a$;
\item the total arithmetic-visible nonmonoidal occurrence energy $b$.
\end{enumerate}
No separate measurement of the twenty-dimensional complement is required.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The forward implication is immediate.  Conversely suppose
$a=b=21/2$.  Put $Q=I-P_{\rm sc}$.  Then
\[
 \Tr(QNQ)=\Tr N-\Tr(P_{\rm sc}N)=b-a=0.
\]
The compression $QNQ$ is positive, hence $QNQ=0$.  Since
$N=N^{1/2}N^{1/2}$,
\[
 QNQ=(N^{1/2}Q)^*(N^{1/2}Q)=0
\]
implies $N^{1/2}Q=0$, and therefore $NQ=QN=0$.  Thus $N$ is supported on the
rank-one range of $P_{\rm sc}$ and equals $aP_{\rm sc}=(21/2)P_{\rm sc}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Quantitative two-scalar defect bounds]
\label{thm:v25-two-scalar-bounds}
Let $\alpha=21/2$ and let $a,b,\ell$ be as in
\eqref{eq:v25-two-scalars}.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 (a-\alpha)^2+\frac{\ell^2}{20}
 \le
 \|N-\alpha P_{\rm sc}\|_{\HS}^2
 \le
 (a-\alpha)^2+2a\ell+\ell^2.}
 \label{eq:v25-two-scalar-bounds}
\end{equation}
Consequently convergence of the two scalar cards
$a\to\alpha$ and $b-a\to0$ forces convergence of the complete occurrence Gram
to the arithmetic target.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
In the orthogonal decomposition
$\mathcal K=\R\tau\oplus\tau^\perp$, write
\[
 N=\begin{pmatrix}a&v^*\\v&C\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad C\succeq0,
 \qquad \Tr C=\ell.
\]
Then
\[
 \|N-\alpha P_{\rm sc}\|_{\HS}^2
 =(a-\alpha)^2+2\|v\|^2+\|C\|_{\HS}^2.
\]
Since $C$ acts on a twenty-dimensional space,
\[
 \frac{\ell^2}{20}\le\|C\|_{\HS}^2\le\ell^2.
\]
Positivity of the block matrix implies
$vv^*\preceq aC$ when $a>0$ (and $v=0$ when $a=0$), hence
$\|v\|^2\le a\Tr C=a\ell$.  Substitution gives both bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Operational interpretation of the two cards]
