\section{Why degree three is now a coherence problem rather than a new arithmetic fit}
\label{sec:v26-context}

V25 reduced the arithmetic-visible degree-two nonmonoidal occurrence on the
exact product-fusion branch to the positive rank-one scalar source
\[
 N=\alpha_*P_{\rm sc},
 \qquad
 \alpha_*=\frac{21}{2}.
\]
Equivalently the source-minimal isotropic normal has amplitude
\[
 \kappa_*:=\frac{\sqrt7}{2},
 \qquad
 \alpha_*=6\kappa_*^2.
\]
The mature Grand-Tensor fusion calculus simultaneously gives a hard firewall:
one- and two-occurrence carriers do not determine degree three.  Even when the
lower fusion maps are exact tensor products, the degree-three carrier may have
a fresh orthogonal source sector, and the two parenthesized fusion maps may
carry a nonzero associator residual \cite{GT77}.

The arithmetic side is more rigid.  The V23--V25 Fubini--Study quadratic
compiler is built functorially from the Hermitian source metric and its complex
structure.  On a unitary source bundle it is parallel.  Consequently the
arithmetic target has no independent covariant cubic normal tensor: at the
next grade the new information is whether the physical degree-two source is
transported coherently, not the value of another freely adjustable arithmetic
isotype.

V26 makes this precise.  It proves that on the scalar-occurrence branch the
entire intrinsic cubic transport reduces to the derivative of one real scalar
$\alpha$, while the graded physical packet contributes two logically
independent positive tests: the triple-fusion associator and the
arithmetic-visible degree-three occurrence innovation.  It then proves a
neighborhood rigidity theorem: once the K\"ahler first-order structure and the
V25 Fubini--Study quadratic tensor hold coherently on a connected neighborhood,
the complete intrinsic source geometry is locally the Fubini--Study germ.
There is then no infinite tower of new intrinsic arithmetic curvature
parameters to fit.

\section{The Fubini--Study quadratic compiler is parallel}
\label{sec:v26-parallel-B}

Let $E\to U$ be a complex rank-three Hermitian bundle with Hermitian metric
$h$, real metric $g=\Re h$, complex structure $J$, and a unitary connection
$D$.  Let $D^{\rm End}$ be the induced connection on
$\operatorname{Herm}(E)$.  Retain the V23 constants
\[
 c=\frac1{\sqrt2},
 \qquad
 d=\frac{\sqrt{29}-2\sqrt2}{6},
\]
and define fibrewise
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal B_{\rm FS}(X,Y)
 =c\,(X Y^*+Y X^*)+d\,g(X,Y)I_E.}
 \label{eq:v26-BFS}
\end{equation}
Here $XY^*$ denotes the rank-one endomorphism $v\mapsto Xh(Y,v)$.

\begin{theorem}[Parallel quadratic compiler]
\label{thm:v26-B-parallel}
For the induced connection on
$\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb R}^2(E_{\mathbb R})^*\otimes
 \operatorname{Herm}(E)$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{D\mathcal B_{\rm FS}=0.}
 \label{eq:v26-DB-zero}
\end{equation}
Hence every iterated covariant derivative also vanishes:
\[
 \boxed{D^k\mathcal B_{\rm FS}=0\qquad(k\ge1).}
\]
In particular the arithmetic Fubini--Study quadratic source has no independent
covariant cubic normal coefficient.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Because $D$ is unitary,
\[
 Dh=0,
 \qquad
 Dg=0,
 \qquad
 DJ=0,
 \qquad
 D^{\rm End}I_E=0.
\]
Moreover the induced endomorphism connection obeys the Leibniz rule
\[
 D^{\rm End}_Z(XY^*)=(D_ZX)Y^*+X(D_ZY)^*.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &(D_Z\mathcal B_{\rm FS})(X,Y)\\
 &\quad:=D_Z^{\rm End}(\mathcal B_{\rm FS}(X,Y))
 -\mathcal B_{\rm FS}(D_ZX,Y)
 -\mathcal B_{\rm FS}(X,D_ZY)=0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:v26-DB-zero}.  Iterating a zero tensor gives the final
statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Parallel scalar and traceless quadratic channels]
\label{cor:v26-parallel-projectors}
Let $P_{\rm sc}$ be the normalized scalar K\"ahler projector and
$P_{\rm tr}$ the traceless K\"ahler projector of V24.  Under the induced
connection on $\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb R}^2(E_{\mathbb R})$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{DP_{\rm sc}=DP_{\rm tr}=0.}
 \label{eq:v26-parallel-P}
\end{equation}
Thus the decomposition into scalar, traceless K\"ahler, and anti-K\"ahler
quadratic sectors is preserved by unitary transport.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The scalar line is generated by the normalized metric tensor
\[
 \tau=\frac1{\sqrt6}\sum_{a=1}^6 f_a\odot f_a
\]
in any real orthonormal frame.  It is frame independent and parallel because
$Dg=0$.  Hence $P_{\rm sc}=|\tau\rangle\langle\tau|$ is parallel.  The
K\"ahler involution
$\mathscr J_2(X\odot Y)=JX\odot JY$ is parallel because $DJ=0$; therefore its
$+1$ projector $P_+$ is parallel.  Since
$P_{\rm tr}=P_+-P_{\rm sc}$, it is parallel as well.
\end{proof}

\section{Intrinsic local symmetry of the arithmetic source germ}
\label{sec:v26-local-symmetry}

The V22 normalization has Fubini--Study sectional curvature
\[
 K_{\rm FS}(X,Y)=1+3g(JX,Y)^2
\]
for real orthonormal $X,Y$.  The corresponding curvature tensor may be written
\begin{equation}
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
R_{\rm FS}(X,Y,Z,T)
={}&g(Y,Z)g(X,T)-g(X,Z)g(Y,T)\\
&+g(JY,Z)g(JX,T)-g(JX,Z)g(JY,T)\\
&+2g(X,JY)g(JZ,T).
\end{aligned}}
\label{eq:v26-RFS}
\end{equation}
Indeed $R_{\rm FS}(X,Y,Y,X)=1+3g(JX,Y)^2$.

\begin{theorem}[Parallel curvature and local symmetry]
\label{thm:v26-R-parallel}
On a K\"ahler source bundle with the curvature tensor
\eqref{eq:v26-RFS},
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\nabla R_{\rm FS}=0.}
 \label{eq:v26-nabla-R-zero}
\end{equation}
Consequently all higher covariant curvature derivatives vanish.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Levi--Civita connection of a K\"ahler metric satisfies
$\nabla g=0$ and $\nabla J=0$.  Every coefficient in
\eqref{eq:v26-RFS} is constant and every tensor factor is obtained from $g$
and $J$ by contraction.  Covariant differentiation therefore annihilates the
right-hand side.  Iteration gives $\nabla^kR_{\rm FS}=0$ for every $k\ge1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Local complex-space-form rigidity]
\label{thm:v26-local-rigidity}
Let $(M^6,g,J)$ be a connected K\"ahler manifold and suppose on an open set
$U\subset M$ that its curvature tensor is exactly
\eqref{eq:v26-RFS}.  Then every point of $U$ has a neighborhood
holomorphically isometric to the V22-normalized Fubini--Study germ in
$\mathbb{CP}^3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fix $p\in U$ and a point $o\in\mathbb{CP}^3$.  Choose a complex-linear
isometry
$L:T_pM\to T_o\mathbb{CP}^3$.  By \eqref{eq:v26-RFS}, $L$ identifies the two
curvature tensors at the base points.  By
\Cref{thm:v26-R-parallel}, both curvature tensors are parallel.

For sufficiently small $v\in T_pM$, define
\[
 F(\exp_p v):=\exp_o(Lv).
\]
The differential of an exponential map in a transverse direction is given by
a Jacobi field $Y$ satisfying
\[
 Y''+R(Y,\dot\gamma)\dot\gamma=0,
 \qquad
 Y(0)=0,
 \qquad
 Y'(0)=w.
\]
Along each radial geodesic, parallel transport makes $R$ constant because
$\nabla R=0$.  The map $L$ identifies the resulting Jacobi equations and their
initial conditions with those in the Fubini--Study model.  Hence it preserves
all Jacobi-field inner products and therefore the metric in normal
coordinates.  Thus $F$ is a local isometry.  Since $J$ is parallel on both
sides and $LJ=JL$ at the base point, the same radial parallel-transport
argument gives $dF\circ J=J\circ dF$.  Hence $F$ is holomorphic.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[No independent higher intrinsic curvature parameters]
\label{cor:v26-no-higher-intrinsic}
On a smooth K\"ahler branch, once the V21 first-order Hermitian source and the
V25 Fubini--Study quadratic curvature tensor hold on a connected neighborhood,
the entire intrinsic local arithmetic source geometry is fixed.  Higher
physical occurrence sectors may still exist, but any such sector must be
arithmetic-invisible unless it preserves the same locally symmetric metric.
\end{corollary}

\section{The scalar-occurrence branch has only one cubic transport field}
\label{sec:v26-scalar-transport}

Now return to the exact product-fusion branch of V25.  Suppose on a smooth
neighborhood $U$ the arithmetic-visible degree-two occurrence remains in the
scalar channel,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{N(p)=\alpha(p)P_{\rm sc}(p),\qquad \alpha(p)\ge0.}
 \label{eq:v26-alpha-field}
\end{equation}
No assumption is yet made that $\alpha$ equals $21/2$ away from the reference
point.

\begin{theorem}[Scalar transport identity]
\label{thm:v26-alpha-transport}
Under unitary/K\"ahler transport,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{DN=(d\alpha)\otimes P_{\rm sc},}
 \label{eq:v26-DN}
\end{equation}
and, with Hilbert--Schmidt norm on the quadratic endomorphism factor,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\|DN\|^2=\|d\alpha\|^2.}
 \label{eq:v26-DN-norm}
\end{equation}
Thus on the V25 rank-one branch the complete arithmetic-visible covariant
cubic transport is the gradient of one real scalar.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Differentiate \eqref{eq:v26-alpha-field} and use
$DP_{\rm sc}=0$ from \Cref{cor:v26-parallel-projectors}.  Since
$P_{\rm sc}$ is a rank-one orthogonal projector,
$\|P_{\rm sc}\|_{\HS}=1$, which gives
\eqref{eq:v26-DN-norm} after summing over an orthonormal tangent frame.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Amplitude form]
\label{cor:v26-kappa-transport}
If the scalar occurrence is represented source-minimally by a unit normal
$\nu$ and a smooth amplitude $\kappa$,
\[
 \mathcal C_{\rm occ}(X,Y)=\kappa\,g(X,Y)\nu,
 \qquad
 \alpha=6\kappa^2,
\]
then the arithmetic normalization is
\[
 \boxed{\kappa^2=\frac74.}
\]
On a symmetry-preserving branch on which the trivial $S_4$ normal line is
preserved by the metric normal connection, a local unit section $\nu$ is
parallel and
\[
 \boxed{D\mathcal C_{\rm occ}=(d\kappa)\otimes g\otimes\nu.}
\]
Hence no independent normal rotation is available in the arithmetic scalar
channel.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The relation $\alpha=6\kappa^2$ is the V25 scalar-line Gram computation.
The trivial $S_4$ line cannot mix equivariantly with the nontrivial
$[31]$, $[22]$, or $[211]$ normal sectors.  A metric connection on a real
one-dimensional line has zero connection form in a local unit frame, so
$D\nu=0$ on that line.  Since $Dg=0$, the derivative formula follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Third-order metric-jet landing]
\label{thm:v26-third-jet}
Let $p\in U$ lie on the V25 arithmetic quadratic landing,
$\alpha(p)=21/2$.  If
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{d\alpha|_p=0,}
 \label{eq:v26-dalpha-zero-point}
\end{equation}
then the candidate Store metric and the Fubini--Study metric have the same
intrinsic metric three-jet at $p$ after matching orthonormal complex normal
coordinates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
On the scalar branch the V24--V25 quadratic source determines the curvature
tensor algebraically from $g,J,$ and $\alpha$.  The parallel tensors $g,J,$
$P_{\rm sc}$ and the universal traceless quadratic compiler contribute no
covariant derivative.  Thus $d\alpha|_p=0$ gives
$\nabla R|_p=0$, equal to the arithmetic value by
\Cref{thm:v26-R-parallel}.  In Riemannian normal coordinates the metric
three-jet is determined by $(g_p,R_p,(\nabla R)_p)$; explicitly, in the present
curvature-sign convention,
\[
 g_{ij}(x)
 =\delta_{ij}
 -\frac13R_{ikjl}x^kx^l
 -\frac16R_{ikjl;m}x^kx^lx^m
 +O(|x|^4).
\]
The two metrics therefore have identical coefficients through cubic order.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Connected-neighborhood closure from one scalar transport law]
\label{cor:v26-alpha-neighborhood}
Assume the scalar-occurrence branch \eqref{eq:v26-alpha-field} holds on a
connected open set $U$, the first-order Store source is K\"ahler with the V21
complex structure, and
\[
 \alpha(p_0)=\frac{21}{2}
\]
at one point $p_0\in U$.  If
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{d\alpha=0\quad\text{throughout }U,}
 \label{eq:v26-alpha-constant-law}
\end{equation}
then $\alpha\equiv21/2$ on $U$ and the intrinsic Store source geometry is
locally holomorphically isometric to the arithmetic Fubini--Study germ.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
A smooth function with zero differential on a connected set is constant, so
$\alpha\equiv\alpha(p_0)=21/2$.  V24--V25 then give the full Fubini--Study
curvature tensor at every point of $U$.  Apply
\Cref{thm:v26-local-rigidity}.
\end{proof}

\section{Why the first triple panel is nevertheless logically necessary}
\label{sec:v26-triple-necessity}

The preceding arithmetic rigidity does not allow degree three to be inferred
from V25 data.  The physical graded source still has to establish coherent
fusion.  Retain the Grand-Tensor triple associator residual
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb A_{1,1,1}^{\rm fus}
 =\mathfrak A_{1,1,1}^*\mathfrak A_{1,1,1}\succeq0,
 \label{eq:v26-associator}
\end{equation}
where
\[
 \mathfrak A_{1,1,1}
 =\Gamma_{2,1}(\Gamma_{1,1}\otimes I)
 -\Gamma_{1,2}(I\otimes\Gamma_{1,1}).
\]
Also let
$N_3^{\rm vis}\succeq0$ denote the compression of the degree-three fusion
innovation $\mathbb I_{2,1}^{\rm fus}$ to the declared arithmetic-visible
covariant cubic packet after the same proper-subset, nuisance, mediator, and
provenance shorts.  Hidden degree-three physical directions orthogonal to this
compiler are not excluded by the arithmetic comparison.

\begin{theorem}[Innovation and associator are independent of all V25 data]
\label{cth:v26-triple-independent}
There are graded source packets with identical degree-one and degree-two data,
including exact V25 quadratic landing, for which:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item the triple associator vanishes but the degree-three fusion innovation has
positive rank;
\item both parenthesized degree-three fusions are onto, hence have zero fusion
innovation, while the associator residual is nonzero.
\end{enumerate}
Therefore neither triple freshness nor parenthesization coherence may be
inferred from the complete one- and two-occurrence arithmetic landing.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For (i), keep the prescribed $H_1,H_2$ and put
\[
 H_3=H_1^{\otimes3}\oplus K
\]
with $K\ne0$.  Use the canonical product embedding for both parenthesizations.
Their images agree, so the associator vanishes, while the orthogonal $K$ sector
is a positive degree-three occurrence innovation.

For (ii), take $H_3=H_1^{\otimes3}$ and let both parenthesized fusion maps be
unitary onto $H_3$, but compose one of them with a nontrivial unitary $U$ on
$H_3$.  Both fusion innovations vanish because both maps are onto, whereas
\[
 \mathfrak A=(I-U)\,\Gamma_{\rm can}
\]
is nonzero whenever $U\ne I$.  All degree-one and degree-two data are
unchanged in both constructions.
\end{proof}

\section{One nonnegative cubic coherence card}
\label{sec:v26-cubic-card}

The arithmetic target has no independent covariant cubic normal tensor, so the
strong degree-three source condition is the simultaneous absence of three
possible defects:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item parenthesization failure;
\item fresh arithmetic-visible degree-three occurrence;
\item variation of the V25 scalar normalization.
\end{enumerate}
Define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak C_3
 :=\Tr\mathbb A_{1,1,1}^{\rm fus}
   +\Tr N_3^{\rm vis}
   +\|d\alpha\|^2.}
 \label{eq:v26-C3}
\end{equation}
Every term is nonnegative.

\begin{theorem}[Strong cubic coherence certificate]
\label{thm:v26-cubic-certificate}
On the exact V25 degree-two branch,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak C_3=0
 \iff
 \mathbb A_{1,1,1}^{\rm fus}=0,
 \quad
 N_3^{\rm vis}=0,
 \quad
 d\alpha=0.}
 \label{eq:v26-C3-exact}
\end{equation}
At a reference point with $\alpha=21/2$, the right-hand conditions imply exact
third-order intrinsic Fubini--Study landing together with coherent
parenthesized source fusion and no fresh arithmetic-visible cubic source.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The reverse implication is immediate.  For the forward implication, all three
summands in \eqref{eq:v26-C3} are nonnegative.  A positive semidefinite finite
matrix with zero trace is zero, so the first two trace conditions force the
associator Gram and the visible innovation Gram to vanish.  The final summand
forces $d\alpha=0$.  Apply \Cref{thm:v26-third-jet} for the intrinsic metric
three-jet and use the definitions of the two fusion defects for the graded
source statements.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Strong source coherence versus hidden triple physics]
The condition $N_3^{\rm vis}=0$ does not assert that the full physical
three-occurrence carrier has no fresh directions.  It asserts only that no
fresh degree-three direction couples to the arithmetic covariant cubic
compiler.  This distinction is required by the Grand-Tensor source-completeness
firewall and is preserved throughout V26.
\end{remark}

\section{A finite scalar-transport card}
\label{sec:v26-finite-card}

The derivative $d\alpha$ need not be postulated.  Once the V25 occurrence
packet can be acquired at neighboring physical base laws, let
$(e_a)_{a=1}^6$ be a local orthonormal real tangent frame and measure the V25
scalar occurrence coefficient at the two neighboring laws
$p_{+h e_a}$ and $p_{-h e_a}$.  Put
\begin{equation}
 D_{h,a}\alpha
 :=\frac{\alpha(+he_a)-\alpha(-he_a)}{2h},
 \qquad
 \boxed{\chi_{3,h}:=\sum_{a=1}^6(D_{h,a}\alpha)^2.}
 \label{eq:v26-finite-gradient}
\end{equation}

\begin{proposition}[Finite central-difference convergence]
\label{prop:v26-finite-gradient}
If $\alpha$ is $C^3$ along the six physical neighboring-law directions, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \chi_{3,h}=\|d\alpha\|^2+O(h^2).}
 \label{eq:v26-finite-gradient-limit}
\end{equation}
In particular the arithmetic scalar-transport target is
\[
 \boxed{\chi_{3,h}\longrightarrow0.}
\]
No third derivative of a fitted arithmetic model is required; the card uses
only repeated V25 scalar reads at actual neighboring laws.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For each $a$, the symmetric Taylor expansion gives
\[
 \frac{\alpha(+he_a)-\alpha(-he_a)}{2h}
 =\partial_{e_a}\alpha+O(h^2).
\]
Squaring and summing over the orthonormal frame gives
\eqref{eq:v26-finite-gradient-limit}.
\end{proof}

\section{Neighborhood closure versus a single-point cubic pass}
\label{sec:v26-neighborhood-firewall}

\begin{scope}[A vanishing cubic jet at one point is not a neighborhood theorem]
\label{fire:v26-point-vs-neighborhood}
The condition $d\alpha|_p=0$ proves only the third-order landing at the chosen
point.  A smooth scalar may have zero gradient at one point and vary elsewhere.
Therefore local Fubini--Study rigidity follows only after the V25 quadratic
identity is known throughout a neighborhood, or after a structural transport
law proves $d\alpha=0$ throughout a connected neighborhood.  Repeated finite
neighbor cards can test this; one isolated cubic pass cannot.
\end{scope}

\begin{theorem}[Intrinsic nonlinear closure criterion]
\label{thm:v26-nonlinear-closure}
Let $U$ be a connected smooth source neighborhood.  Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the V21 complex source extends to a K\"ahler source bundle on $U$;
\item the degree-two product fusion is metrically exact and the V24 universal
      traceless quadratic source is transported by the induced unitary
      connection;
\item the arithmetic-visible nonmonoidal occurrence has the scalar form
      $N=\alpha P_{\rm sc}$;
\item $\alpha=21/2$ at one point and $d\alpha=0$ on $U$;
\item the arithmetic-visible triple associator and triple occurrence
      innovation vanish coherently on $U$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the intrinsic source geometry on $U$ is locally holomorphically isometric
to the V22-normalized Fubini--Study germ.  No additional intrinsic
fourth- or higher-order curvature parameter is available to be fitted.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By (C3)--(C4) and connectedness,
$\alpha\equiv21/2$.  By V24--V25 the full quadratic source Gram and hence the
curvature tensor are the Fubini--Study tensor at every point.  Assumptions
(C1)--(C2) identify the same parallel $g,J$ structures used in
\eqref{eq:v26-RFS}; (C5) ensures that the physical graded realization is
independent of parenthesization and contains no fresh arithmetic-visible cubic
source.  The intrinsic local isometry now follows from
\Cref{thm:v26-local-rigidity}.  Once $R$ has the algebraic form
\eqref{eq:v26-RFS}, \Cref{thm:v26-R-parallel} gives all higher covariant
curvature derivatives equal to zero.
\end{proof}

\begin{scope}[What V26 closes and what it does not]
\label{scope:v26-closure-scope}
The preceding theorem closes the \emph{intrinsic local source geometry} on the
stated smooth K\"ahler/coherent branch.  It does not prove that the historical
Store supplies the required triple panel, does not remove arithmetic-invisible
higher occurrence sectors, and does not prove equality of the actual transfer,
Krylov, Frobenius, or Wilson operators.  Those remain separate dynamic gates.
\end{scope}

\section{Upstream reduction at the tetrahedrally symmetric Store base law}
\label{sec:v27-context}

V26 identified three logically independent degree-three defects on the exact
V25 branch: the fusion associator, a fresh arithmetic-visible triple source,
and the transport gradient $d\alpha$ of the rank-one scalar occurrence.
The Grand-Tensor countertheorem shows that none of the first two is determined
by lower occurrence grades \cite{GT77}.  Before acquiring a complete triple
panel, however, one should exploit the symmetry already proved for the V21
reference law.

Let
\[
 W:=W_0^{\mathbb C}
 =\{z\in\mathbb C^4:\ \sum_{i=1}^4 z_i=0\},
 \qquad \dim_{\mathbb C}W=3,
\]
with its standard unitary $S_4$ action.  Its realification is the V21
future-null source
\[
 W_{\mathbb R}\cong 2[31],
 \qquad \dim_{\mathbb R}W_{\mathbb R}=6.
\]
The canonical Store reference law is the four-identical-cell product point
$z=0$ and is fixed by the full cell-permutation group $S_4$.
The V21 endpoint-sign involution gives the antiunitary real structure
$K_{\rm ren}$, which is ordinary complex conjugation on $W$.

The V25 fresh quadratic occurrence is the trivial scalar line.  Write its
normalized real generator as $\nu$ and its scalar energy as
\[
 N_2=\alpha P_{\rm sc},
 \qquad
 \alpha(0)=\frac{21}{2}.
\]
V27 proves three reductions.
First, tetrahedral symmetry already forces $d\alpha_0=0$; no neighboring-law
measurement is needed for that statement at the symmetric base point.
Second, after restricting the two parenthesized triple fusions to the
scalar-occurrence-times-tangent channel, their complete associator is one real
number.  Third, the complete fresh arithmetic-visible triple innovation is
one nonnegative number.  Thus the full strong V26 cubic card at the symmetric
base point can be decided from two scalar triple reads rather than a large
matrix panel.

\section{Tetrahedral symmetry kills scalar transport at the base point}
\label{sec:v27-alpha-symmetry}

\begin{theorem}[Fixed-point vanishing of the V25 scalar gradient]
\label{thm:v27-alpha-gradient-zero}
Let $U\subset W_{\mathbb R}$ be an $S_4$-stable neighborhood of the origin and
let
\[
 \alpha:U\longrightarrow\mathbb R
\]
be a differentiable $S_4$-invariant scalar occurrence coefficient.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{d\alpha_0=0.}
 \label{eq:v27-alpha-gradient-zero}
\end{equation}
In particular the V26 scalar-transport term vanishes automatically at the
V21 tetrahedrally symmetric Store base law.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For every $g\in S_4$,
$\alpha(gz)=\alpha(z)$.  Since $g0=0$, differentiation at the origin gives
\[
 d\alpha_0\circ g=d\alpha_0.
\]
Hence $d\alpha_0$ is an invariant covector in
$(W_{\mathbb R}^*)^{S_4}$.  But
$W_{\mathbb R}\cong2[31]$ and the standard module $[31]$ has no trivial
subrepresentation.  Therefore
$(W_{\mathbb R}^*)^{S_4}=0$, proving
\eqref{eq:v27-alpha-gradient-zero}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Improved finite central-difference scaling]
\label{cor:v27-central-difference}
If $\alpha$ is $C^3$ at the origin, then for every unit tangent vector $v$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \frac{\alpha(hv)-\alpha(-hv)}{2h}=O(h^2).}
 \label{eq:v27-central-difference-O2}
\end{equation}
Consequently the V26 six-direction card obeys
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\chi_{3,h}=O(h^4)}
 \label{eq:v27-chi-O4}
\end{equation}
at the symmetric base law.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Taylor expansion gives
\[
 \alpha(hv)-\alpha(-hv)
 =2h\,d\alpha_0[v]+\frac{h^3}{3}D^3\alpha_0[v,v,v]+o(h^3).
\]
Use \Cref{thm:v27-alpha-gradient-zero} and divide by $2h$.  Squaring and
summing over an orthonormal six-frame gives \eqref{eq:v27-chi-O4}.
\end{proof}

\begin{scope}[Fixed-point symmetry is not neighborhood constancy]
\label{fire:v27-fixed-not-constant}
Equation \eqref{eq:v27-alpha-gradient-zero} is a pointwise symmetry theorem,
not a transport theorem.  For example
\[
 \alpha(z)=\frac{21}{2}+c\,\|z\|^2
\]
is $S_4$-invariant, $U(1)$-invariant, and compatible with the V21 real
structure, and it satisfies $d\alpha_0=0$ for every $c$, while it is nonconstant
for $c\ne0$.  Thus V26's neighborhood firewall remains essential.
\end{scope}

\section{The scalar-occurrence triple channel is one complex standard module}
\label{sec:v27-scalar-times-tangent}

Assume the V25 scalar occurrence line has been acquired source-minimally and
that the degree-three left and right product fusions exist isometrically on
this channel.  Using the normalized generator $\nu$, identify
\[
 \mathbb R\nu\otimes W\cong W,
 \qquad
 W\otimes\mathbb R\nu\cong W,
\]
and define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 F_Lx:=\Gamma_{2,1}(\nu\otimes x),
 \qquad
 F_Rx:=\Gamma_{1,2}(x\otimes\nu).}
 \label{eq:v27-FLR}
\end{equation}
Thus $F_L,F_R:W\to H_3^{\rm vis}$ are isometries.

\begin{theorem}[One-parameter classification of the visible associator]
\label{thm:v27-associator-one-parameter}
Assume $F_L$ and $F_R$ are $S_4$-equivariant and complex-linear on the V21
complex source.  Put
\[
 T_3:=F_R^*F_L.
\]
Then there is a unique $z_3\in\overline{\mathbb D}$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{T_3=z_3I_W.}
 \label{eq:v27-T-z}
\end{equation}
If, in addition, both fusions intertwine the V21 antiunitary real structures,
then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{z_3\in[-1,1].}
 \label{eq:v27-z-real}
\end{equation}
For the restricted associator
\[
 \mathfrak A_{\rm sc}:=F_L-F_R
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak A_{\rm sc}^*\mathfrak A_{\rm sc}
 =2(1-\Re z_3)I_W,}
 \label{eq:v27-associator-Gram-complex}
\end{equation}
and, on the real-descent branch,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak A_{\rm sc}^*\mathfrak A_{\rm sc}
 =2(1-z_3)I_W,
 \qquad
 \Tr_{\mathbb C}\mathbb A_{\rm sc}=6(1-z_3).}
 \label{eq:v27-associator-trace}
\end{equation}
Hence exact scalar-channel associativity is equivalent to the single scalar
condition
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{z_3=1.}
 \label{eq:v27-associativity-z1}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The cross operator $T_3$ commutes with the complex standard $S_4$ action.
The complex standard representation $W=[31]_{\mathbb C}$ is irreducible, so
Schur's lemma gives $T_3=z_3I_W$.  Since $F_L,F_R$ are isometries,
$\|T_3\|_{\rm op}\le1$, hence $|z_3|\le1$.

If $K_3F_L=F_LK_{\rm ren}$ and $K_3F_R=F_RK_{\rm ren}$ for the degree-three
antiunitary real structure $K_3$, then $T_3$ commutes with complex conjugation.
For $T_3=z_3I$ this is equivalent to $z_3=\overline{z_3}$, proving
\eqref{eq:v27-z-real}.

Finally,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathfrak A_{\rm sc}^*\mathfrak A_{\rm sc}
 &=F_L^*F_L+F_R^*F_R-F_L^*F_R-F_R^*F_L\\
 &=2I_W-T_3^*-T_3
 =2(1-\Re z_3)I_W.
 \end{aligned}
\]
On the real-descent branch $z_3$ is real.  Since $\dim_{\mathbb C}W=3$,
its complex trace is $6(1-z_3)$.  A positive operator of the displayed form
vanishes exactly when $z_3=1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Range equality is weaker than associativity]
If $|z_3|=1$, the two isometries have the same range.  But the physical fusion
maps agree only when $z_3=1$.  In particular the real-descent value $z_3=-1$
represents the same source plane with the opposite fusion map and gives the
maximal scalar-channel associator trace $12$.  This distinction is why the
triple gate cannot be replaced by a projector-range test.
\end{remark}

\section{Fresh visible triple occurrence also collapses to one scalar}
\label{sec:v27-fresh-triple}

The V26 arithmetic-visible cubic transport module is the tangent standard
module itself: after the parallel Fubini--Study compiler, the only intrinsic
cubic transport field is $d\alpha\otimes P_{\rm sc}$, whose coefficient lives
in $W_{\mathbb R}^*$.  Compress any fresh degree-three occurrence innovation
to the corresponding complex standard channel and denote its positive Gram by
$N_{3,W}^{\rm vis}$.

\begin{theorem}[One-scalar visible triple innovation]
\label{thm:v27-triple-innovation-scalar}
Assume $N_{3,W}^{\rm vis}$ is positive Hermitian, $S_4$-equivariant, and
complex-linear with respect to the V21 complex structure.  Then there is a
unique $\beta_3\ge0$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{N_{3,W}^{\rm vis}=\beta_3I_W,}
 \label{eq:v27-N-beta}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \beta_3=\frac13\Tr_{\mathbb C}N_{3,W}^{\rm vis}.}
 \label{eq:v27-beta-trace}
\end{equation}
Thus the absence of any fresh arithmetic-visible triple source on this channel
is equivalent to the single scalar condition
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\beta_3=0.}
 \label{eq:v27-beta-zero}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By complex $S_4$ equivariance and irreducibility of $W$, Schur's lemma gives
$N_{3,W}^{\rm vis}=\lambda I_W$.  Hermiticity makes $\lambda$ real and
positivity gives $\lambda\ge0$.  Put $\beta_3=\lambda$ and take the complex
trace.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Triplet-sized freshness]
\label{cor:v27-triplet-freshness}
On the complex standard channel, fresh visible degree-three occurrence is
all-or-nothing:
\[
 \rank_{\mathbb C}N_{3,W}^{\rm vis}
 =\begin{cases}
 0,&\beta_3=0,\\
 3,&\beta_3>0.
 \end{cases}
\]
After realification the corresponding ranks are $0$ and $6$.
\end{corollary}

\section{The symmetric-base cubic card uses only two scalar triple reads}
\label{sec:v27-two-scalar-card}

At the V21 reference law, \Cref{thm:v27-alpha-gradient-zero} removes the
transport contribution from the V26 card.  Under the common
$S_4$--complex--real hypotheses above, define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 z_3:=\frac13\Tr_{\mathbb C}(F_R^*F_L),
 \qquad
 \beta_3:=\frac13\Tr_{\mathbb C}N_{3,W}^{\rm vis}.}
 \label{eq:v27-two-reads}
\end{equation}
The first number is a same-history mixed overlap of the two parenthesized
fusion channels; the second is the total fresh visible triple innovation per
complex standard dimension.

\begin{theorem}[Two-scalar strong cubic certificate at the symmetric base law]
\label{thm:v27-two-scalar-certificate}
On the exact V25 branch and under the symmetry hypotheses of
\Cref{thm:v27-associator-one-parameter,thm:v27-triple-innovation-scalar},
the V26 arithmetic-visible cubic card at the tetrahedrally symmetric Store
base point is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak C_{3,0}^{\rm vis}
 =6(1-z_3)+3\beta_3.}
 \label{eq:v27-C3-two-scalars}
\end{equation}
Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak C_{3,0}^{\rm vis}=0
 \iff
 z_3=1
 \ \text{and}\ 
 \beta_3=0.}
 \label{eq:v27-C3-exact}
\end{equation}
Thus a complete matrix-valued triple audit is unnecessary for the
arithmetic-visible cubic channel once the common symmetry, complex structure,
and real descent have been independently established.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{thm:v27-alpha-gradient-zero}, $\|d\alpha_0\|^2=0$.  The associator
trace is $6(1-z_3)$ by \eqref{eq:v27-associator-trace}, and the visible fresh
innovation trace is $3\beta_3$ by \eqref{eq:v27-beta-trace}.  Both summands
are nonnegative because $z_3\le1$ and $\beta_3\ge0$.  Their sum vanishes
exactly when both vanish.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[One pass/fail scalar versus two diagnostic scalars]
The nonnegative sum in \eqref{eq:v27-C3-two-scalars} is one scalar certificate
for the binary question of exact cubic coherence.  Keeping $z_3$ and
$\beta_3$ separately is operationally preferable because it distinguishes
parenthesization failure from genuinely fresh triple occurrence.
\end{remark}

\section{Sharp nonidentifiability even after imposing all current symmetries}
\label{sec:v27-nonidentifiability}

The reduction to two numbers does not make those numbers inferable from V25.
The following construction strengthens the V26 firewall by preserving the
full $S_4$ action, complex structure, and real descent.

\begin{theorem}[Every $(z_3,\beta_3)$ is compatible with identical lower-grade data]
\label{thm:v27-two-parameter-nonidentifiability}
Fix the complete V25 one- and two-occurrence data.  For every
\[
 z\in[-1,1],
 \qquad
 \beta\ge0,
\]
there exists a degree-three extension with the same lower-grade packet and the
same diagonal $S_4$, complex, and real structures such that
\[
 z_3=z,
 \qquad
 \beta_3=\beta.
\]
Therefore neither scalar can be deduced from the complete V25 data, even after
all current representation-theoretic reductions.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Take
\[
 H_3^{\rm vis}=W\oplus W\oplus W
\]
with diagonal $S_4$ action, diagonal complex structure, and componentwise
conjugation.  Define
\[
 F_Lx=(x,0,0),
 \qquad
 F_Rx=(zx,\sqrt{1-z^2}\,x,0).
\]
Both maps are equivariant real-compatible complex isometries and
\[
 F_R^*F_L=zI_W.
\]
Add an orthogonal fresh triple synthesis
\[
 G_\beta x=(0,0,\sqrt\beta\,x).
\]
Its Gram is $G_\beta^*G_\beta=\beta I_W$.  All modifications occur first in
degree three, so every degree-one and degree-two source, fusion, action, and
occurrence datum is unchanged.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Minimal acquisition boundary]
\label{cor:v27-minimal-acquisition}
Under the V27 symmetry hypotheses, the first complete arithmetic-visible
triple decision requires no unrestricted degree-three Gram reconstruction.
It requires only:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item one mixed overlap scalar $z_3$ between the two parenthesized scalar--tangent
      fusion channels;
\item one nonnegative innovation trace $\beta_3$ on the visible complex
      standard channel.
\end{enumerate}
No lower-grade calculation can replace these two actual degree-three
occurrence reads.
\end{corollary}

\section{Automatic first-order stability after an exact symmetric-base pass}
\label{sec:v27-first-order-stability}

There is one further consequence which matters for finite acquisition.  Let
$z_3(p)$ and $\beta_3(p)$ vary smoothly with the physical base law while the
V27 symmetry reduction remains valid.  The contraction and positivity bounds
hold pointwise:
\[
 z_3(p)\le1,
 \qquad
 \beta_3(p)\ge0.
\]

\begin{proposition}[Exact base-point coherence has no linear drift]
\label{prop:v27-no-linear-drift}
If at an interior base point $p_0$
\[
 z_3(p_0)=1,
 \qquad
 \beta_3(p_0)=0,
\]
and $z_3,\beta_3$ are differentiable there, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{dz_3|_{p_0}=0,
 \qquad
 d\beta_3|_{p_0}=0.}
 \label{eq:v27-zbeta-grad-zero}
\end{equation}
Together with \Cref{thm:v27-alpha-gradient-zero}, every term in the strong
cubic card has zero first derivative at an exact symmetric-base pass.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The function $z_3$ has a local maximum at $p_0$ because $z_3\le1$, while
$\beta_3$ has a local minimum because $\beta_3\ge0$.  Differentiability at an
interior extremum forces the gradients to vanish.  The statement for
$\alpha$ is \Cref{thm:v27-alpha-gradient-zero}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Quadratic onset of triple-coherence drift]
\label{cor:v27-quadratic-onset}
If the three scalar fields are $C^2$ and the exact V27 base-point gate passes,
then along every smooth tangent direction $v$,
\[
 1-z_3(tv)=O(t^2),
 \qquad
 \beta_3(tv)=O(t^2),
 \qquad
 \alpha(tv)-\alpha(0)=O(t^2).
\]
Thus the first nontrivial neighborhood obstruction after an exact symmetric
base-point pass is second order in source displacement.
\end{corollary}

\section{Why the next step is transport rather than another occurrence grade}
\label{sec:v28-context}

V27 reduced the arithmetic-visible degree-three entrance at the tetrahedrally

\[
 \alpha,\qquad z_3,\qquad \beta_3,
\]
with arithmetic base values
\[
 \alpha(0)=\frac{21}{2},\qquad z_3(0)=1,\qquad \beta_3(0)=0.
\]
The first is the V25 scalar quadratic-occurrence coefficient, the second is
the scalar overlap of the two parenthesized scalar--tangent fusion channels,
and the third is the fresh visible triple-innovation coefficient.  V27 proved
that all three have zero first derivative after an exact symmetric-base pass.
The remaining question is therefore whether one should continue to measure
higher jets of these functions or instead search for a structural transport
law.

This continuation proves three facts.  First, the second-order drift is highly
compressed by the already established tetrahedral, real, and complex
structures.  Second, no finite jet order, however high, can prove neighborhood
constancy of the three scalar fields.  Third, an exact finite transport packet
for the quadratic occurrence and the two degree-three fusion channels does
propagate one exact base-point pass to a whole connected physical family.  The
third statement is the structural transport theorem requested at the end of
V27 and is the point at which the intrinsic occurrence tower should stop.

\section{Invariant Hessians on the complex tetrahedral source}
\label{sec:v28-hessian-commutant}

Write the V21 real source as
\[
 W_{\mathbb R}\cong W_0\otimes\mathbb R^2,
\]
where $W_0=[31]_{\mathbb R}$ is the real three-dimensional standard
representation of $S_4$.  Let
\[
 J=I_{W_0}\otimes
 \begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 K=I_{W_0}\otimes
 \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}
\]
be, respectively, the V21 complex structure and renewal real structure.  Let
$g$ be the fixed $S_4$-invariant Euclidean metric.

\begin{theorem}[Complete Hessian commutant hierarchy]
\label{thm:v28-hessian-commutant}
Let $H$ be a real symmetric bilinear form on $W_{\mathbb R}$ which is
$S_4$-invariant.  Then there is a unique real symmetric $2\times2$ matrix
$S$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 H=I_{W_0}\otimes S.}
 \label{eq:v28-H-S2}
\end{equation}
Consequently the space of $S_4$-invariant Hessians has dimension three.
If in addition
\[
 H(Kx,Ky)=H(x,y),
\]
then $S$ is diagonal and the invariant Hessian space has dimension two.  If
instead, or in addition,
\[
 H(Jx,Jy)=H(x,y),
\]
then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{H=c\,g}
 \label{eq:v28-H-scalar}
\end{equation}
for one real number $c$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The real standard representation $W_0$ is absolutely irreducible, so
\[
 \operatorname{End}_{S_4}(W_0)=\mathbb R I_{W_0}.
\]
Hence
\[
 \operatorname{End}_{S_4}(W_{\mathbb R})
 =I_{W_0}\otimes M_2(\mathbb R).
\]
Using $g$ to identify symmetric bilinear forms with self-adjoint
endomorphisms, $S_4$-invariance therefore gives
$H=I_{W_0}\otimes S$ with $S=S^T$, proving the first statement.

Let $K_2=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$.  The $K$-invariance condition is
$K_2^TSK_2=S$, which kills the off-diagonal entry of $S$.  Let
$J_2=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$.  The
$J$-invariance condition is $J_2^TSJ_2=S$.  For a real symmetric $S$ this is
equivalent to $S=cI_2$.  This proves all claims.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One second-order coefficient per scalar on the complex branch]
\label{cor:v28-one-hessian-coefficient}
Let $f$ be any one of $\alpha,z_3,\beta_3$ on a physical branch on which the
scalar read is $S_4$-invariant and its second derivative is compatible with
the V21 complex structure.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{D^2f_0=c_f g}
 \label{eq:v28-D2-scalar}
\end{equation}
for one real coefficient $c_f$.
If the exact V27 base gate passes, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{c_{z}\le0,\qquad c_{\beta}\ge0,}
 \label{eq:v28-signs}
\end{equation}
while $c_{\alpha}$ has no sign constraint from positivity alone.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply \Cref{thm:v28-hessian-commutant}.  Since $z_3\le1$ and
$z_3(0)=1$, the origin is a local maximum of $z_3$, hence its Hessian is
negative semidefinite and $c_z\le0$.  Similarly $\beta_3\ge0$ and
$\beta_3(0)=0$ make the origin a local minimum, giving $c_\beta\ge0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{scope}[What is and is not assumed]
The $S_4$ reduction is forced by tetrahedral covariance.  The further
collapse from three Hessian coefficients to one uses compatibility of the
second-order scalar read with the V21 complex structure.  This is a physical
branch condition, not a consequence of bare $S_4$ symmetry.  If only the V21
real structure is certified, two diagonal second-order coefficients remain;
if only $S_4$ is certified, three remain.  V28 never silently promotes a
complex source coordinate into a physical quarter-turn symmetry.
\end{scope}

\section{A one-ray finite card for the complete second-order drift}
\label{sec:v28-second-order-card}

Assume now the complex-compatible branch of
\Cref{cor:v28-one-hessian-coefficient}.  For a unit tangent $v\in W_{\mathbb R}$
define the central second difference
\begin{equation}
 d_{2,h}f(v)
 :=\frac{f(hv)-2f(0)+f(-hv)}{h^2}.
 \label{eq:v28-central-second}
\end{equation}

\begin{proposition}[One ray determines the isotropic Hessian coefficient]
\label{prop:v28-one-ray}
If $f$ is $C^4$ at the origin and $D^2f_0=c_fg$, then for every unit $v$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{d_{2,h}f(v)=c_f+O(h^2).}
 \label{eq:v28-one-ray-asymptotic}
\end{equation}
Thus, after the symmetry hypotheses have been independently certified, one
physical radial pair $\pm hv$ per scalar is sufficient to determine the
complete quadratic drift.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Taylor expansion in the one-dimensional parameter $t$ gives
\[
 f(tv)=f(0)+t\,df_0[v]+\frac{t^2}{2}D^2f_0[v,v]
 +\frac{t^3}{6}D^3f_0[v,v,v]+O(t^4).
\]
Adding the $+h$ and $-h$ expressions cancels the odd terms.  Since
$D^2f_0[v,v]=c_f$ for $\|v\|=1$, division by $h^2$ proves the claim.
\end{proof}

Define the second-order neighborhood card
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak D_2
 :=c_{\alpha}^{\,2}-c_z+c_\beta\ \ge0.}
 \label{eq:v28-D2-card}
\end{equation}

\begin{corollary}[Three-scalar second-order pass]
\label{cor:v28-D2-pass}
On an exact V27 base-point pass and on the complex-compatible branch,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak D_2=0
 \iff
 c_\alpha=0,\quad c_z=0,\quad c_\beta=0.}
 \label{eq:v28-D2-exact}
\end{equation}
Thus all second-order neighborhood drift is decided by three real numbers,
and each number can be obtained from one symmetric radial pair.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use \eqref{eq:v28-signs}.  Each summand in
\eqref{eq:v28-D2-card} is nonnegative, so the sum vanishes exactly when all
three do.
\end{proof}

\section{Finite-jet closure is impossible}
\label{sec:v28-finite-jet-firewall}

The reduction above is useful diagnostically, but it does not justify an
infinite sequence of V29, V30, \ldots{} derivative tests.  The next theorem
shows why.

\begin{theorem}[No finite jet can certify neighborhood constancy]
\label{thm:v28-no-finite-jet}
Fix any integer $m\ge2$.  There exist real-analytic scalar fields on a
neighborhood of $0\in W_{\mathbb R}$ of the form
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \alpha_m(z)&=\frac{21}{2}+a\|z\|^{2m},\\
 z_{3,m}(z)&=1-b\|z\|^{2m},\\
 \beta_{3,m}(z)&=c\|z\|^{2m},
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:v28-flat-finite-jets}
\end{equation}
with $a\in\mathbb R$ and $b,c\ge0$, which preserve $S_4$, the complex
structure, the real structure, and the pointwise bounds
$z_{3,m}\le1$, $\beta_{3,m}\ge0$, yet agree with the constant arithmetic
values through every derivative of order $<2m$ at the origin.
For nonzero $a$, $b$, or $c$ the corresponding field is nevertheless
nonconstant on every neighborhood of the origin.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The norm $\|z\|^2$ is invariant under the full orthogonal group and hence
under all current source symmetries.  Its $m$th power is a homogeneous
polynomial of degree $2m$, so every derivative of order strictly less than
$2m$ vanishes at the origin.  The sign restrictions on $b,c$ give the required
pointwise contraction and positivity bounds.  Nonzero coefficients make the
fields nonconstant.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Upstream stopping rule]
\label{cor:v28-stop-jets}
No finite collection of base-point derivative cards can prove the neighborhood
identities
\[
 \alpha\equiv\frac{21}{2},\qquad
 z_3\equiv1,\qquad
 \beta_3\equiv0.
\]
Even real analyticity does not make any \emph{fixed finite jet} sufficient.
Accordingly, after the second-order card one should search for a structural
transport law rather than continue climbing the local jet tower.
\end{corollary}

\section{Finite transport propagation of the complete arithmetic-visible packet}
\label{sec:v28-transport}

The Grand-Tensor programme consistently separates physical source transport
from quantities reconstructed after transport \cite{GT77}.  We now specialize
that principle to the V25--V27 arithmetic-visible packet.

Let $\mathcal G=(\mathcal V,\mathcal E)$ be a connected graph of physically
occurring neighboring Store laws.  At each vertex $p$ let
\[
 W_p\cong\mathbb C^3
\]
be the acquired complex standard tangent source, let
\[
 N_{2,p}=\alpha_pP_{{\rm sc},p}
\]
be the V25 quadratic occurrence Gram on the scalar K\"ahler line, let
\[
 F_{L,p},F_{R,p}:W_p\to H_{3,p}^{\rm vis}
\]
be the two V27 parenthesized scalar--tangent fusion isometries, and let
\[
 N_{3,p}=\beta_p I_{W_p}
\]
be the fresh visible triple-innovation Gram.

For an oriented edge $e:p\to q$, let
\[
 U_e:W_p\to W_q,
 \qquad
 V_e:H_{3,p}^{\rm vis}\to H_{3,q}^{\rm vis}
\]
be unitary physical transports, with $U_e$ complex-linear and $S_4$-equivariant.
Let $\widehat U_e$ denote the induced unitary on the real symmetric-square
source, so that
\[
 \widehat U_eP_{{\rm sc},p}\widehat U_e^*=P_{{\rm sc},q}.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Exact finite transport closure]
\label{thm:v28-exact-transport-closure}
Assume that on every edge $e:p\to q$ the following four physical transport
rectangles close:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 N_{2,q}&=\widehat U_eN_{2,p}\widehat U_e^*,\\
 F_{L,q}U_e&=V_eF_{L,p},\\
 F_{R,q}U_e&=V_eF_{R,p},\\
 N_{3,q}&=U_eN_{3,p}U_e^*.
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:v28-four-transport-rectangles}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \alpha_q=\alpha_p,
 \qquad
 z_{3,q}=z_{3,p},
 \qquad
 \beta_q=\beta_p.}
 \label{eq:v28-edge-constant}
\end{equation}
Hence all three scalar fields are constant on the connected graph.
In particular, if one vertex satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \alpha=\frac{21}{2},
 \qquad z_3=1,
 \qquad\beta_3=0,}
 \label{eq:v28-one-base-pass}
\end{equation}
then every vertex does.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first identity in \eqref{eq:v28-four-transport-rectangles} and the
transport of $P_{\rm sc}$ give
\[
 \alpha_qP_{{\rm sc},q}
 =\alpha_pP_{{\rm sc},q},
\]
so $\alpha_q=\alpha_p$.

Let $T_{3,p}=F_{R,p}^*F_{L,p}=z_{3,p}I_{W_p}$.  The two fusion rectangles give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 U_e^*T_{3,q}U_e
 &=U_e^*F_{R,q}^*F_{L,q}U_e\\
 &=(V_eF_{R,p})^*(V_eF_{L,p})\\
 &=F_{R,p}^*F_{L,p}=T_{3,p}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Since both cross operators are scalar, $z_{3,q}=z_{3,p}$.
Finally the last rectangle reads
$\beta_qI=\beta_pI$ after unitary conjugation, hence
$\beta_q=\beta_p$.  Connectivity propagates the equalities from any base
vertex to all vertices.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Structural closure of the intrinsic arithmetic source geometry]
\label{cor:v28-geometric-closure}
Suppose the vertices of $\mathcal G$ exhaust a connected physical source
neighborhood and the hypotheses of V26's nonlinear closure theorem hold at
each vertex.  If the four transport rectangles
\eqref{eq:v28-four-transport-rectangles} close on a connected transport graph
and one vertex passes \eqref{eq:v28-one-base-pass}, then the intrinsic Store
source geometry is locally Fubini--Study throughout that physical neighborhood.
No higher intrinsic occurrence or curvature coefficient is required.
\end{corollary}

\section{Approximate transport and a finite stability bound}
\label{sec:v28-approx-transport}

The exact theorem has a quantitative finite-card version.  On an edge
$e:p\to q$ define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \delta_{2,e}&:=
 \|N_{2,q}-\widehat U_eN_{2,p}\widehat U_e^*\|_{\HS}^2,\\
 \delta_{L,e}&:=\|F_{L,q}U_e-V_eF_{L,p}\|_{\HS}^2,\\
 \delta_{R,e}&:=\|F_{R,q}U_e-V_eF_{R,p}\|_{\HS}^2,\\
 \delta_{3,e}&:=\|N_{3,q}-U_eN_{3,p}U_e^*\|_{\HS}^2.
 \end{aligned}}
 \label{eq:v28-edge-residuals}
\end{equation}
Their sum
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak T_e
 :=\delta_{2,e}+\delta_{L,e}+\delta_{R,e}+\delta_{3,e}\ge0}
 \label{eq:v28-transport-card}
\end{equation}
is one nonnegative edgewise transport card.

\begin{theorem}[Sharp scalar drift bounds from transport residuals]
\label{thm:v28-transport-stability}
On the V27 scalar-reduced branch,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 |\alpha_q-\alpha_p|=\sqrt{\delta_{2,e}},}
 \label{eq:v28-alpha-drift}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 |z_{3,q}-z_{3,p}|
 \le
 \frac{\sqrt{\delta_{L,e}}+\sqrt{\delta_{R,e}}}{\sqrt3},}
 \label{eq:v28-z-drift}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 |\beta_q-\beta_p|
 =\sqrt{\frac{\delta_{3,e}}{3}}.}
 \label{eq:v28-beta-drift}
\end{equation}
Consequently, along any path $p_0\to p_1\to\cdots\to p_m$ the drift from
$p_0$ is bounded by the sum of the corresponding edgewise right-hand sides.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Because $P_{{\rm sc},q}$ is rank one and is exactly transported,
\[
 N_{2,q}-\widehat U_eN_{2,p}\widehat U_e^*
 =(\alpha_q-\alpha_p)P_{{\rm sc},q},
\]
and $\|P_{{\rm sc},q}\|_{\HS}=1$, proving
\eqref{eq:v28-alpha-drift}.

Put
\[
 A=F_{R,q}U_e,\quad B=F_{L,q}U_e,
 \quad C=V_eF_{R,p},\quad D=V_eF_{L,p}.
\]
All four maps have operator norm one.  Since
\[
 U_e^*T_{3,q}U_e-T_{3,p}=A^*B-C^*D,
\]
we have
\[
 \|A^*B-C^*D\|_{\HS}
 \le\|B-D\|_{\HS}+\|A-C\|_{\HS}
 =\sqrt{\delta_{L,e}}+\sqrt{\delta_{R,e}}.
\]
But the left-hand side equals
$\sqrt3\,|z_{3,q}-z_{3,p}|$, proving
\eqref{eq:v28-z-drift}.
Finally
\[
 N_{3,q}-U_eN_{3,p}U_e^*
 =(\beta_q-\beta_p)I_{W_q},
\]
whose Hilbert--Schmidt norm is
$\sqrt3|\beta_q-\beta_p|$, proving
\eqref{eq:v28-beta-drift}.  The path estimate is the triangle inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[A spanning tree is sufficient]
\label{cor:v28-spanning-tree}
For a finite connected family of physical laws, exact vanishing of
$\mathfrak T_e$ on the edges of any spanning tree, together with one exact
base-point pass, propagates the arithmetic values of
$(\alpha,z_3,\beta_3)$ to every sampled law.  Approximate edge cards give the
corresponding path-sum error bars from
\Cref{thm:v28-transport-stability}.
\end{corollary}

\section{V28 status and next noncircular attack}
\label{sec:v28-status}

V28 resolves the question raised at the end of V27 in two stages.
At the symmetric base law, second-order drift is already tiny in
representation-theoretic complexity:
\[
 \boxed{
 D^2\alpha_0=c_\alpha g,
 \qquad
 D^2z_{3,0}=c_zg,
 \qquad
 D^2\beta_{3,0}=c_\beta g}
\]
on the complex-compatible branch, with
$c_z\le0$ and $c_\beta\ge0$.  Thus one radial pair per scalar determines the
complete quadratic drift.  However
\Cref{thm:v28-no-finite-jet} proves that continuing to higher local jets can
never establish neighborhood constancy from any fixed finite order.

The correct upstream replacement is finite physical transport.  The complete
arithmetic-visible neighborhood packet is
\begin{equation}
\boxed{
\begin{gathered}
N_2=\alpha P_{\rm sc},\qquad
F_L,F_R:W\to H_3^{\rm vis},\qquad
N_3=\beta I_W,\\
\Downarrow\quad\text{physical neighboring-law transports}\quad\Downarrow\\
\delta_2,\ \delta_L,\ \delta_R,\ \delta_3.
\end{gathered}}
\label{eq:v28-final-packet}
\end{equation}
If these four transport residuals vanish on a connected physical neighborhood,
one exact V27 base-point pass propagates
\[
 \boxed{
 \alpha\equiv\frac{21}{2},
 \qquad
 z_3\equiv1,
 \qquad
 \beta_3\equiv0.}
\]
V26 then closes the intrinsic Fubini--Study source geometry, and no further
intrinsic occurrence grade should be introduced.

The next noncircular attack is therefore:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(N\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item acquire one genuine neighboring-law transport rectangle for the V25
      scalar occurrence source and the two V27 parenthesized fusion channels;
\item compute the four nonnegative residuals in
      \eqref{eq:v28-edge-residuals};
\item if they vanish, extend the same transport to a spanning set of the
      physical source neighborhood rather than measuring higher base-point
      derivatives;
\item if the transport packet closes and the base-point gate passes, stop the
      intrinsic source-geometry tower and return downstream to
      transfer/Krylov and Frobenius--Wilson;
\item if a residual is positive, retain it as the exact primitive transport
      obstruction.  Do not compensate it by changing the already fixed
      Fubini--Study source metric or the V25 scalar occurrence normalization.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Version integrity.}
All V1--V27 mathematical bodies and status ledgers are preserved byte for
byte.  V28 adds only the invariant-Hessian classification, the one-ray
second-order card, the finite-jet no-go theorem, the exact finite transport
closure theorem, and its quantitative edgewise stability bounds above.
Future continuations must follow this block.

\part*{V29 continuation: native transport compilation, determinant-oriented holonomy collapse, and the external-source firewall}
\addcontentsline{toc}{part}{V29 continuation: native transport compilation, determinant-oriented holonomy collapse, and the external-source firewall}

\section{Why V28 must be audited one layer upstream}
\label{sec:v29-upstream}

V28 reduced neighborhood closure to four physical transport rectangles for
\[
 N_2=\alpha P_{\rm sc},\qquad
 F_L,F_R:W\to H_3^{\rm vis},\qquad
 N_3=\beta I_W.
\]
It is essential not to promote these four rows to independent primitives before
asking whether some of them are already functorial consequences of the finite
history algebra.  The Grand-Tensor transport theorem gives exactly the needed
criterion: a unitary source transport with vanishing finite word-level monoidal
residual is the $L^2$ extension of a trace-preserving unital $*$-isomorphism
\cite{GT77}.  On the other hand, the same monograph proves that flat linear
holonomy alone need not be monoidal.  We now specialize those facts to the
arithmetic-visible packet.

The outcome is a dichotomy.  Native occurrence objects are transported for
free once the finite monoidal card vanishes; genuinely external occurrence
objects are not determined by that card at all.  Separately, the already
identified $S_4$, complex, real, and determinant structures collapse the
possible source holonomy from $U(1)$ to the identity.

\section{Naturality of the finite native compiler}
\label{sec:v29-native-compiler}

Let $\mathcal A_p,\mathcal A_q$ be finite source-generated unital
$C^*$-history algebras with faithful trace, and let
\[
 \mathcal U:L^2(\mathcal A_p)\longrightarrow L^2(\mathcal A_q)
\]
be a unitary whose finite flat-depth monoidal residual
$\mathbb I_{\rm mon}(\mathcal U)$ is the one defined in the inherited
word-level transport theorem.  Thus
\[
 \mathbb I_{\rm mon}(\mathcal U)=0
\]
if and only if $\mathcal U$ is induced by a trace-preserving unital
$*$-isomorphism $\varphi:\mathcal A_p\to\mathcal A_q$.

We call a finite source construction \emph{native} if, on a fixed-rank branch,
it is obtained from the declared represented source generators by finitely many
applications of:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item algebra products, adjoints, and finite linear combinations;
\item tensor, symmetric, or exterior powers;
\item Gram formation and inverse or inverse square root on an already certified
      positive block;
\item orthogonal projection onto a represented source range;
\item Anderson--Trapp/Schur shorting by a represented source range.
\end{enumerate}
No new external Read is permitted in this definition.

\begin{lemma}[Unitary naturality of projections and shorts]
\label{lem:v29-short-naturality}
Let $U:H\to H'$ be unitary, let $A:E\to H$ be injective, and put
\[
 P_A=A(A^*A)^{-1}A^*.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{UP_AU^*=P_{UA}.}
 \label{eq:v29-projection-naturality}
\]
If $G\succeq0$ and $\operatorname{Short}_{\operatorname{Ran}A}(G)$ denotes the
positive short of $G$ to $\operatorname{Ran}A$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 U\,\operatorname{Short}_{\operatorname{Ran}A}(G)\,U^*
 =\operatorname{Short}_{\operatorname{Ran}(UA)}(UGU^*).}
 \label{eq:v29-short-naturality}
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The projection identity follows by direct substitution:
\[
 P_{UA}=UA\bigl(A^*U^*UA\bigr)^{-1}A^*U^*=UP_AU^*.
\]
The positive short is characterized as the maximal positive operator $X$ with
$0\preceq X\preceq G$ and $\operatorname{Ran}X\subseteq\operatorname{Ran}A$.
Unitary conjugation preserves positivity, order, range inclusion, and maximality,
which proves \eqref{eq:v29-short-naturality}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Native transport compiler]
\label{thm:v29-native-transport-compiler}
Assume $\mathbb I_{\rm mon}(\mathcal U)=0$ and that $\mathcal U$ maps the
declared primitive typed source generators at $p$ to their declared partners at
$q$.  Then every native finite construction $\mathfrak F$ satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal U\,\mathfrak F_p\,\mathcal U^*=\mathfrak F_q}
 \label{eq:v29-native-functoriality}
\]
with the obvious induced tensor-power unitary when $\mathfrak F$ acts on a
tensor, symmetric, or exterior carrier.

Consequently, if the V25 scalar occurrence line, the two V27 parenthesized
fusion channels, and the V27 fresh visible triple innovation are native in this
sense, all four V28 transport rectangles are consequences of one finite
monoidal transport certificate and are not independent physical rows.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Vanishing of $\mathbb I_{\rm mon}$ makes $\mathcal U$ the $L^2$ extension of a
trace-preserving unital $*$-isomorphism.  Hence it commutes exactly with
products, involution, and all finite $*$-polynomials.  Tensor, symmetric, and
exterior functors are algebraic and therefore commute with the induced unitary.
Gram matrices are unchanged because $\mathcal U$ is unitary; positive inverses
and inverse square roots therefore intertwine.  Projection and shorting
naturality are \Cref{lem:v29-short-naturality}.  Induction over the finite
construction tree proves \eqref{eq:v29-native-functoriality}.

For the V25--V27 packet, $P_{\rm sc}$ is a native projection once the complex
source and its metric are represented; product fusion is native by monoidality;
and every connected innovation obtained by orthogonal shorting of a complete
represented panel is native by \Cref{lem:v29-short-naturality}.  Therefore the
corresponding restrictions of $\mathcal U$ give the four V28 rectangles.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[What the theorem does not assume]
\label{rem:v29-native-not-occurrence}
\Cref{thm:v29-native-transport-compiler} is not an occurrence theorem.  It does
not prove that the V25 scalar occurrence or V27 triple source is represented by
old histories.  It says only that \emph{if} such a source is already represented
and is obtained by the fixed native compiler, then its transport need not be
measured again independently.
\end{remark}

\section{External occurrence transport is not inferable from the old algebra}
\label{sec:v29-external-firewall}

\begin{theorem}[External-source transport nonidentifiability]
\label{cth:v29-external-source-transport}
There are two extended transport systems with identical old history algebras,
identical primitive old-source transport, identical vanishing monoidal residual,
and identical old path holonomy, but different transport of one additional
external occurrence source.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Take any finite source-generated history algebra $\mathcal A$ and the identity
transport on $L^2(\mathcal A)$.  Adjoin one orthogonal external source line
$E=\mathbb C\nu$ which is not in the represented history algebra.  On
$L^2(\mathcal A)\oplus E$ define
\[
 \widetilde U_+=I\oplus I_E,
 \qquad
 \widetilde U_-=I\oplus(-I_E).
\]
Both extensions restrict to the same identity $*$-isomorphism on
$L^2(\mathcal A)$, hence have the same zero monoidal residual and the same old
holonomy.  Yet
\[
 \widetilde U_+\nu=\nu,
 \qquad
 \widetilde U_-\nu=-\nu.
\]
Thus the external source rectangle is not determined by any old word-level
transport datum.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact reopening criterion for the V28 rectangles]
\label{cor:v29-v28-dichotomy}
For each V28 source row there are only two logically distinct cases:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the row is native to the represented typed history/connected-panel
      compiler, in which case zero monoidal residual transports it exactly;
\item the row contains a genuinely external occurrence source, in which case
      its transport is independent acquisition data.
\end{enumerate}
No amount of further calculation inside the old history algebra can turn case
\textup{(b)} into case \textup{(a)}.
\end{corollary}

\section{Holonomy collapse of the structured arithmetic-visible source}
\label{sec:v29-holonomy-collapse}

We now treat the global path ambiguity independently of monoidality.  Let
$W_p\cong\mathbb C^3$ be the complex standard $S_4$ source at a physical law
$p$, with complex structure $J_p$, antiunitary real structure $K_p$, and, when
available, an oriented nonzero determinant vector
$\omega_p\in\Lambda^3_{\mathbb C}W_p$.

Let $H_c:W_p\to W_p$ be the unitary holonomy around a closed physical loop $c$.
Assume the edge transports preserve the stated structures, so the loop holonomy
commutes with the $S_4$ action and with $J_p$, and, on the real branch, with
$K_p$.

\begin{theorem}[Holonomy hierarchy $U(1)\to\mathbb Z_2\to\{1\}$]
\label{thm:v29-holonomy-hierarchy}
On the complex standard source $W_p$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item $S_4$-equivariance and complex linearity imply
      \[
       \boxed{H_c=\lambda_cI_W,\qquad |\lambda_c|=1.}
       \label{eq:v29-u1-holonomy}
      \]
\item if $H_cK_p=K_pH_c$, then
      \[
       \boxed{\lambda_c\in\{+1,-1\}.}
       \label{eq:v29-z2-holonomy}
      \]
\item if in addition the oriented determinant source is preserved,
      $\Lambda^3H_c\,\omega_p=\omega_p$, then
      \[
       \boxed{H_c=I_W.}
       \label{eq:v29-trivial-holonomy}
      \]
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The complexified standard representation of $S_4$ is irreducible.  Schur's
lemma therefore gives $H_c=\lambda_cI$, and unitarity gives
$|\lambda_c|=1$.  Since $K_p$ is anti-linear,
\[
 K_p(\lambda_cv)=\overline{\lambda_c}K_pv.
\]
Commutation with $K_p$ forces
$\lambda_c=\overline{\lambda_c}$, proving
\eqref{eq:v29-z2-holonomy}.  Finally
\[
 \Lambda^3H_c=\lambda_c^3I_{\Lambda^3W}.
\]
For $\lambda_c\in\{\pm1\}$ and complex dimension three, preservation of the
oriented determinant vector forces $\lambda_c^3=1$, hence $\lambda_c=1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Discrete real-holonomy gap]
\label{cor:v29-holonomy-gap}
On the real-compatible branch,
\[
 \boxed{
 \|I-H_c\|_{\HS}^2\in\{0,12\}.}
 \label{eq:v29-holonomy-gap}
\]
Thus a nontrivial exact loop defect cannot be arbitrarily small.  If the
oriented determinant source is also preserved, the nonzero value is excluded.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If $H_c=I$ the defect is zero.  If $H_c=-I$ on a complex three-dimensional
space, then $I-H_c=2I$ and
\[
 \|2I\|_{\HS}^2=4\operatorname{Tr}I=12.
\]
The final statement is \Cref{thm:v29-holonomy-hierarchy}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[No independent source-holonomy audit after oriented descent]
\label{cor:v29-no-loop-audit}
Suppose a connected physical source bundle carries exact $S_4$ covariance,
complex structure, renewal real descent, and a transported oriented determinant
source.  Then every closed-path holonomy on the arithmetic-visible tangent
source is the identity.  Once those structures are independently certified,
path independence of the tangent source does not require an additional loop
measurement.
\end{corollary}

\section{Monoidality and linear flatness are independent gates}
\label{sec:v29-independence}

The preceding holonomy theorem must not be confused with monoidal transport.
The inherited Grand-Tensor countertheorem already gives a cycle with identity
linear holonomy and nonzero edgewise monoidal residual \cite{GT77}.  The reverse
independence is equally elementary.

\begin{theorem}[Monoidal transport need not be linearly flat]
\label{cth:v29-monoidal-not-flat}
There is a closed transport loop with zero word-level monoidal residual on every
edge but nontrivial linear holonomy.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Take $\mathcal A=\mathbb C^3$ with normalized trace and let $P$ be a nontrivial
coordinate permutation.  The induced unitary on $L^2(\mathcal A)$ is a
trace-preserving unital $*$-automorphism, so its monoidal residual vanishes.
Use one loop edge whose transport is $P$.  The closed-path holonomy is $P\ne I$.
Thus monoidality does not imply linear flatness.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Two logically distinct transport questions]
\label{cor:v29-two-transport-questions}
Before the determinant-oriented descent is imposed, a complete transport audit
has two independent parts:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item a local finite monoidal/source-nativity question on the edges;
\item a global linear holonomy question on cycles.
\end{enumerate}
On the structured arithmetic-visible branch of
\Cref{cor:v29-no-loop-audit}, the second part collapses identically and only the
first remains.
\end{corollary}

\section{A one-card native closure theorem}
\label{sec:v29-one-card}

For a physical edge $e:p\to q$ on a fixed flat-depth branch, define the scalar
finite monoidal card
\[
 \boxed{
 \mu_e:=\operatorname{Tr}\mathbb I_{\rm mon}(\mathcal U_e)\ge0.}
 \label{eq:v29-monoidal-card}
\]
Because $\mathbb I_{\rm mon}\succeq0$,
\[
 \mu_e=0\iff \mathbb I_{\rm mon}(\mathcal U_e)=0.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Native neighborhood closure from one finite edge card]
\label{thm:v29-native-neighborhood-closure}
Assume on a connected physical source graph that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item the V25 scalar occurrence and V27 visible triple packet are native finite
      constructions from the represented typed history/connected-panel data;
\item the physical edge transport maps the primitive typed generators and has
      $\mu_e=0$ on every edge of a connected spanning subgraph;
\item the $S_4$, complex, renewal-real, and oriented determinant structures are
      transported exactly;
\item one base vertex passes
      \[
       \alpha=\frac{21}{2},\qquad z_3=1,\qquad\beta_3=0.
      \]
\end{enumerate}
Then all four V28 transport rectangles close on that spanning subgraph, the
arithmetic-visible tangent holonomy is trivial on every loop, and
\[
 \boxed{
 \alpha\equiv\frac{21}{2},\qquad z_3\equiv1,\qquad\beta_3\equiv0}
 \label{eq:v29-global-packet}
\]
throughout the connected physical family.  Under the V26 hypotheses, the
intrinsic Store source geometry is therefore locally Fubini--Study throughout
the family.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{thm:v29-native-transport-compiler}, $\mu_e=0$ compiles every V28
rectangle on each spanning edge.  V28 then propagates the three scalar values
from the base vertex to every vertex.  By
\Cref{thm:v29-holonomy-hierarchy}, the structured tangent transport has trivial
holonomy, so the propagated identification is path independent.  The V26
closure theorem then gives the local Fubini--Study source geometry.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Why this is not an unconditional closure]
\label{fire:v29-native-closure}
\Cref{thm:v29-native-neighborhood-closure} applies only after the occurrence
packet is shown to be native to the represented typed history/connected-panel
compiler.  If the V25 scalar occurrence or the V27 fresh triple source is an
external Read, \Cref{cth:v29-external-source-transport} applies and its
transport row remains independent physical data.  The theorem does not allow
one to declare an external occurrence native merely because doing so would
close the arithmetic branch.
\end{remark}

\section{V29 status and next noncircular attack}
\label{sec:v29-status}

V29 turns the V28 transport problem into an occurrence-nativity decision.
There is no longer a reason to acquire four separate transport rectangles

\Downarrow\\[-0.3em]
\text{V28/V26 neighborhood closure.}
\end{gathered}}
\label{eq:v29-final-dichotomy}
\end{equation}

The next noncircular attack is therefore upstream and finite:
