\section{A signed channel twirl dynamically compiles the native pseudoscalar (V39)}
\label{sec:v39-signed-channel-twirl}

\subsection{Aim: replace a specially aligned channel by one scalar overlap}
V38 ended with a deliberately strict dynamic entrance: one should acquire a
forward/reverse CPTP tangent whose Hamiltonian projection is already of the
form $a_{\rm ps}C_{22}$.  The inherited channel-native calculus is more
flexible than that.  It supplies actual two-sided differentiated channels and
represented tetrahedral relabellings, while the V38 pseudoscalar $C_{22}$ is
itself word-native.  The remaining question is therefore whether an arbitrary
physical Hamiltonian tangent on the same five-axis carrier can be projected
\emph{operationally}, rather than algebraically after the fact, onto the unique
sign line.

V39 proves that it can.  The sign-isotypic Hamiltonian subspace on the
five-axis carrier is one-dimensional.  Consequently one real derivative
coefficient decides whether an arbitrary actual channel contains the missing
V37--V38 mode.  If that coefficient is nonzero, a finite signed tetrahedral
twirl built only from the actual forward/reverse pair and represented
relabelings produces the required pseudoscalar tangent.  Negative coefficients
never appear in a convex channel mixture: the minus sign is supplied by the
\emph{physical reverse branch}.  Thus V38's dynamic entrance reduces from a
specially aligned channel to one same-history two-sided channel plus one scalar
nonorthogonality test.

\subsection{The sign-isotypic Hamiltonian line is unique}
Let
\[
 E_5^{\mathbb C}=W_3^{\mathbb C}\oplus W_2^{\mathbb C}
 \cong [31]\oplus[22]
\]
be the complexified V36--V38 five-axis carrier, with tetrahedral action
$U_g$.  Let $\mathfrak h_0(E_5)$ denote its real Hilbert space of traceless
Hermitian operators with Hilbert--Schmidt inner product.  Conjugation gives an
orthogonal $S_4$ action
\(
 H\mapsto U_gHU_g^*.
\)

\begin{theorem}[There is exactly one tetrahedral sign Hamiltonian]
\label{thm:v39-unique-sign-Hamiltonian}
The sign-isotypic subspace of $\mathfrak h_0(E_5)$ is one-dimensional and is
spanned by the V38 self-twist $C_{22}=i\Omega_{\rm ps}$:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak h_0(E_5)^{\rm sgn}
 =\mathbb R C_{22}.}
 \tag{V39.1}\label{eq:v39-sign-line}
\end{equation}
Equivalently,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \dim\operatorname{Hom}_{S_4}
 \bigl(\operatorname{sgn},\operatorname{End}(E_5^{\mathbb C})\bigr)=1.}
 \tag{V39.2}\label{eq:v39-sign-multiplicity}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By tensor--Hom adjunction,
\[
 \operatorname{Hom}_{S_4}
 \bigl(\operatorname{sgn},\operatorname{End}(E_5^{\mathbb C})\bigr)
 \cong
 \operatorname{Hom}_{S_4}
 \bigl(E_5^{\mathbb C}\otimes\operatorname{sgn},E_5^{\mathbb C}\bigr).
\]
Now
\[
 E_5^{\mathbb C}\otimes\operatorname{sgn}
 \cong [211]\oplus[22],
 \qquad
 E_5^{\mathbb C}\cong[31]\oplus[22].
\]
Only the $[22]$ summands agree, each with multiplicity one.  Hence the complex
intertwiner space has dimension one.  V38 supplies the nonzero Hermitian
sign-covariant operator $C_{22}$, so its real Hermitian span is exactly the
sign-isotypic line.  Since $C_{22}$ is traceless, the line lies in
$\mathfrak h_0(E_5)$.
\end{proof}

Define the sign Reynolds operator on Hermitian five-axis operators by
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Pi_{\rm ps}(H)
 :=\frac1{24}\sum_{g\in S_4}
 \operatorname{sgn}(g)\,U_gHU_g^*.}
 \tag{V39.3}\label{eq:v39-sign-Reynolds}
\end{equation}

\begin{corollary}[One scalar reconstructs the complete pseudoscalar component]
\label{cor:v39-one-scalar-Hamiltonian}
The map $\Pi_{\rm ps}$ is the Hilbert--Schmidt orthogonal projection onto
$\mathbb RC_{22}$ and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Pi_{\rm ps}(H)
 =a_{\rm ps}(H)C_{22},
 \qquad
 a_{\rm ps}(H)
 =\frac12\Tr(C_{22}H).}
 \tag{V39.4}\label{eq:v39-H-coefficient}
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|\Pi_{\rm ps}(H)\|_{\rm HS}^2
 =2a_{\rm ps}(H)^2.}
 \tag{V39.5}\label{eq:v39-H-projection-norm}
\end{equation}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The usual character Reynolds operator is an orthogonal projector onto the
corresponding isotype.  Apply \Cref{thm:v39-unique-sign-Hamiltonian}.  V38 gives
$\Tr C_{22}^2=2$, so the orthogonal projection coefficient is
$\Tr(C_{22}H)/2$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The coefficient is directly visible at channel level}
Let $d=5$ and let
\[
 \mathscr D_H(X):=-i[H,X]
\]
denote the Hamiltonian derivation on $M_d(\mathbb C)$.  Equip superoperators
with the real Hilbert--Schmidt pairing
\(
 \langle\mathcal A,\mathcal B\rangle_{\rm sup}
 :=\Re\Tr_{\rm sup}(\mathcal A^*\mathcal B).
\)
For traceless Hermitian $A,B$ one has
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \langle\mathscr D_A,\mathscr D_B\rangle_{\rm sup}
 =2d\,\Tr(AB).}
 \tag{V39.6}\label{eq:v39-derivation-pairing}
\end{equation}

Let $\mathcal L$ be an arbitrary Hermiticity-preserving physical tangent and
write its inherited canonical orthogonal decomposition as
\[
 \mathcal L=\mathscr D_{H_{\mathcal L}}+\mathcal D_{\perp},
 \qquad
 \mathcal D_{\perp}\perp
 \{\mathscr D_H:H=H^*,\ \Tr H=0\}.
\]

\begin{theorem}[A single differentiated channel scalar detects dynamic promotion]
\label{thm:v39-channel-scalar}
The V38 pseudoscalar coefficient of the canonical Hamiltonian projection is
obtainable directly from the channel tangent:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 a_{\rm ps}(\mathcal L)
 =\frac1{4d}
 \langle\mathscr D_{C_{22}},\mathcal L\rangle_{\rm sup}
 =\frac1{20}
 \langle\mathscr D_{C_{22}},\mathcal L\rangle_{\rm sup}.}
 \tag{V39.7}\label{eq:v39-channel-coefficient}
\end{equation}
Thus one marked derivative correlation, together with the inherited
Hamiltonian-tangent residual, is enough to decide whether the actual channel
has a nonzero pseudoscalar component.  Full Hamiltonian tomography is not
required for this decision.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Orthogonality of the canonical Hamiltonian projection gives
\[
 \langle\mathscr D_{C_{22}},\mathcal L\rangle_{\rm sup}
 =\langle\mathscr D_{C_{22}},\mathscr D_{H_{\mathcal L}}\rangle_{\rm sup}.
\]
Apply \eqref{eq:v39-derivation-pairing} and then
\eqref{eq:v39-H-coefficient}:
\[
 \langle\mathscr D_{C_{22}},\mathcal L\rangle_{\rm sup}
 =2d\Tr(C_{22}H_{\mathcal L})
 =4d\,a_{\rm ps}(\mathcal L).
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Generic but not forced]
\label{rem:v39-generic-not-forced}
The map
\(
 H\mapsto a_{\rm ps}(H)
\)
is a nonzero real linear functional because $a_{\rm ps}(C_{22})=1$.  Hence
its zero set is a codimension-one hyperplane in the traceless Hermitian
Hamiltonian space.  A nonzero pseudoscalar component is therefore generic, but
not representation-theoretically forced.  In particular, a connected-support
Hamiltonian can still have $a_{\rm ps}=0$: any real symmetric connected
Hamiltonian is Hilbert--Schmidt orthogonal to the purely imaginary Hermitian
operator $C_{22}$.  Thus the inherited channel-native condition of connected
Hamiltonian support does not by itself close the V38 gate.
\end{remark}

\subsection{A physical signed twirl compiles the pseudoscalar tangent}
The preceding projection is algebraic.  The key point is that a two-sided
physical channel pair realizes it without negative channel weights.

Assume actual CPTP curves $\Phi_+(t),\Phi_-(t)$ through the identity satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \Phi_\pm(0)=\operatorname{id},
 \qquad
 \Phi_+'(0)=\mathcal L_+,
 \qquad
 \Phi_-'(0)=\mathcal L_-.
 \tag{V39.8}\label{eq:v39-two-sided-tangent}
\end{equation}
For each tetrahedral relabelling define the conjugated physical channel
\[
 \Phi_{g,\pm}(t)
 :=\operatorname{Ad}_{U_g}\circ
   \Phi_\pm(t)\circ
   \operatorname{Ad}_{U_g^{-1}}.
\]
Choose any ordering $g_1,\ldots,g_{24}$ of $S_4$ and set
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Psi_h
 :=\Phi_{g_{24},\epsilon_{24}}(h/24)\circ\cdots\circ
   \Phi_{g_1,\epsilon_1}(h/24),
 \qquad
 \epsilon_j=\begin{cases}
 +,&\operatorname{sgn}(g_j)=+1,\\
 -,&\operatorname{sgn}(g_j)=-1.
 \end{cases}}
 \tag{V39.9}\label{eq:v39-physical-signed-twirl}
\end{equation}
Every factor is CPTP for $h\ge0$.

\begin{theorem}[Tetrahedral reverse-branch compiler]
\label{thm:v39-physical-twirl}
The differentiated compiled channel is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Psi_0'
 =\frac1{24}\left(
 \sum_{g\ {
m even}}\operatorname{Ad}_{U_g}^{\rm sup}(\mathcal L_+)
 +\sum_{g\ {
m odd}}\operatorname{Ad}_{U_g}^{\rm sup}(\mathcal L_-)
 \right).}
 \tag{V39.10}\label{eq:v39-compiled-derivative}
\end{equation}
If the forward/reverse derivatives are exact opposites,
\(
 \mathcal L_-=-\mathcal L_+=-\mathcal L,
\)
then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Psi_0'=\Pi_{\rm ps}^{\rm sup}(\mathcal L),}
 \tag{V39.11}\label{eq:v39-super-sign-projector}
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
 \Pi_{\rm ps}^{\rm sup}(\mathcal L)
 :=\frac1{24}\sum_g
 \operatorname{sgn}(g)\,
 \operatorname{Ad}_{U_g}^{\rm sup}(\mathcal L).
 \tag{V39.12}\label{eq:v39-super-Reynolds}
\end{equation}
If moreover $\mathcal L=\mathscr D_H$ is Hamiltonian, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Psi_0'
 =\mathscr D_{\Pi_{\rm ps}(H)}
 =\mathscr D_{a_{\rm ps}(H)C_{22}}.}
 \tag{V39.13}\label{eq:v39-compiled-pseudoscalar}
\end{equation}
Consequently an arbitrary actual two-sided Hamiltonian tangent with
$a_{\rm ps}\ne0$ dynamically promotes the V38 pseudoscalar after a finite
24-step tetrahedral compiler.  No specially aligned microscopic channel is
required.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Differentiate the finite product at $h=0$.  Since every factor equals the
identity there, the derivative is the sum of the $24$ conjugated derivatives,
with the common factor $1/24$, giving
\eqref{eq:v39-compiled-derivative}.  Exact reversal turns the odd sum into the
negative odd conjugates, which is precisely the sign Reynolds projector.
Finally
\[
 \operatorname{Ad}_{U_g}^{\rm sup}(\mathscr D_H)
 =\mathscr D_{U_gHU_g^*},
\]
so \Cref{cor:v39-one-scalar-Hamiltonian} gives
\eqref{eq:v39-compiled-pseudoscalar}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Robustness to imperfect reversal and non-Hamiltonian tangent noise]
\label{cor:v39-twirl-robustness}
Let
\[
 \varepsilon_{\rm rev}
 :=\|\mathcal L_++\mathcal L_-\|_{\rm sup,HS},
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_{\rm Ham}
 :=\operatorname{dist}_{\rm sup,HS}
 \bigl(\mathcal L_+,\{\mathscr D_H\}\bigr).
\]
Then the compiled derivative satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{dist}_{\rm sup,HS}
 \bigl(\Psi_0',\mathbb R\mathscr D_{C_{22}}\bigr)
 \le
 \varepsilon_{\rm Ham}
 +\frac12\varepsilon_{\rm rev}.}
 \tag{V39.14}\label{eq:v39-robustness-bound}
\end{equation}
If the channel second derivatives are uniformly bounded, the finite compiled
channel has the corresponding pseudoscalar generator with $O(h^2)$ local
channel error; the inherited noisy direct/Klein compilation may then be used
exactly as in the channel-native Grand-Tensor branch.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The ideal sign Reynolds operator is an orthogonal projection in superoperator
Hilbert space and preserves the Hamiltonian-derivation subspace by covariance,
so it cannot increase the distance to that subspace.  Replacing the ideal odd
derivative $-\mathcal L_+$ by $\mathcal L_-$ changes
\eqref{eq:v39-compiled-derivative} by
\[
 \frac1{24}\sum_{g\ {
m odd}}
 \operatorname{Ad}_{U_g}^{\rm sup}
 (\mathcal L_-+\mathcal L_+).
\]
There are twelve odd elements and unitary conjugation preserves the norm, so
this contribution is bounded by $\varepsilon_{\rm rev}/2$.  On the
Hamiltonian subspace, \Cref{thm:v39-unique-sign-Hamiltonian} reduces the sign
projection to $\mathbb R\mathscr D_{C_{22}}$.  The finite-time statement is the
ordinary product expansion together with the inherited bounded-second-
derivative channel estimates.
\end{proof}

\subsection{What the inherited channel-native branch does and does not settle}
The Grand-Tensor channel-native finite-SM branch already supplies the correct
\emph{kind} of physical input: a forward/reverse CPTP pair through the identity,
a canonical Hamiltonian projection, reversal and tangent residuals, and noisy
refocusing \cite{GT77}.  V39 therefore removes the need for a new
``pseudoscalar-shaped'' channel primitive.

What the supplied material does not establish is that the already acquired
channel-native pair acts on the same resolved five-axis carrier on which
$C_{22}$ and the V33 Clifford packet are represented.  Nor does connected
Hamiltonian support force the scalar \eqref{eq:v39-channel-coefficient} to be
nonzero.  These are same-history occurrence questions.

\begin{theorem}[The V38 dynamic gate reduces to one incidence plus one scalar]
\label{thm:v39-reduced-dynamic-gate}
Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(V39.\arabic*)},leftmargin=3.5em]
\item an actual forward/reverse CPTP pair through the identity acts on the
      represented five-axis carrier;
\item the tetrahedral relabellings $U_g$ are executable on that same carrier;
\item the inherited tangent/reversal residuals vanish;
\item the single channel coefficient
      \(
       a_{\rm ps}=(20)^{-1}
       \langle\mathscr D_{C_{22}},\mathcal L_+\rangle_{\rm sup}
      \)
      is nonzero.
\end{enumerate}
Then the physical compiler \eqref{eq:v39-physical-signed-twirl} produces the
V38 pseudoscalar Hamiltonian tangent and hence the full missing $SO(2)$ axis
factor.  Combined with the V36--V37 $SO(3)$ curvature branch, both arithmetic
prime conjugacy classes are spectrally reachable.

Conversely, if $a_{\rm ps}=0$, this entire tetrahedral signed compiler has zero
pseudoscalar output from that channel tangent.  No additional conjugation of
the same tangent by the represented tetrahedral group can change that fact;
one must acquire another physical tangent or another genuine operation source.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The forward implication is \Cref{thm:v39-physical-twirl} followed by
\Cref{thm:v38-dynamic-promotion,cor:v38-two-angle-repair}.  For the converse,
all tetrahedral conjugates of a Hamiltonian $H$ have sign projection
$\operatorname{sgn}(g)a_{\rm ps}(H)C_{22}$ by covariance.  If
$a_{\rm ps}(H)=0$, their entire linear span has zero sign projection.  Hence no
compiler using only those conjugates and their physical reverse branches can
produce a nonzero element of the sign Hamiltonian line at first order.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Revised stopping rule after V39}
V38's dynamic-occurrence problem is now smaller than previously stated:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{array}{c}
 \text{same-history two-sided CPTP tangent on }E_5\\
 +\ \text{represented tetrahedral relabellings}\\
 \Downarrow\\
 a_{\rm ps}=\frac1{20}
 \langle\mathscr D_{C_{22}},\mathcal L_+\rangle_{\rm sup}\\
 \Downarrow\\
 a_{\rm ps}\ne0
 \ \Longrightarrow\ 
 \text{finite signed twirl}\ \Longrightarrow\ SO(2)\\
 \Downarrow\\
 SO(3)\times SO(2)\ \Longrightarrow\
 \text{V34--V35 Wilson character card}.
 \end{array}}
 \tag{V39.15}\label{eq:v39-decision-tree}
\end{equation}

Thus no new pseudoscalar-shaped physical channel has to be postulated.  The
minimal new physical information is:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(V39.\alph*)},leftmargin=3.5em]
\item the same-history placement of one already legitimate two-sided channel
      tangent on the five-axis carrier; and
\item one real derivative overlap $a_{\rm ps}$.
\end{enumerate}
If these pass, dynamic promotion is compiled from the existing tetrahedral
operations.  If the same-history placement is absent, or every acquired
physical tangent has $a_{\rm ps}=0$, the branch remains dynamically
unpopulated.  More static parity, grading or tetrahedral moments cannot decide
that occurrence question.

The downstream Clifford--router incidence and the V31 labelled lag packet are
unchanged.  V39 only removes an unnecessarily strong entrance assumption at
the pseudoscalar stage.

\section{Multiplicity-free source incidence canonically places the channel on the five-axis carrier (V40)}
\label{sec:v40-five-axis-incidence}

\subsection{Aim: replace an unspecified fibre identification by one source-overlap scalar}
V39 reduced the missing pseudoscalar dynamics to an actual two-sided channel
acting on the same five-axis carrier as the native operator $C_{22}$.  The
remaining phrase ``acting on the same carrier'' should itself be given an
operational finite certificate.  The inherited joint-source theorem already
provides the correct language: a same-history mixed source Gram determines the
normalized cross transport, its singular values are principal-angle cosines,
and vanishing mutual Schur residuals are equivalent to equality of the two
source ranges \cite{GT77}.

The tetrahedral five-axis carrier is especially rigid.  It is the
multiplicity-free real representation
\[
 E_5=W_3\oplus W_2\cong [31]\oplus[22],
 \qquad \dim W_3=3,\quad \dim W_2=2.
\]
V40 proves that on a common tetrahedrally covariant history the entire relative
placement of a locked five-axis source and a channel source core is therefore
controlled by two scalar cross coefficients.  One positive scalar decides
whether their ranges coincide.  On that coincidence branch, every residual
source-frame ambiguity commutes with the V38--V39 pseudoscalar $C_{22}$, so
both the pseudoscalar coefficient and the signed channel compiler are
placement invariant.  Thus no additional orientation or phase acquisition is
needed between the source-incidence gate and V39.

\subsection{The normalized cross transport has only two blocks}
Let $\sigma:S_4\to O(E_5)$ be the V36 tetrahedral five-axis action and let
$P_3,P_2$ be the orthogonal projectors onto $W_3=[31]$ and $W_2=[22]$.
Suppose two full-rank source families occur on one common history,
\[
 S_{\rm ax}:E_5\to\mathcal H,
 \qquad
 S_{\rm ch}:E_5\to\mathcal H,
\]
with positive marginal Grams
\[
 G_{\rm ax}=S_{\rm ax}^*S_{\rm ax},
 \qquad
 G_{\rm ch}=S_{\rm ch}^*S_{\rm ch},
\]
and mixed block
\[
 C=S_{\rm ch}^*S_{\rm ax}.
\]
Whiten the two families:
\[
 V_{\rm ax}=S_{\rm ax}G_{\rm ax}^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 V_{\rm ch}=S_{\rm ch}G_{\rm ch}^{-1/2},
\]
so both $V$'s are isometries, and define the normalized cross transport
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 T:=V_{\rm ch}^*V_{\rm ax}
 =G_{\rm ch}^{-1/2}CG_{\rm ax}^{-1/2}.}
 \tag{V40.1}\label{eq:v40-cross-transport}
\end{equation}
Assume the two source families carry the same represented tetrahedral action,
\[
 U_gV_{\rm ax}=V_{\rm ax}\sigma(g),
 \qquad
 U_gV_{\rm ch}=V_{\rm ch}\sigma(g).
\]

\begin{theorem}[Multiplicity-free five-axis cross transport]
\label{thm:v40-two-block-cross}
The normalized cross transport is a contraction and has the exact form
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 T=z_3P_3+z_2P_2,
 \qquad |z_3|\le1,\quad |z_2|\le1.}
 \tag{V40.2}\label{eq:v40-two-block-form}
\end{equation}
If the common real descent is also retained, then $z_3,z_2\in[-1,1]$.
The two mutual Schur innovations have ranks in the set
\[
 \boxed{\{0,2,3,5\},}
\]
and, after whitening, are
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 I-T^*T
 =(1-|z_3|^2)P_3+(1-|z_2|^2)P_2.}
 \tag{V40.3}\label{eq:v40-whitened-innovation}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The inherited joint-source theorem makes $T=V_{\rm ch}^*V_{\rm ax}$ a
contraction.  Equivariance gives
\[
 \sigma(g)T=T\sigma(g)
\]
for every $g$.  Since $[31]$ and $[22]$ are inequivalent irreducibles and each
occurs with multiplicity one, Schur's lemma gives
$T=z_3P_3+z_2P_2$.  Contractivity gives the two modulus bounds.  A common
antiunitary real structure sends each scalar to its complex conjugate and
commutes with $T$, so the scalars are real on that branch.  The innovation
formula is immediate, and its rank is the sum of $3$ when $|z_3|<1$ and $2$
when $|z_2|<1$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{One positive scalar decides exact placement}
Define the normalized same-history incidence overlap
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \kappa_{\rm inc}
 :=\frac15\Tr(T^*T)
 =\frac{3|z_3|^2+2|z_2|^2}{5}.}
 \tag{V40.4}\label{eq:v40-kappa-inc}
\end{equation}
Equivalently, if
$\Pi_{\rm ax}=V_{\rm ax}V_{\rm ax}^*$ and
$\Pi_{\rm ch}=V_{\rm ch}V_{\rm ch}^*$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \kappa_{\rm inc}
 =\frac15\Tr(\Pi_{\rm ax}\Pi_{\rm ch}).}
 \tag{V40.5}\label{eq:v40-projector-overlap}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[One-scalar exact incidence certificate]
\label{thm:v40-one-scalar-incidence}
One has
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{0\le\kappa_{\rm inc}\le1,}
 \tag{V40.6}\label{eq:v40-kappa-bounds}
\end{equation}
and the following are equivalent:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \kappa_{\rm inc}=1
 &\iff |z_3|=|z_2|=1\\
 &\iff T\text{ is unitary}\\
 &\iff \operatorname{Ran} S_{\rm ax}=\operatorname{Ran} S_{\rm ch}\\
 &\iff R_{{\rm ax}\mid{\rm ch}}
       =R_{{\rm ch}\mid{\rm ax}}=0.
 \end{aligned}}
 \tag{V40.7}\label{eq:v40-incidence-equivalences}
\end{equation}
Moreover the projector distance is exactly
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|\Pi_{\rm ax}-\Pi_{\rm ch}\|_{\rm HS}^2
 =10(1-\kappa_{\rm inc}).}
 \tag{V40.8}\label{eq:v40-projector-distance}
\end{equation}
Thus one positive same-history scalar decides whether the five-axis channel
core is the locked five-axis source range.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first inequality follows from contractivity.  Since both terms in
\[
 5(1-\kappa_{\rm inc})
 =3(1-|z_3|^2)+2(1-|z_2|^2)
\]
are nonnegative, equality $\kappa_{\rm inc}=1$ holds exactly when both vanish.
The remaining equivalences are the inherited mutual-range theorem.  Finally,
for rank-five projections,
\[
 \|\Pi_{\rm ax}-\Pi_{\rm ch}\|_{\rm HS}^2
 =10-2\Tr(\Pi_{\rm ax}\Pi_{\rm ch}),
\]
which is \eqref{eq:v40-projector-distance}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Quantitative principal-angle control from the same scalar]
\label{cor:v40-incidence-robustness}
If
\(
 \kappa_{\rm inc}=1-\varepsilon
\)
with $0\le\varepsilon\le2/5$, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 1-|z_3|^2\le\frac{5}{3}\varepsilon,
 \qquad
 1-|z_2|^2\le\frac{5}{2}\varepsilon,}
 \tag{V40.9}\label{eq:v40-block-defect-bounds}
\end{equation}
and the largest principal angle $\theta_{\max}$ between the two source ranges
obeys
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sin\theta_{\max}
 \le\sqrt{\frac52\varepsilon}.}
 \tag{V40.10}\label{eq:v40-angle-bound}
\end{equation}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Each nonnegative summand of
$3(1-|z_3|^2)+2(1-|z_2|^2)=5\varepsilon$ is bounded by the total.  The five
principal-angle cosines are $|z_3|$ with multiplicity three and $|z_2|$ with
multiplicity two, so
$\sin^2\theta_{\max}=1-\min\{|z_3|^2,|z_2|^2\}$ and the second bound follows.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The pseudoscalar is invariant under every residual placement ambiguity}
On the exact incidence branch let
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 T=e^{i\phi_3}P_3+e^{i\phi_2}P_2.}
 \tag{V40.11}\label{eq:v40-unitary-commutant}
\end{equation}
The phases reduce to signs under real descent.  Recall that the V38--V39
pseudoscalar satisfies
\[
 C_{22}=P_2C_{22}P_2,
 \qquad
 C_{22}^2=P_2.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Placement independence of the pseudoscalar channel coefficient]
\label{thm:v40-pseudoscalar-placement-invariance}
On the exact incidence branch,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 TC_{22}T^*=C_{22},
 \qquad
 T\Omega_{\rm ps}T^*=\Omega_{\rm ps}.}
 \tag{V40.12}\label{eq:v40-C22-invariant}
\end{equation}
Suppose an ambient same-history tangent $\widetilde{\mathcal L}$ preserves the
common rank-five source algebra and let $\mathcal L_{\rm ch}$ and
$\mathcal L_{\rm ax}$ be its pullbacks through $V_{\rm ch}$ and
$V_{\rm ax}$ respectively.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal L_{\rm ax}
 =\operatorname{Ad}_{T^*}^{\rm sup}
   \circ\mathcal L_{\rm ch}
   \circ\operatorname{Ad}_{T}^{\rm sup}.}
 \tag{V40.13}\label{eq:v40-pullback-conjugacy}
\end{equation}
Consequently the V39 differentiated pseudoscalar coefficient is identical in
both placements:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 a_{\rm ps}(\mathcal L_{\rm ax})
 =a_{\rm ps}(\mathcal L_{\rm ch}).}
 \tag{V40.14}\label{eq:v40-aps-invariant}
\end{equation}
The V39 signed Reynolds compiler is likewise conjugate through $T$ and has the
same physical output coefficient.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Since $T$ is scalar on $W_2$ and $C_{22},\Omega_{\rm ps}$ are supported on
$W_2$, the two conjugation identities are immediate.  Equality of the source
ranges gives $V_{\rm ax}=V_{\rm ch}T$.  If
$\iota_a(X)=V_aXV_a^*$, then
\[
 \iota_{\rm ax}(X)=\iota_{\rm ch}(TXT^*).
\]
Compressing the same ambient tangent through the two isometries gives
\eqref{eq:v40-pullback-conjugacy}.  The V39 channel coefficient is the
superoperator Hilbert pairing with $\mathscr D_{C_{22}}$; unitary conjugation
preserves that pairing and \eqref{eq:v40-C22-invariant} fixes the marked
pseudoscalar derivation.  This proves \eqref{eq:v40-aps-invariant}.  The same
argument commutes with every tetrahedral conjugation in the signed Reynolds
sum.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[No new orientation bit is needed at the placement gate]
\label{rem:v40-no-orientation-bit}
The two residual phases in \eqref{eq:v40-unitary-commutant} are genuine frame
ambiguities of the two inequivalent tetrahedral irreducibles.  They do not act
on $C_{22}$ by conjugation.  In particular, even on the real branch the four
possible sign choices
$\pm P_3\pm P_2$ give the same pseudoscalar operator.  Thus the placement gate
needs range equality, not an additional orientation calibration.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Multiplicity saturation gives an even stronger zero-acquisition branch}
The one-scalar incidence card is necessary only when the common carrier has
room for more than one copy of a relevant isotype.

\begin{corollary}[Multiplicity-one saturation closes placement automatically]
\label{cor:v40-multiplicity-saturation}
Suppose the common physical carrier contains the standard and two-dimensional
tetrahedral isotypes with multiplicities exactly one:
\[
 \mathcal H_{[31]\oplus[22]}
 \cong [31]\oplus[22].
\]
Then every $S_4$-equivariant full-rank five-axis source has the same range.
Hence
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\kappa_{\rm inc}=1}
 \tag{V40.15}\label{eq:v40-saturation-kappa}
\end{equation}
identically and no mixed incidence measurement is needed.  This applies in
particular when the actual two-sided channel is already represented directly
on the canonical six-edge contrast carrier
$\mathbf1_6^\perp=[31]\oplus[22]$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
With multiplicity one, the complete isotypic subspace of each type is the
unique carrier for that irreducible.  A full-rank equivariant copy of
$[31]\oplus[22]$ must therefore exhaust both isotypic subspaces, so all such
source ranges coincide.
\end{proof}

\subsection{What is and is not settled by the inherited channel-native theorem}
The inherited channel-native construction already gives the exact mechanism
needed after placement.  Given a source-fixing isometry
$C:\mathbb C^5\to\mathcal H_F$, its source-core leakage and Hamiltonian tangent
residual decide whether an ambient forward/reverse CPTP pair induces a genuine
two-sided Hamiltonian tangent on the encoded five-dimensional matrix algebra
\cite{GT77}.  V40 identifies the missing entrance to that theorem:

\begin{theorem}[Reduced same-history channel-placement gate]
\label{thm:v40-reduced-placement-gate}
Assume the locked five-axis source and a rank-five channel source core are
jointly visible and carry the same tetrahedral action.  Then the complete
placement entrance required by V39 is equivalent to the single scalar
condition
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\kappa_{\rm inc}=1.}
 \tag{V40.16}\label{eq:v40-placement-gate}
\end{equation}
On that branch the inherited source-fixing encoder is unique up to the
commutant \eqref{eq:v40-unitary-commutant}, and that entire ambiguity fixes
$C_{22}$.  Therefore the next physical test is directly the V39 scalar
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 a_{\rm ps}
 =\frac1{20}
 \langle\mathscr D_{C_{22}},\mathcal L_+\rangle_{\rm sup},}
 \tag{V40.17}\label{eq:v40-next-aps}
\end{equation}
with no intervening fibre-orientation gate.

If no same-history mixed source block exists from which
$\kappa_{\rm inc}$ can be obtained, separate five-axis and channel marginals
do not determine placement.  The correct status is then ``incidence
unpopulated'', not ``aligned by representation type''.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The exact placement equivalence is \Cref{thm:v40-one-scalar-incidence}.  The
inherited joint-source uniqueness supplies the source-fixing identification.
\Cref{thm:v40-pseudoscalar-placement-invariance} removes its commutant
ambiguity from the marked pseudoscalar and channel coefficient.  The final
sentence is the ordinary joint-source nonidentifiability firewall: source
marginals alone do not determine the mixed Gram.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Revised stopping rule after V40}
The V39 placement problem has therefore split into two sharply distinguished
branches:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{array}{c}
 \textbf{multiplicity-one common carrier}\\
 \Downarrow\\
 \text{placement automatic}\\[1mm]
 \textbf{or}\\[1mm]

 \kappa_{\rm inc}=\frac15\Tr(\Pi_{\rm ax}\Pi_{\rm ch})\stackrel?=1

 a_{\rm ps}\stackrel?\ne0

 SO(2).
\]
Thus V40 removes the need for an unspecified five-dimensional fibre
identification or orientation convention.  The only genuinely new
same-history information is the source incidence itself; on the common

The next noncircular attack should therefore be an audit of the inherited

\section{The pseudoscalar channel needs only the centered matching core (V41)}
\label{sec:v41-matching-core}

\subsection{Aim: remove the unnecessary five-dimensional channel entrance}
V40 formulated the same-history placement problem using a full
$E_5=[31]\oplus[22]$ channel source.  An audit of the inherited channel-native
entrance shows that this is stronger than what is currently supplied and
stronger than what the V38--V39 pseudoscalar compiler actually needs.  The
literal primitive four-cell score bank supplies standard triplets, while the
locked $K_4$ cut--cycle packet supplies a standard triplet and its
orientation-twisted triplet; the inherited channel-native tangent theorem is
parametric in a chosen logical source core and does not itself identify a
five-dimensional $[31]\oplus[22]$ core \cite{GT77}.  Thus the
multiplicity-one automatic branch of V40 is not presently inherited as a
channel occurrence.

The missing V37 mode, however, is supported entirely on the two-dimensional
$[22]$ summand.  V41 proves that this summand is already the centered matching
coordinate of the literal Store half-edge record, that its tetrahedral action
factors through $S_3$, and that the V39 twenty-four-step signed twirl compresses
exactly to a six-step physical twirl on a two-dimensional channel core.  Full
$[31]$ channel placement is irrelevant for this purpose.

\subsection{The $[22]$ axis plane is exactly the centered matching coordinate}
Order the six undirected edges as
\[
 (12),(13),(14),(23),(24),(34)
\]
and the three perfect matchings as
\[
 m_1=\{12,34\},\qquad
 m_2=\{13,24\},\qquad
 m_3=\{14,23\}.
\]
Let $f_a\in\mathbb R^6$ be the indicator vector of $m_a$ and define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 F:\mathbb R^3\longrightarrow\mathbb R^6,
 \qquad
 Fe_a=\frac1{\sqrt2}f_a.}
 \tag{V41.1}\label{eq:v41-matching-isometry}
\end{equation}
Let
\[
 P_{\mathsf M}=I_3-\frac13\one_3\one_3^{\mathsf T}
\]
be the centered matching projector and let $P_{22}$ be the tetrahedral
$[22]$ projector in the six-edge permutation representation.

\begin{theorem}[Centered matching realization of the two-dimensional axis source]
\label{thm:v41-centered-matching-22}
The map $F$ is an $S_4$-equivariant isometry and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 F^*F=I_3,
 \qquad
 FP_{\mathsf M}F^*=P_{22}.}
 \tag{V41.2}\label{eq:v41-matching-projector}
\end{equation}
Consequently
\[
 W_{\mathsf M}:=\one_3^\perp
\]
is a canonical normalized copy of $[22]$, and its image under $F$ is exactly
the $W_2=[22]$ summand of the V36--V40 five-axis carrier.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The three perfect matchings partition the six edges into three disjoint pairs,
so $f_a^*f_b=2\delta_{ab}$ and hence $F^*F=I_3$.  Moreover
\[
 F\one_3=\frac1{\sqrt2}\one_6,
\]
so $F$ maps the uniform matching line onto the uniform edge line and maps its
orthogonal complement into $E_5=\one_6^\perp$.  Relabelling vertices permutes
perfect matchings and edges compatibly, so $F$ is $S_4$ equivariant.  The
centered matching representation is the irreducible two-dimensional
representation $[22]$.  Since $[22]$ occurs with multiplicity one in the
six-edge permutation representation, the image projector is exactly
$P_{22}$.
\end{proof}

Let $r=(123)$ and let $Q_r$ be its permutation matrix on the three matchings.
Define on $W_{\mathsf M}$
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Omega_{\mathsf M}
 =\frac1{\sqrt3}
 P_{\mathsf M}(Q_{r^{-1}}-Q_r)P_{\mathsf M},
 \qquad
 C_{\mathsf M}=i\Omega_{\mathsf M}.}
 \tag{V41.3}\label{eq:v41-matching-C22}
\end{equation}

\begin{corollary}[Matching-coordinate formula for the V38 pseudoscalar]
\label{cor:v41-matching-pseudoscalar}
One has
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 F\Omega_{\mathsf M}F^*=\Omega_{\rm ps},
 \qquad
 FC_{\mathsf M}F^*=C_{22}.}
 \tag{V41.4}\label{eq:v41-C22-intertwining}
\end{equation}
Moreover
\[
 \Omega_{\mathsf M}^{\mathsf T}=-\Omega_{\mathsf M},
 \qquad
 \Omega_{\mathsf M}^2=-P_{\mathsf M},
 \qquad
 C_{\mathsf M}^2=P_{\mathsf M}.
\]
Thus the V38 sign-twist generator is already a deterministic function of the
three matching labels and their tetrahedral relabelling action.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Equivariance gives $U_rF=FQ_r$.  Insert
$P_{22}=FP_{\mathsf M}F^*$ from
\Cref{thm:v41-centered-matching-22} into the V38 formula
$\Omega_{\rm ps}=3^{-1/2}P_{22}(U_{r^{-1}}-U_r)P_{22}$.
The remaining identities follow because $Q_r$ is a $120^\circ$ rotation on
the centered matching plane.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Only the $[22]$ source incidence is needed}
Let two normalized same-history $[22]$ sources be
\[
 V_{\rm ax},V_{\rm ch}:W_{\mathsf M}\longrightarrow\mathcal H,
 \qquad
 V_{\rm ax}^*V_{\rm ax}=V_{\rm ch}^*V_{\rm ch}=I_{W_{\mathsf M}},
\]
and assume both intertwine the same represented matching action.  Put
\[
 T_{22}=V_{\rm ch}^*V_{\rm ax}.
\]

\begin{theorem}[One-scalar matching-plane placement certificate]
\label{thm:v41-22-incidence}
There is a scalar $z_2$ with $|z_2|\le1$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{T_{22}=z_2I_{W_{\mathsf M}}.}
 \tag{V41.5}\label{eq:v41-z2}
\end{equation}
Define
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \kappa_{22}
 :=\frac12\Tr(T_{22}^*T_{22})
 =|z_2|^2.}
 \tag{V41.6}\label{eq:v41-kappa22}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \kappa_{22}=1
 \iff
 \operatorname{Ran}V_{\rm ax}=\operatorname{Ran}V_{\rm ch}.}
 \tag{V41.7}\label{eq:v41-range22}
\end{equation}
If $\Pi_{\rm ax}^{22}$ and $\Pi_{\rm ch}^{22}$ are the corresponding range
projectors, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \|\Pi_{\rm ax}^{22}-\Pi_{\rm ch}^{22}\|_{\HS}^2
 =4(1-\kappa_{22}).}
 \tag{V41.8}\label{eq:v41-projector-distance22}
\end{equation}
On the exact branch the residual identification is one phase
$T_{22}=e^{i\phi}I$, and therefore
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 T_{22}C_{\mathsf M}T_{22}^*=C_{\mathsf M}.}
 \tag{V41.9}\label{eq:v41-C22-phase-invariant}
\end{equation}
The $[31]$ placement coefficient of V40 is absent from every statement.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Schur's lemma on the irreducible $[22]$ module gives
$T_{22}=z_2I$.  The inherited joint-source theorem makes the cross transport a
contraction.  Equality in the normalized overlap holds exactly when the two
isometric source ranges coincide.  The projector identity is the standard
rank-two formula
\[
 \|P-Q\|_{\HS}^2=4-2\Tr(PQ),
\]
with $\Tr(PQ)=\Tr(T_{22}^*T_{22})=2\kappa_{22}$.  The final identity is
immediate for a scalar unitary.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The five-dimensional V40 incidence gate is stronger than necessary]
\label{cor:v41-full-placement-unneeded}
To transport the V38--V39 pseudoscalar channel coefficient onto the locked
axis carrier, it is sufficient that \eqref{eq:v41-range22} hold.  Equality of
the $[31]$ source ranges is not required.  In particular, a channel core may
have an unrelated or absent $[31]$ sector while still supplying the complete
missing $SO(2)$ factor.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Both $C_{22}$ and $\Omega_{\rm ps}$ vanish on $[31]$ and are supported on the
$[22]$ block.  Every V38--V39 pseudoscalar coefficient, Hamiltonian derivation
and signed twirl therefore factors through that block.  The V37 $SO(3)$
curvature acts independently on $[31]$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Exact two-sided CPTP reversal already forces a Hamiltonian tangent}
The inherited channel-native theorem tests Hamiltonianity and reversal
separately.  On an exact two-sided tangent these conditions are not
independent.

\begin{theorem}[Lineality of the CPTP tangent cone at the identity]
\label{thm:v41-cptp-lineality}
Let
\[
 \Phi_\pm:[0,\varepsilon)\longrightarrow\operatorname{CPTP}(M_d)
\]
be differentiable at zero with
\[
 \Phi_\pm(0)=\operatorname{id},
 \qquad
 \Phi_\pm'(0)=\pm\mathcal L.
\]
Then there is a unique traceless Hermitian $H\in M_d$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \mathcal L=-i[H,\,\cdot\,].}
 \tag{V41.10}\label{eq:v41-cptp-lineality}
\end{equation}
Thus the lineality space of the finite-dimensional CPTP tangent cone at the
identity channel is exactly the space of Hamiltonian derivations.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $J_0=|I\rangle\!\rangle\langle\!\langle I|$ be the unnormalized Choi
matrix of the identity channel and let $K=J_{\mathcal L}=K^*$.  With $P$ the
rank-one projector onto $\mathbb C|I\rangle\!\rangle$ and $Q=I-P$, complete
positivity of both curves gives
\[
 J_0\pm tK+o(t)\succeq0.
\]
Compressing to $Q$ and dividing by $t$ yields
$\pm QKQ\succeq0$, hence
\[
 QKQ=0.
\]
Therefore $K$ has only the $P$ block and the two $P$--$Q$ cross blocks.
Since $P$ has rank one, there is a matrix $A$ such that, in vectorized Choi
notation,
\[
 K=|A\rangle\!\rangle\langle\!\langle I|
   +|I\rangle\!\rangle\langle\!\langle A|.
\]
(The map $A\mapsto K$ has exactly the required real block dimension; its
only kernel is the imaginary scalar line.)  The Choi--map correspondence then
gives
\[
 \mathcal L(X)=AX+XA^*.
\]
Trace preservation to first order gives
\[
 A+A^*=0.
\]
Thus $A=-iH$ for Hermitian $H$ and
$\mathcal L=-i[H,\cdot]$.  Adding a scalar to $H$ does not change the
commutator; imposing $\Tr H=0$ gives uniqueness.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Exact reversal makes the Hamiltonian residual redundant]
On the exact branch
$\Phi_-'(0)=-\Phi_+'(0)$, the separate Hamiltonian-distance terms in the
inherited channel-native defect vanish automatically by
\Cref{thm:v41-cptp-lineality}.  They remain useful and independent in noisy or
imperfectly reversed data.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The $S_4$ signed twirl collapses to a minimal six-step $S_3$ twirl}
The action of $S_4$ on the three perfect matchings has kernel the Klein four
group $V_4$, so
\[
 S_4/V_4\cong S_3.
\]
Because every element of $V_4$ is even, the sign character also descends to
this quotient.  Let
\[
 \rho_{\mathsf M}:S_3\to O(W_{\mathsf M})
\]
be the centered matching representation.

For a linear map $\mathcal L:M_2\to M_2$, define the quotient sign projector
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Pi_{\rm sgn}^{(6)}(\mathcal L)
 =\frac16\sum_{q\in S_3}
 \operatorname{sgn}(q)\,
 \operatorname{Ad}_{\rho_{\mathsf M}(q)}^{\rm sup}(\mathcal L).}
 \tag{V41.11}\label{eq:v41-six-sign-projector}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Six-step matching-core signed compiler]
\label{thm:v41-six-step-compiler}
Let $\Phi_\pm$ be a physical forward/reverse channel pair on the centered
matching core with
\[
 \Phi_\pm(0)=\operatorname{id},
 \qquad
 \Phi_\pm'(0)=\pm\mathcal L.
\]
For any ordering of the six quotient elements, put
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Psi_h^{(6)}
 =\prod_{q\in S_3}
 \operatorname{Ad}_{\rho_{\mathsf M}(q)}
 \circ
 \Phi_{\operatorname{sgn}(q)}(h/6)
 \circ
 \operatorname{Ad}_{\rho_{\mathsf M}(q)^{-1}}.}
 \tag{V41.12}\label{eq:v41-six-physical-twirl}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \left.\frac{d}{dh}\right|_{h=0}\Psi_h^{(6)}
 =\Pi_{\rm sgn}^{(6)}(\mathcal L).}
 \tag{V41.13}\label{eq:v41-six-derivative}
\end{equation}
If the reversal is exact, then
$\mathcal L=\mathscr D_H:=-i[H,\cdot]$ by
\Cref{thm:v41-cptp-lineality}, and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Pi_{\rm sgn}^{(6)}(\mathscr D_H)
 =a_{\rm ps}\,\mathscr D_{C_{\mathsf M}},
 \qquad
 a_{\rm ps}=\frac12\Tr(C_{\mathsf M}H).}
 \tag{V41.14}\label{eq:v41-six-Hamiltonian}
\end{equation}
Equivalently, directly at superoperator level,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 a_{\rm ps}
 =\frac18
 \langle\mathscr D_{C_{\mathsf M}},\mathcal L\rangle_{\rm sup}.}
 \tag{V41.15}\label{eq:v41-aps-eight}
\end{equation}
Thus $a_{\rm ps}\ne0$ compiles the complete missing $SO(2)$ tangent with only
six channel factors rather than the twenty-four factors of V39.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The derivative of a finite product through the identity is the sum of the six
first derivatives, which gives \eqref{eq:v41-six-derivative}.  On the
Hamiltonian branch, conjugation transports Hamiltonians, so the projector on
superoperators is the Hamiltonian derivation of the sign Reynolds projector
of $H$.  On $W_{\mathsf M}$ one has
\[
 \operatorname{End}(W_{\mathsf M})
 \cong[4]\oplus[1111]\oplus[22],
\]
and the sign line is spanned by $C_{\mathsf M}$.  Orthogonal projection gives
$a_{\rm ps}=\Tr(C_{\mathsf M}H)/\Tr(C_{\mathsf M}^2)$; the denominator is two.
For $d=2$, the inherited inner-derivation norm identity gives
\[
 \|\mathscr D_{C_{\mathsf M}}\|_{\rm sup,HS}^2
 =2d\|C_{\mathsf M}\|_{\HS}^2=8,
\]
which proves \eqref{eq:v41-aps-eight}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Six quotient actions are minimal for an exact orbit projector]
\label{thm:v41-six-minimal}
Consider first-order compilers obtained from relabelled copies of one physical
forward/reverse tangent on $W_{\mathsf M}$, allowing arbitrary nonnegative
pulse durations and merging repeated quotient actions.  If such a compiler is
to implement the exact sign Reynolds projector
\eqref{eq:v41-six-sign-projector} for every input tangent, then every one of
the six elements of $S_3$ must occur.  Hence the six distinct quotient actions
in \eqref{eq:v41-six-physical-twirl} are minimal within this orbit-compiler
class.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The conjugation representation on
$\operatorname{End}(W_{\mathsf M})$ decomposes as
\[
 [4]\oplus[1111]\oplus[22],
\]
so it contains every irreducible representation of $S_3$.  The induced
representation of the group algebra
$\mathbb C[S_3]\cong\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C\oplus M_2(\mathbb C)$ is
therefore faithful.  Consequently the six conjugation operators
$\operatorname{Ad}_{\rho_{\mathsf M}(q)}$ are linearly independent.  The sign
central idempotent has the unique group-basis expansion
\[
 \frac16\sum_{q\in S_3}\operatorname{sgn}(q)q,
\]
whose six coefficients are all nonzero.  Any exact first-order orbit compiler
must therefore use all six quotient actions after repeated actions are merged.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The minimal remaining physical entrance is two dimensional}
Combining the preceding results gives the revised gate
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{array}{c}
 \text{actual two-sided CPTP channel on a }[22]\text{ core}\\
 +\text{ same-history }[22]\text{ incidence}\\
 \Downarrow\\[-1mm]
 \kappa_{22}=1\\
 \Downarrow\\[-1mm]
 a_{\rm ps}=\frac18
 \langle\mathscr D_{C_{\mathsf M}},\mathcal L_+\rangle_{\rm sup}\ne0\\
 \Downarrow\\[-1mm]
 \text{minimal six-step signed twirl}\\
 \Downarrow\\[-1mm]
 SO(2)\\
 \Downarrow\\[-1mm]
 SO(3)\times SO(2)\text{ with the V37 curvature sector.}
 \end{array}}
 \tag{V41.16}\label{eq:v41-revised-gate}
\end{equation}
If the physical channel is already represented directly on the centered
matching coordinate of the literal Store half-edge record, then
$\kappa_{22}=1$ automatically and even the placement scalar disappears.

The supplied inherited material does not presently establish such a channel
occurrence.  It supplies the centered matching record and its $[22]$ source,
and separately supplies the channel-native theorem for an arbitrary chosen
logical core, but it does not identify the channel core with the centered
matching plane.  Therefore the current acquisition boundary is only a
\emph{two-dimensional matching-core channel occurrence}, not a full
five-axis channel occurrence.
